We are in the last days, and have been since the first fruit of Christ, and the harvest of 5,000 made by the disciples on Pentecost. We shall bring in the sheaves for the Lord. To Him the increase. Until the fullness of the harvest comes in.

Amen

teachings.title: Bloom where the Lord has planted you
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah, who longed to flee to the wilderness but was sent to preach at the temple gates, Christians are not to retreat to compounds but to be a light where people are, enduring tribulation with hope because Christ has overcome the world.
teachings.text:
*Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.*

**Jeremiah 9** continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea.

And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart.

But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them.

This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness.

We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods.

And so we are in the world, not of it.

Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ*.

Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To *glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

**James 1:12**
*Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.*

**Romans 8:18**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

**James 1:2-4**
*My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.*

We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us.

**John 16:33**
*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.*

teachings.title: Separation from heathen practices
teachings.summary: God forbade pagan customs such as enchantment, pagan haircuts, cuttings and tattoos for the dead, and believers should not imitate the heathen.
teachings.text:
Next in **Leviticus 19:26,** God begins to address separation from the heathen practices of the idolaters that are being driven from Canaan, and the Egyptians God freed them from.

Again, a prohibition against consuming blood, specifically tied in with enchantment, witchcraft, astrology (observing times), rounding the corners of their heads and beards, a custom of many pagans of the time and a popular look for religious Egyptians, (think whitewalls and goatees). No cuttings of the flesh for the dead, ritual scaring or tattoos. This is a difficult commandment for many today, who do weird haircuts, cutting eyebrows, beards, etc, along with tribal tats and remembering the dead with ink, "RIP Pop!" and the like. Making it fashionable to larp as ancient pagans.

The prohibition against whoring out your daughters is obvious, but also in the sense of the temple prostitute that many cults utilized. God refers to both actual prostitution and chasing after false gods as whoredoms, and normalizing this brings a land to become full of wickedness.

teachings.title: Kings and priests should not drink wine
teachings.summary: Believers are a royal priesthood and princes, so like the priests and kings they should abstain from alcohol and be sober.
teachings.text:
Note that Moses instructs the priests should remain sober. And that if they drink alcohol and enter into the Tabernacle, they will die.

*Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations*...

This instruction coming on the heels of the devastating loss of two sons, may have been directed at Aaron in his grief, but it's a standing command from the Lord for those who are called His priests. We who are saved are of the royal priesthood. We are a Tabernacle of the Spirit of God.

Just as **Proverbs 31** states;

*It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes strong drink: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.*

We who are saved are joint heirs to the kingdom. We are princes.

As priests and princes, we should abstain from intoxicants. We are called to be sober. To refrain from the appearance of evil. To be holy because He is holy.

It is incredibly difficult to read these scriptures and come to the conclusion that it's ok to drink booze.

And it is gravely heretical to claim, as the Romans do, that the priests they appoint should drink alcohol as part of their false sacrifice at the altar they claim is holy. Blasphemously calling it the blood of Christ.

teachings.title: Make Straight Paths for Your Feet
teachings.summary: Believers must be separate from the world, accept chastening, and avoid bitterness so their good report draws others to God's grace.
teachings.text:
So understanding this, that we need separation from this world, not to despise our promised blessings for a bowl of pottage, that we not satisfy the flesh in our short time here rather than see our hope for eternity. But, as Moses, *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.*

Don't be down or angry with God for His chastening, which as it happens may seem grievous, but understand it builds righteousness so that we may better serve the living God, and bring forth fruit as an example to others.

*Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.*

As scripture says:

*I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths. I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.*

And again,

*In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil.*

Following God's word, the hope that we believe on, we are given wisdom, our paths made straight. Not only for us but for those without, who are lame, who are perishing. That they may see God's glory reflecting from us like Moses come down from the mountain.

Be peaceable with all men, showing holiness, the separation we are called for, that our faith obtains a good report, as it did the elders before us.

*Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;*

Don't allow your burdens and sin, or bitterness at correction or anything to give a bad report of the faith, that others may not be defiled and not accept the grace of God.

We are a holy priesthood. We are heirs to a kingdom. We have hope everlasting. Act like it that others may attain the same. It is the least we can do considering what Christ did for us.

For when it is too late for those we turned away by our bitterness and strife, our bad report and our sin, our despising our inheritance, our lack of faith, they are rejected. And there will be no place for repentance.

teachings.title: The World Hates an Evil Report of Sin
teachings.summary: As Joseph's brothers hated him for his evil report, the world hates faithful Christians because preaching against sin exposes their deeds.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 37** begins the tale of Joseph and Judah, the other brothers and how the sons of Jacob came to be in Egypt. The generations of Israel, told by God through Moses. In this narrative, there lays prophecy of Christ Jesus, both as a figure in Joseph and in the blessing upon Judah, which we will see later near the end.

But keeping in mind the picture of Jesus in Joseph and the traits of man in the brothers, especially Judah/Jews of Christ's time, there's a lot to digest.

First, we are given the timing and situation; Joseph, the first son born unto Rachel, Jacob's first love, and so the father's favorite. Joseph, out with his half brothers tending the flocks returns to his father, bringing an "evil report." Bringing word to the father that the children are in sin.

And the brothers hate him for it.

Much the same way today the world hates a faithful Christian for the reminder of their sin we bring. The light shined on their inequity. As Jesus says in **John 3:20**:

*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.*

Christians standing fast against sin bring an evil report of the wicked hearts of men. The world resents it.

**John 15:18** I*f the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.*

Joseph's brothers hated him for the same reason. Sinners hate preaching against sin. Standards and morality. God's word, which convicts them. Christians who bring an evil report to their deeds.

And like Joseph's brothers, the world plots and schemes ways to shut us up. To sully Christ's name by our own failings. To discredit God's word. To subvert His people. To call good evil and evil good.

[Isaiah 5:20](https://t.me/ApeMtn37/3516)
*Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!*

teachings.title: Righteous Lot, the backslidden believer
teachings.summary: Lot pictures the saved man taken in by the world, vexed but mired in sin, whose worldly-raised daughters fell into abomination.
teachings.text:
This is the lesson of Sodom. This is the truth about sodomites.

And righteous Lot, saved by faith while in the camp of Abram, who pitched his tent towards Sodom and Gomorrah, on the plains of the Jordan, representing the saved man who is taken in by the world rather than living a life of separation. Worldly. Carnal. Vexed in the spirit by the filthy conversation around him, but mired in it. So much so his daughters are betrothed to men of the city. So much so, he took wine with him when he was practically dragged out by the angels. His wife, unable to leave sin behind looks back despite the warning, at her old life, and is consumed into a pillar of salt.

Compelled to go into the mountains for safety by the angels, a picture of Christ and the protection of Zion, Lot begs to go to another city, Zoar. Afraid of the mountains and what evil may befall him, even as he had just been saved by angels of the Lord. The backslidden believer, unable to build on the faith that's saved him to escape sin. The struggle many have today.

As everyone and everything around us falls into wickedness. Sodomites glorified and rapists and murderers hailed. Every depravity known to man, even the spoiling of children. And yet we cling to the worldly and the profane, despite knowing better. Despite having the Spirit within us. Despite our being vexed constantly by the filthy conversation of the reprobates and unregenerate man around us.

We are told Lot did take his daughters to the mountains, and sought refuge in a cave. Perhaps his conscience spurred by the Spirit made him wary of again entering a worldly city.

His possessions including strong wine, he in despair having lost everything drinks to a stupor. His daughters, raised in Sodom, raised worldly, desensitized to the wickedness that surrounded them, plan an abomination.

Having lost their mother and home and betrothed husbands, and seeing the wrath poured out on the plains and the cities of the plains, they think it is the end of them. And they decide to lay with their own father and become pregnant. This is the influence of the carnal world that they grew up in. Rather than being raised in faith and taught righteousness. And so this evil seems reasonable to them. And they birth the nations of the Moabites and Ammon.

Remember, the law given the Israelites would prohibit Moabites from the assembly of God, **as a punishment for their maltreatment of the children of Israel and for engaging Balaam to curse the children of Israel**, while they journeyed in the wilderness. Just as the Lord says in Genesis 18 that faithful Abraham and his descendants will keep the faith of God, backslidden Lot's won't.

There's so many lessons to take from this for saved believers living in this wicked world.

teachings.title: Abram rescues Lot and refuses Sodom's spoils
teachings.summary: Abram stayed out of the kings' war, rescued his brother and refused the wicked king's treasure, a pattern for believers defending the righteous without entanglement.
teachings.text:
Abram, seeing his brother in Christ, his nephew Lot, who we saw pitch his tent towards Sodom and get punished being spoiled and taken into captivity by the other kings' armies, seeks Lot's rescue. He is not part of the war of the kings, itself. But he is the finisher of it with God's hand defeating his does and freeing Lot and his people and possessions.

Abram refuses spoils from the King of Sodom, not wanting anything from that wicked man. He did what he did because it was right.

This should be a picture of what action of saved believers looks like, staying out of the war, not getting entangled in commitments with the wicked, not seeking treasure, but defending brethren from violence and having faith in God to destroy our enemies when we do defend the righteous.

Abram rejects the treasure, but ensures a tenth of the spoils were given to Melchizedek as an offering to God. Because all things are God's.

teachings.title: Walk as children of light
teachings.summary: Heirs of God should not walk as the children of disobedience but be filled with the Spirit through psalms, hymns and thanksgiving, rather than filling their minds with worldly entertainment.
teachings.text:
Are you a child of God or a child of disobedience? As heirs, by Christ, we are of God the Father. And so we should walk as such. Carrying ourselves as befitting our station, in meekness because only grace has brought us in, and blameless in mercy and righteousness, a light that shines so that others may become fellow brothers, who are as what we were.

The children of disobedience are fornicators, unclean, covetous, filthy and foolish talkers, jesters joking rather than giving thanks, whoremongers, idolaters. They have no share of the inheritance and God's wrath is upon them, so why walk with them? Why act as they act? Why sin as they sin? Why partake in the things unbefitting heirs?

So we should walk in the light, where the sins of the dark are made manifest. Christ is that light. Making the most of our short time here, in these evil days. Not being as fools, but wise with the wisdom God has given us in his mercy. Not drunk, but in the Spirit.

Paul in a few short paragraphs gives God's will for us that He's adopted. It isn't asking much, considering the gift we've been given. But the flesh is weak and wars against our spirit. Still we should strive for this bare minimum.

And how are we filled with the Spirit? It's not gnosticism. It's not a secret. The Bible gives us answers.

*Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.*

Not drowning out your thoughts with music that dishonors God. Listening to others talk, often blasphemy, all day as you work, pushing out the spiritual and filling your head with foolishness and earthly cares. Consuming the latest Jewish fables to talk about with coworkers. Sporting contests brought to you by drunkenness, gambling and vice.

We all waste time, not redeeming the day, rather than being in prayer, song and praise. But the more we walk as we should, the more we are in the Spirit and absent distractions of this world, the easier it is to be in the light, and the more useful we are to God. And the more useful we are to God, the more he blesses us with the Spirit  That's really what it's all about.

teachings.title: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers
teachings.summary: Being unequally yoked reaches beyond marriage to every alliance with unbelievers and Christ-haters, and believers must come out and be separate rather than seek salvation from worldly allies.
teachings.text:
Paul transitions to instruction that is very relevant in our circles, being unequally yoked with unbelievers.

Many apply this to marriage and being with an unbelieving spouse, but it's far more broad than that. In a similar way 1 Corinthians chastised them for taking other believers to secular judges to settle disputes, this is an admonition and call for separation. He asks "*what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?*" So many Christians, in desperation and fear, join forces and ally themselves with unbelievers, and not only unsaved supposed agnostics and cultural Christians but actual people who despise Jesus or tolerate those who do.

*And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.*

Come out then, from them. God is your father. He will lead your people. We don't need anything from the worldly, the mockers, the scoffers.

How can one set of unbelieving, Christ-hating, worldly materialists help save us from another group of Christ-hating worldly materialists? They can't. All they can do is lead us to a place that brings offense and blame to our ministry, and make our gift of Grace in vain.

teachings.title: Churches soft on fornication
teachings.summary: Fornication, including cohabiting couples who call it love, is sin and self-harm that churches wink at, though the apostles in Acts made a point of warning against it.
teachings.text:
Many so-called Christians today have rationalized away fornication as not a big deal. Not only do they give exception for monogamous relationships outside of marriage, cohabitation etc, where they claim that since they are" in love" it's just as good as marriage, but even to the point where they forgive the whore-mongering and harlotry of their members. Allowing that leaven to leaven the whole lump as it were.

By being soft on fornication, they not only are being contrary to God's law but they're opening their own members up to self-abuse in this regard. God tells us that it's not only a sin but harmful to us and yet, most churches won't even preach against it except to teenagers perhaps.

It was such an important Doctrine, that in Acts of the Apostles where they are debating the things they can tell other churches that they should be wary of regarding the Jews and circumcision, and idolatry and the like, they make it a point to speak out against fornication. The teaching on it is quite clear.

Incels take the W.

teachings.title: Saul was consenting unto his death
teachings.summary: By holding the coats Saul consented to Stephen's death, and even passive consent to sin is sin, so believers must boldly stand against evil.
teachings.text:
*Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, And cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul.*

*And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was* **consenting unto his death***.*

*And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.*

*As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison*.

The Bible says that even by his presence and holding the coats of those stoning Stephen to death that Saul/Paul was "consenting unto his death."

**1 Timothy 5:22** *Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins*

Giving even passive consent to sin is a sin. We are to loudly and boldly proclaim the word of God and stand against evil.

teachings.title: Wine in the Bible and the Lord's supper
teachings.summary: Wine in scripture usually means juice, drunkenness is sin, and it was not fermented wine at the Last Supper, so using alcohol as Christ's blood is blasphemous.
teachings.text:
I won't get too far into the "wine means juice" debate. Most places in the Bible it does, and wine simply means freshly squeezed or preserved fruit juice. Some places it means fermented. This first miracle of the wedding of Cana is hard for many to not see it being fermented, but then would Jesus get people drunken, when the Bible *is* clear that's a sin to even look upon it?

**Proverbs 23**
*31 Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.*

*32 At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.*

*33 Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.*

(Grape juice is clear until fermented, turning it red)

In before Redditards say "They didn't know how to preserve juice until Louis Pasteur!!" That's an ignorant lie. They did, with multiple methods, including sulphur, boiling, wax capped bottles, etc.

But it's a distraction. I can say with confidence that at the Last Supper it wasn't booze, and the practice of using fermented wine to claim it's Jesus' blood is doubly blasphemous.

But let's not get bogged down in the weeds.

teachings.title: No want to them that fear Him
teachings.summary: God provides for those who fear Him and live righteously, chastens those who do not, and expects believers to love the brethren by not forsaking the assembling of the local church.
teachings.text:
*O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.*

Believers, sanctified in the Spirit by faith in the risen Christ, are given the promise that the Lord will redeem us, His servants.

But His provision for us extends beyond the fact of eternal salvation, and gives us hope and comfort here, in this life. Our daily bread, shelter, clothing, we shall not want for any good thing.

But more, He's given us His word, and His standards for separation that we may fear the Lord and be blessed by having a longer life and see good within the years we are allotted.

His burden is light. Don't speak evil of others, don't lie. Don't seek to harm others, but do good and seek peace.

**Romans 12:18**
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

Vengeance is Mine, sayeth the Lord. He will repay. We not only believe He is, and a rewarder of those that diligently seek Him, but that He is our shield and strength against our enemies. We do not need to fight a battle, but trust in Him to fight for us. We simply need to walk in the Spirit, love our enemies, hate His, and seek others' profit. Doing good.

If we want our Father's blessing, live righteously. He hears the righteous and answers their cry.

We are known by our love for the brethren. By our edifying one another.

**Hebrews 10:22–25**
*Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

You don't want the face of God against you in your time of need.

**Hebrews 10:26–29**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?*

God will chasten His children. He will shorten your life and withhold blessings, and even bring you home for not doing His work at His pleasure.

**Hebrews 10:31**
*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

Note that we are expected to love and care for our fellow saints. And where do we do this? On the called out assembly of believers. Our local church. Forsaking this opportunity is spiteful to the Spirit of grace which has bought you. Go to church!

teachings.title: I am my beloved's
teachings.summary: The bride's choice to rise early and go forth with her beloved pictures the mature believer deliberately making Christ the centre of each day and working with Him to bear fruit in new believers.
teachings.text:
Song of Solomon 7 opens with the King, having called his beloved Shulamite woman to return to him that he may look upon her at the end of chapter 6, now detailing what he sees of his beloved. He describes her beauty and the perfect symmetry of her body.

*How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!*

Everything he sees of her is good. Just as we are seen as perfect and without spot when God looks upon us, clothed in the righteousness of Christ.

**2 Corinthians 11:2**
*For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.*

**Colossians 1:22**
*In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

The woman responds to her husband, her brother, her spouse with unwavering confidence;

*I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.*

We are Christ's, and His desire is for us.

Beginning there in verse 10, she responds to her beloved, knowing she is his, and inviting him to go forth with her, to live with her. To get up early to the vineyards, to see the vine flourish and come to fruition, where she will give him her love.

The spiritual application here; She has gone from her initial humble acceptance of his love, to the joy of the wedding feast, to her period of complacency, persecution, profession of faith and renewal, to now making the decision to plan her day and life around him, is a beautiful picture of the Christian life.

A believer makes the conscious decision to make Jesus their companion. To go forth with Him and to reside with Him. To wake early in the morning, starting the day with Christ, and His word. In prayer.

This intentionality is contrasted with the bride laying in bed, hesitant to wake, making excuses to avoid letting in her beloved. As mature Christians, in it for the long haul, we seek Him first.

We work with Him to tend the vine, which is His church, bringing forth fruit which are new believers. Planting the seed of His word. Watering and nurturing. Tending to them, the babes in Christ, and helping them grow to maturity. Through it all, giving Him all our love.

We lay up our fruit, those people we have given the gospel to, the needy to whom we give comfort. The broken hearted we have consoled. This treasure we have laid up for Heaven, but to Him is the increase. We give Him our all because He is our beloved.

teachings.title: The bride who would not open
teachings.summary: The bride who delayed to open to her beloved pictures saved believers who grow complacent and make excuses when God calls them to His work, and so lose His fellowship and suffer His chastening.
teachings.text:
Chapter 5 opens with the aftermath of the close of the previous chapter, which ended with the woman calling upon her bridegroom, her lord.

The spiritual moment of acceptance and humility, asking Him for salvation. Opening yourself to be intimately known of God.

Verse 1 gives the bridegroom's POV. Having entered the garden, come unto his dearest sister, his spouse, gathered the spices and ointments of myrrh, eaten the sweet of the honeycomb, drunk the wine and milk, and calling those at the wedding feast, and his bride, to eat and drink, abundantly.

**Revelation 22:17**
*And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.*

This picture of salvation, the immediate joy and celebration, the call to get your fill of an abundance of the sweet and precious food and anointing oils, wine and milk, to drink abundantly, is God's call to us to now walk in His Spirit. To take full advantage of the relationship His children have with the Father in Christ, the true King. The Shepherd. The Bridegroom. Not a thief, but our Savior.

**John 10:10**
*The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.*

We are called to walk in the Spirit and receive the fruit thereof;

**Galatians 5:22–25**
*But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law. And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.*

This initial feeling of having come to a feast and being overwhelmed with the love of God towards us, His blessings and rest, is marvelous. But we may tire and sleep in that contentment.

The bride sleeps, but her heart wakes. She hears a knock. A voice. It is her beloved, calling to her to let him in. He asks her to open to him, *my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled*. He has come, his hair wet with the dew of the night to see her.

He is Christ come to give His bride a blessing, but she doesn't leap to open the door.

She makes excuses; *I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?* Rather than hear His voice and do His will, that we may be blessed, a believer may see their contentment and undefiled spirit as a bed to rest upon. When God asks so little of us whom He has saved, to open when He knocks, will we respond?

**Revelation 3:20**
*Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.*

In the Christian life, God gives us works to do. Poor to be fed. A gospel to be preached. Divine appointments to be kept. His burden is light. He wants so little from us, yet in our own selfish interests, we make excuses. Taking for granted all He has given us.

And, even as the beloved reaches his hand in through the door, making that extra effort to stir his bride, God will try and overcome our hesitation, moving in our lives.

His effort stirs her. She rises but too late. She feels the sweet smelling myrrh, the holiness of Christ, upon the lock. But, He has withdrawn.

When we don't respond to God's callings, and hesitate to do His will, He will give us a taste of life without Him. He will lift His hedge of protection. He will let us suffer consequences He has spared us from. He will chasten every son.

The bride's soul fails, knowing she did wrong and desperately she seeks her beloved, in the very manner she once sought him. Wandering in the dark streets, calling for him. Trying to find her own way.

This time, the watchmen find her and persecute her. The smote her and wound her and remove her veil of purity. She suffers for her love's sake.

The watchmen who could not tell her the way to her love in chapter 3, now treat her wickedly.

teachings.title: Wisdom maketh his face to shine
teachings.summary: Walking with God and being anointed by the Spirit changes a believer's countenance and gives boldness to preach the truth, so that others see they have been with Jesus.
teachings.text:
The Preacher continues his sermon. Having said he has searched for wisdom by observation of all things under the Sun, and having found all have sinned and fallen short. That the wise and the fool, the rich and the poor, all are appointed to die, and after this, judged and found wanting, that then the only way is God's. That fear of Him and seeking His favor is the only alternative to the vanity and vexation of spirit that man travails in.

Solomon begins **Ecclesiastes 8** praising the effect that seeking God's wisdom has on us. That it makes the face to shine, and to speak boldly His truth. That it changes the countenance of a person to walk with God.

**Exodus 34:29-30**
*And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.*

Moses had to cover his face from the people, it disturbed them so much to see the radiance coming from his time with God.

**Psalm 104:15**
*And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart*.

The Spirit is described as oil, which anoints us as we walk in Him. The bread, His word. Our heart, merry from the juice of the vine, which is Christ. He does make our faces shine. His light magnified through us, that men see us and know, we have been with Jesus. And the boldness of our wisdom comes from the confidence we have in Him and His word.

The Spirit filled the disciples of Christ, gathered in the upper room on Pentecost, and having His anointing, they went out among the multitudes gathered for the feast in Jerusalem, and preached with boldness.

Acts 2:1-4
*And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance*.

The men, hearing the miracle of preaching Christ from scripture, in their own tongues, languages from around the known world, they wondered; *Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans?* But the disciples had been changed by their time with God. The boldness to preach Christ from scripture, and 3,000 souls came to repentance.

Just as when Peter and John were brought before the religious leaders of the Jews for preaching Christ, these lowly fishermen gave witness that they had been with Christ by their boldness.

**Acts 4:13**
*Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.*

Their light so shined, that others saw and praised God. The anointing of the Spirit, the truth of God's word, the wisdom they trusted, gave them boldness to preach the truth. They were changed.

The understanding that man's countenance gives away their time with God to others, has a counterpoint in scripture. That the reprobate, those that hold the truth in unrighteousness, have a similar change;

**Isaiah 3:9**
*The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.*

We should seek to walk with God, to be anointed with the Spirit, that men look upon us and take note that we have been with Jesus. To speak boldly the wisdom of the gospel. To make known the truth of His way.

teachings.title: Give me neither poverty nor riches
teachings.summary: Agur's prayer for neither poverty nor riches shows we should be content with what God gives, since riches make men forget God and want makes them steal, as Paul learned contentment.
teachings.text:
Continuing **Proverbs 30** and the sayings attributed to Agur the son of Jakeh.

Vs 7-9 is a form of prayer to the Lord to grant Agur favor in this lifetime; That God removes from him vanity and lies and to give neither poverty or riches, yet have sufficient food to eat.

*Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.*

This should be the attitude we strive for. To take away the worthless and useless things in our life that take us away from fully serving God. That we deal honestly, not only with others but ourselves and therefore with God. Hiding nothing. Rationalizing or excusing nothing. Not heeding delusion that covers sin.

Being satisfied with what God has blessed you with. Being content to have sufficient food to eat. Living simply unto the Lord. As many Proverbs before this have shown, the rich place their trust in their possessions. Themselves. They deny God and say "Who is the Lord?"

Make no mistake, that even the temporary and sudden wealth an average or lower middle-class person may receive, a windfall or an unexpected inheritance or bonus, is often sufficient to knock them off the pathway of God. To make them forget the blessings and the Blesser. How much worse to have the wealth always about you, where you want for nothing and grow complacent towards God?

And be thankful that you're not poor, and left to steal to eat. To curse God for your station and take His name in vain.

Sometimes, in our Christian walk, we are tempted. Covetousness turns to greed. How often do we pray, not with thanksgiving for what we have, but desiring "just a little more, God, please?" That He would increase our wealth so we can afford some luxury or extravagance that we've convinced ourselves that we deserve. "Everyone else has one!" Coveting. "If we only had a little more!" Greed.

**Philippians 4:12**
*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.*

Paul writes the end goal that Agur sought. To know how to be both rich and poor, everywhere in all things, to know *whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.*

Why? *I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.*

The vanity of riches and the lies that rationalize sin away, are traps we should call upon the Lord to save us from. Contentment and gratitude go a long way to remove these things far from us.

teachings.title: Asking for more with a full pantry
teachings.summary: With more plenty than we can store we still ask God for more, so we should practise gratitude and contentment as in Agur's prayer.
teachings.text:
An example of this in my life, a small thing that maybe others can relate to; After grocery shopping, putting away the perishables in the fridge, and there being no room for the plenty, and cursing how nothing more fits, and finding old leftovers and nearly empty bottles of sauces, angrily throwing them away to make room for more...Or the pantry too full. Cans or boxes falling out because the shelf is packed, and cursing to yourself, "Dang it!"

Imagine having so much plenty that this is a problem, and then asking God separately, "Lord, could you please increase my salary?"

Or worse, many keep subscriptions to worldly streaming services, eat out multiple times a week, blow their money on a video game or some fancy brand clothing, or on bad and sinful habits like drinking, smoking or gambling...AND then asking God to give you more!

We all do it to some degree, and you don't have to be on the extreme ends of rich or poor to have vanity and lies in our life. To forget the Lord, and deny Him. To justify sin and use His name in vain.

Gratitude for the grace of God should be sufficient for us. Agur's prayer should be our own. Like Paul we need to work on being content, and doing the work of the Lord, allowing Him to bless us and provide what we need, keeping the vanity and lies away from us, leading us not into temptation. Delivering us from evil, even the evil of our own heart.

teachings.title: Take away the dross from the silver
teachings.summary: Walking in the Spirit and seeking God's wisdom refines believers like silver, giving the heirs the character to rule and judge righteously as vessels of honour.
teachings.text:
Continuing in the chapter; if the deeper things of God are the glory of kings to search out, then the heart of the king is as high as Heaven and as deep as the earth; unsearchable to the common man.

The Spirit that brings those who seek it, understanding, being absent in the natural man (who receiveth not the spiritual things of God) cannot fathom the heart of the king.

This process, walking in the Spirit, seeking wisdom and the richness of God's judgment, produces a refinement; the fire of God removes the dross, the impurities in a man, and we come forth a finer vessel, pure silver, fit for holy use.

While we have the legal inheritance to rule, as sons and co-heirs with Christ, we gain the character needed to rule, to judge righteous judgment, by this refinement. Our God is a consuming fire and all that burns away is dross.

We are meant to be fitted as vessels of honor, and so the instructions for Godly living, His wisdom given by inspiration to Solomon, here written by order of Hezekiah, is designed to act as a refining fire. To see things the way God sees things. To walk His path, to be in the way of righteousness, following after Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: Ease made them forget grace
teachings.summary: Centuries of protection left the Jews complacent and unready for Christ, so we should be content and steadfast in faith in good times and bad, not taking God for granted.
teachings.text:
Interesting to consider that having hundreds of years of divine protection after being thoroughly devastated by the Babylonians, was both a blessing and a curse for the Jews.

Obviously they remained under the protectorate God, even as Rome eventually conquered the region. Jerusalem stood. The people were generally unaffected by all of the turmoil in the time in between. Persia, Greece, the Ptolemaic empires, Rome... Jerusalem and the temple stood. The line of David was protected.

But the lack of affliction also caused most Jews to forget about grace and supplication, to not be ready for repentance when Christ came. Unable to believe on Him Who was sent. Jesus came into His own and How own received Him not.

And of course, they lost the hedge of protection and as Jesus foretold, Jerusalem was sacked and burned and the Temple destroyed in 70AD.

It is easy to forget the power of God upon us when things are going well, just as it can be easy to gripe and complain at petty inconvenience when we have it so good. Having sure and steady faith in the promises of God, good times or bad, when we are abased and when we abound, is a key skill to develop in the Christian life. Being content. Knowing His grace is sufficient. Not allowing complacency to lead to taking God for granted.

teachings.title: Josiah a model of the Christian life
teachings.summary: Josiah's seeking God, purging idols, repairing the temple, being convicted by the found law and covenanting to serve God pictures the path a believer can choose to follow.
teachings.text:
**2 Chronicles 34** tells the reign of Josiah, son of the repentant Manasseh, who was only 8 years old when he took the throne from his father. We can infer that he was born later in Manasseh's life, and the influence of his father's conversion had an impact on him. At 16, by faith he began to diligently seek after the things of God. And we know *without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

With a heart towards God, having purged the land of the idols and high places, Josiah began the repair of the temple. Just as a Christian seeking the Lord would cast out those things in their old life, and then begin building up the temple, repairing their hearts. Seeking after the things of God.

And He rewards the king with the rediscovered copy of the Law. Just as the Spirit brings all knowledge and truth, and we study the Bible. And as Josiah is read the word, he rends his clothes knowing how far from God's will the people had fallen away. Just as we are convicted of sin the more we study His word.

And so the king seeks after a prophet, to learn the will of the Lord, to know what to do. As the Christian may assemble under a pastor to be preached to.

Josiah makes a covenant to serve God all his days, and God brings him peace and spares the king the wrath that is due the nation.

It isn't a perfect parable to the Christian life, and we all must make the decisions along the path to do as Josiah, but it is a fine model for that life. One we can choose to follow.

teachings.title: The spirit of Josiah, not Hezekiah
teachings.summary: Unlike Hezekiah, content that judgment would not come in his day (the attitude behind the pre-tribulation rapture's appeal), believers should, like Josiah, lament sin and preach against it even facing tribulation.
teachings.text:
*Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal. And the Lord said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.*

The revival and zeal for the Lord shown by King Josiah led God to grant his reign a measure of peace and delayed their judgement against them. But it did not prevent God's wrath from being poured out eventually.

And Josiah knew by the prophecy given to him that the judgment was inevitable. But he still did that which was right and was tearful and full of regret for the evil done in the land by his fathers and the people.

Contrast that with when Hezekiah said unto Isaiah, who had given the same warning; *Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. And he said, Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?*

Hezekiah, a good king as well who did fear the Lord, accepted the judgment and was glad it wasn't in his day, but did not utterly purge the land as Josiah did. He was relieved that the wrath was held back, and that his children would suffer the consequences rather than him.

This mentality is common among what is called the "baby boomer" generation, many of whom recognizing that the consequences for their sin would lead to judgment, took comfort in the fact that they wouldn't be here to see it. And it is no wonder that the false doctrine of a pre-tribulation rapture was so appealing to them.

They rested in the delusion that while the nation may be going to Hell in a hand basket, and that judgment was coming, that they didn't need to worry. They would be spared any trouble when it "got really bad." They didn't make any effort to turn back to the Lord with zeal and lead a revival in hopes of turning back God's wrath or buying more time. They said *Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?*

Then you see another generation come, who like Josiah, look to the word of God and understand that the sodomites and the idols and the failure to walk in the statutes of the Lord is the cause of the judgment, and as righteous as God's indignation against us is, we still have a duty to follow His commandments, even if it means facing great tribulation. To lament the wickedness done and to preach and act against it. And to proclaim the word of God and His righteousness to the world. In season or out of season.

It is a different attitude, and one that the old guard of Christians often resent and look down upon, because it convicts them for their inaction, or leads them to special pleading, saying "I tried ...it's not my fault."

I would rather have the spirit of Josiah rending his clothes and seeking after the Lord than of Hezekiah's acquiescence and pride in his earthly wealth.

teachings.title: Don't let your zeal fade like Jehu's
teachings.summary: Jehu's zeal burned bright but faded, so believers should keep their zeal for the Lord burning steadily all their lives.
teachings.text:
Then he meets with Jehonadab the Kenite, son of Rechab. The Rechabites, mentioned in Jeremiah, are non-Israelites who lived among them as nomads, never owning land, planting vineyards or drinking wine. Fierce followers of the Lord.

Jehu, seeking his approval and support meets with Jehonadab and shaking hands in peace, invites him into his chariot, saying; *Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord.*

They then set out and slew all the men loyal to Ahab, and those of his seed, according to the saying of the Lord, which he spake to Elijah.

We, as Christians, like to think of ourselves as Jehu in this moment, and with other believers, show our zeal. I know I have been fired up for the Lord and eager to do His bidding and to show that zeal to others. It is a line of scripture that always has my heart stirring and gets me pumped up.

I think we can learn a lesson from this to not allow our zeal to burn bright and fade away, as it did for Jehu to some extent. In his zeal, he did the things the Lord set before him with gusto. But long term, the Bible says;

*But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, which made Israel to sin.*

Sometimes, especially for new Christians, that initial zeal can be lost and faded over time. We are better to stoke our zeal for the Lord as a fire, and keep it going as warm embers for our entire life, than burn out quickly and fade like Jehu.

teachings.title: Seek ye first the kingdom of God
teachings.summary: Solomon building God's house before his own shows that those who seek God's kingdom first are blessed, not with a prosperity gospel but with fellowship and reward, as pillars in Christ's temple.
teachings.text:
Solomon built the House of God in 7 years, his own palace in 13. His zeal was towards the Lord.

**Matthew 6:33**
*But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

By seeking first the things of God, Solomon had the peace and blessings to them see to his own. The same promise to all believers, that in building up the temple of Christ, of which every believer is a pillar, we will be blessed in our lives.

**Mark 10:28-30**
*Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee. And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.*

Not a "prosperity gospel," so much as a promise to be rewarded in our relationships with others, and the opening of their homes to those who do the work of the Lord. Fishers of men. Persecution and all, but we shall overcome.

**Revelation 3:12**
*Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.*

The pillars Hiram made for the Temple, named *Jachin*—He will establish; and *Boaz*—in Him is strength, pictures of that Heavenly temple in which we are pillars of Christ's church.

teachings.title: Secret sin and the Father's rod
teachings.summary: God chastens His adopted children and brings secret sins to light, and the guilt of conscience should drive the believer to confess and forsake sin.
teachings.text:
Of course, David takes Bathsheba as his wife, one of many. He lives with his sin and the poor decisions he has made. But the Lord is displeased and David's actions won't remain hidden for long.

**Hebrews 12:6-7**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

**Hebrews 10:26-27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

That fearful looking for judgment, the guilt we feel when we disobey God's word, the pangs of our conscience, is a powerful motivation to get right with the Lord. To call out to Christ our redeemer for forgiveness, to repent of our actions and seek to do the right thing. Especially knowing that, as adopted children, our Father will not spare the rod, and the sins we do in secret will be revealed in the light.

**Psalms 90:8**
*Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.*

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy*.

**Luke 8:17**
*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: Get right with God before the battle
teachings.summary: Even with a righteous cause, as Israel against Benjamin, we cannot expect God's help until we are right with Him ourselves.
teachings.text:
All Israel assembles an army to go to Gibeah and demand the Benjamites turn over the sons of Belial, the reprobates who raped the concubine to death. Benjamin refuses and prepares for war.

The Israelites go to seek council of God and He grants they go forth, Judah first, and Benjamin repels them and kills many. Then they go against Gibeah again, and again are smitten.

Finally they fast and give offerings, getting right with God, and He delivers the Benjamites into their hands.

Even when our cause is righteous, and even when the right thing is to oppose the wicked, if we aren't right with God ourselves, we cannot expect His help.

He may agree with us that our grievance is real and that His vengeance has to be done, but if we aren't right with Him, if the beam isn't out of our eye, how can we expect things to go our way?

Seek ye first the kingdom of God. Walk in the Spirit. Sanctify yourself, knowing that God is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

teachings.title: Be strong and of a good courage
teachings.summary: Joshua's charge teaches that a peaceful, profitable life in Christ requires courage to obey God's commands, separate from the world and leave an example for our children.
teachings.text:
As we near the end of Joshua's life, the leader of Israel in the promised land, we see his repeating the instruction and admonition of the Lord given as promise, from **Joshua 1**;

*Now after the death of Moses the servant of the Lord it came to pass, that the Lord spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister, saying,*

*2 Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel.*

*3 Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you, as I said unto Moses.*

*4 From the wilderness and this Lebanon even unto the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your coast.*

*5 There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life: as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.*

*6 Be strong and of a good courage: for unto this people shalt thou divide for an inheritance the land, which I sware unto their fathers to give them.*

*7 Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper withersoever thou goest.*

*8 This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.*

*9 Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

This promise is the inheritance they now possess.

As a parable of salvation, the entrance into the promised land, with some battles, backslides, attacks by the world, and deliverance by the Lord, Joshua serves to remind us that to live a peaceful and profitable life in Christ requires our having the strength and courage to obey the commandments of God. To follow where He leads. That it be well with us.

To not cling to the old ways. To separate ourselves from the things of this world. To walk neither to the right nor left, but on the path God has laid out for us. To cleave ourselves to the Lord of our deliverance.

And when we are old and waxen of age, we may say to our children and grandchildren that this is the living God who delivered us, gave us prosperity and that His was are right and proper. So that they don't turn back to other gods, to disobedience. That they may inherit the same promised land of salvation, by our example. Amen

teachings.title: Meditate therein day and night
teachings.summary: As with Joshua, believers are saved by faith and blessed in this life by loving and keeping God's word, so be strong and not afraid.
teachings.text:
Beginning the **Book of Joshua**, the narrative of the capture of Canaan by the Israelites, the land given them by God for their rest, led by a deliverer named Joshua, a Hebrew variation of the name Jesus. A picture of the Christ to come.

We read the Lord speaking to Joshua as He had Moses, and reaffirming the promises made in His word, upon which Joshua trusted. By faith the people would possess the land for an inheritance, which God had sworn unto their fathers. The Lord's promise is the same to those of us who believe;

*I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee*.

The captains of the tribes give their loyalty to Joshua, to lead them in Moses' place. And God reminds Joshua of the promise made in the covenant with Moses, that if they obey His commandments, and follow His law, turning neither to the right nor the left, that they shall prosper. That by meditating day and night upon His word, and letting His law depart not from their mouth, they will have good success.

This promise is to us as well. That if we love His word and keep it in our hearts, His law upon our lips, meditating on it day and night, we will prosper and have success in this life.

Like the Israelites, we are saved by faith, delivered by His mighty hand into the promised land, but we are also blessed in this world by keeping His commandments. That it be well with us. This is the hope of God, the good news of His Gospel. The same faith that saves us today, and the same obedience that blessed those who keep His law. So be not afraid.

*Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.*

Amen

teachings.title: Obedience brings victory, disobedience fear
teachings.summary: Obedience brought Israel water and victory while disobedience sent them away in fear, as backsliding Christians retreat until they humbly return to a forgiving God.
teachings.text:
You can see comparing this story to the incident in **Exodus 17**, where Moses sent Joshua against the Amalek shortly after bringing forth the water from the rock, and they were victorious against their oppressors.

Obedience to the word of God, and they received the water and later victory against their enemies by the power of the Lord.

And here, in disobedience, slinking away in fear.

In the Christian life, we may go through phases like this. Where despite being delivered for so much early in our salvation, and despite seeing the blessings that come from obeying God, we may backslide. Become disillusioned. No longer listen to what His says, and do our own thing. Striking the rock, twice even. And when it comes time for battles against the world, turning in fear, unsure without faith.

It can be difficult to get back on track. To turn to God in humility and ask forgiveness. But if we do, He is merciful to forgive and forget. He wants to do things for His children that we may sanctify His holy name.

teachings.title: Fleeing back to Egypt in our own will
teachings.summary: Ishmael's rebellion and Judah's flight to Egypt picture how taking matters into our own hands against God's will leads back into the bondage of sin.
teachings.text:
The captivity underway, we see that the captain of the guard, of the Chaldeans, freed Jeremiah from his bonds and set him at liberty to go where he liked, with provisions and reward, freed in the name of the Lord.

The people who resisted heeding God's word are slain or led away captive to serve the Babylonian king. The poor and oppressed in the land of Judah are given the fields and vineyards and told to live peacefully. And those Jews who had fled to other lands returned.

As God had said through the prophet, so it was.

And then a particular Jew, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, using trickery, took matters into his own hands and murdered Gedaliah, the governor, and also killed collaborators and those that came down from Samaria, formerly Israel, with gifts.

And though the rebels were chased from the land and slain, Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites.

And the people, for fear of the Chaldeans who may seek to punish them for Ishmael's treachery, fled to Egypt.

These all are a figure of sin and salvation, bondage and liberty. Using our own works and judgment, going against God's will to establish our own. Fleeing back to the yoke of bondage in sin.

Jeremiah believed the Lord and it was given to him liberty. The people oppressed, set free. The wicked slain or taken away.

But Ishmael sought to establish his own ways and will. By his own works. He goes against God's judgement in rebellion, and the people flee back to Egypt, where their forefathers had been in bondage. Egypt acting as a picture of sin so often in scripture.

These things happened and were written that we can see the nature of God and man. We often cannot see how the will of God is better than our own flawed understanding of how things should be. And when we take matters into our own hands to "fix" it, we make things worse, and turn to sin.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord in good times, not only in trouble
teachings.summary: Christians who turn to God only in trouble slide back in prosperity, so we should walk with Him in praise, prayer and His word when times are good.
teachings.text:
I should note, the cycle of turning to the Lord in tribulation, only to gain the prosperity of fools, the good times and blessings that may come in relief, but then in that prosperity, turning back to sin and not listening to the word of God, is something that afflicts many Christians. It has me.

I have had periods of my life where, walking in the spirit during rough times, and being delivered and given blessings and grace, get comfortable and forget what brought me low to begin with. Sliding back to old ways that had brought me troubles to begin with. To forget the Lord and His deliverance.

This is why it is vitally important for a Christian to not wait until there's trouble in their life to take their walk seriously. To turn to the Lord in praise and thanksgiving when times are good. To humble yourself and understand that all blessings and tribulation are of God and work for good to those who love Him. To seek His wisdom early. To be constant in prayer and in His word. To do all things in Him. That His will be done.

Life's ups and downs become less volatile and the waters calm.

*And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm. And he said unto them, Where is your faith?*

teachings.title: Beginning each day as the Lord's first fruits
teachings.summary: As the tabernacle was reared on the first day of the first month and the firstfruits belong to God, the believer gives himself to God daily, washed in Christ's blood and sanctified by the Spirit through his walk.
teachings.text:
**Exodus 12:1-2**
*And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.*

**Exodus 40:17**
*And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.*

It has been a year for the children of Israel, a year since the passover and exodus from Egypt. A year in the wilderness, preparing all that God required; the covenant, the Tabernacle, the carnal ordinances and priestly vestments. The diverse washings and oils ready. The veil over the word of God, in the Ark at the heart of the Tabernacle.

And it is fitting on the first day of the first month that it is given to the Lord God as His. The first fruits are His. The first sons of Israel. The first of the flock. The first 10th of your earnings. All His. And as we begin each day as His, seeking first the kingdom of God.

**Luke 9:23**
*And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.*

**1 Corinthians 15:31**
*I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.*

We give to God ourselves daily. We put on the new man daily. We renew ourselves while we are yet in the flesh, beginning everything with God if we walk in the spirit.

And on that first day of the first month, Moses washed Aaron and his sons, anointing the vessels and sanctifying all, according to the word of God.

**Leviticus 20:7-8**
*Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you.*

**John 17:17**
*Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.*

**Hebrews 13:12**
*Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.*

**Romans 6:6**
*Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.*

We are washed in His blood, we are sanctified in the Spirit and we are made new daily, by our walk with Christ.

**Philippians 1:6**
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: Faith expected to grow
teachings.summary: After salvation our faith should grow by believing a preserved Bible and its doctrine, avoiding the snares of false teachers and carnal readings of scripture.
teachings.text:
Once you believe on the gospel and have faith that it's true, that Jesus died for your sins and that you have eternal life that can never be lost or taken away from you because of His perfect work on the cross, your faith is expected to grow.

We are conformed into the vessel that God needs for His purpose. In order to do that, you have to believe that you can find the will of God. You have to have faith that His word is available to us that we may know His will. You have to have a Bible that contains the whole word that you believe is inspired and preserved. You have to believe the doctrine that His will reveals to us through the Holy Spirit. You have to have faith that it's not by your works of righteousness but by those He has elected us too do. By His will not ours.

There are many stumbling blocks and snares laid in our path as we run towards the finish that we are predestinated for. They are laid there by people who either are not saved and fumbling, or are vipers who are deliberately misleading. You miss out on so much of God's word and the joy of living faith to faith. Contending for the faith set before us.

We've all been sidetracked off of the path by doctrines of devils and doubtful disputations at one point or another. Getting caught up in the worldly aspects that people draw out of scripture, taking things in a carnal way like Nicodemus.

In that we lose track of the spiritual aspects. Which, when we have faith in them, transforms us here in this world that we may better serve him and His will, for His glory in the next.

teachings.title: Daily bread: prayer and the word against temptation
teachings.summary: A daily walk of prayer and Bible reading feeds the new man and keeps Satan at bay, while neglecting them leaves us without the means of escape God has given.
teachings.text:
It is our daily walk with God that protects us. We ask Him to provide our daily bread, not just physical need for food, but spiritually, studying the word of God. We start our day in prayer, taking to God, and reading His word that His will be made known to us. His promises made clear that we may grow in faith. This is how we resist temptation. This is how we keep Satan at bay.

We are weak in the flesh, but if we feed the spirit, the "new man," as Paul describes it, that quickened spirit that is the surety of our eternal life, we shall overcome as Jesus has overcome.

And when we walk after the flesh, and neglect our prayers and our reading of the word, and we get caught up in the cares of this world, the way Satan caught up Jesus to the top of that mountain, to the heights of the temple, and we fear, and lust, feel wrath, covet and put ourselves at risk tempting God, and have not the means to escape though God has given them to us. His word; The pattern made by Christ to follow.

teachings.title: God's Will Is Found in His Word
teachings.summary: Those seeking God's will or more faith should start with His word, which gives faith and plainly states His will for His children.
teachings.text:
People often say they are waiting on the revelation of the "will of God" to make decisions or a sign to show them the way. They don't know if they have the faith to make a change in their lives or the understanding to do what God wants in a given situation. They express fear at circumstances or tribulation that befalls them. They may pray for guidance and strength, but struggle to find what God wants for their life.

The Bible tells us where faith comes from. It tells us God's will for us as His children. It gives instruction for how to gain knowledge, insight, understanding and peace. How to live, what our roles are. To obey those in charge of us, to love those under us. In all things, doing it for God, for that is His will. To abstain from fornication. To flee Idolatry. To trust in Him to guide us. To live by faith and to gain faith by His word. (The just shall live by faith)

If you are feeling rudderless. If you are searching for more faith. If you don't know what you should do. Start with the word. Make sure you are doing the things God has told us are His will (obviously starting with obeying the Gospel, and believing on the Lord Jesus Christ).

Tomorrow's study on Hebrews 11, the Hall of Faith heroes of the OT, will demonstrate how faith led them to serve the will of God.

teachings.title: How to increase your faith
teachings.summary: Faith grows by hearing the word, doing it, praying for faith, and obeying God in things like church and tithing so that His kept promises teach us to trust Him more.
teachings.text:
How to increase your faith? The Bible tells us:

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

Read the word and listen to preaching from His word.

**James 1:22-24**
*But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.*

By living the word we begin to rely more of God and less on ourselves. The word becomes part of us, shoring up faith.

**Psalm 51:12-14**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; And uphold me with thy free spirit. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; And sinners shall be converted unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: And my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

Pray for faith.

**Malachi 3:10**
*Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.*

God says to prove, or test Him. Obey His word (go to church, pay tithes in this example) and see how His blessings reward your faith in being a doer of the word. God keeping His promises is a huge way to learn to trust Him with more.

teachings.title: Work Faithfully Like Joseph Even in Prison
teachings.summary: Saved workers should be like Joseph, working hard and doing right in every condition, trusting God to bless their hand.
teachings.text:
Now catching up with Joseph, we see the contrast between him and his brother Judah. Who being free and rich, fell in to the wrong crowd, was taken by lust and had sons slain by the Lord for their wickedness, while Joseph was a slave who strived to do right in the eyes of the Lord and was blessed exceedingly.

As a worker, we who are saved should strive to be as Joseph. Working hard, loyally and having faith God will bless our hand if we do. Joseph in the worst of conditions, even prison, rises to the top because of his faith.

The wife who trapped him with a lie did a wicked evil to him. He could have given in, he could have cursed God for his fate, he could have been bitter or angry. Instead he just does what's right even in jail. And God continues to bless him.

**Philippians 4:12**

*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.*

teachings.title: Enoch walked with God
teachings.summary: Enoch, translated by faith and prophet of Christ's coming, is the example of walking separated and pleasing God, and the patriarchs picture the steps of coming to Christ.
teachings.text:
**And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.*

**Hebrews 11:5**
*By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.*

**Jude 1:14-15**
*And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.*

I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation.

Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God.

That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men.

But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord.

We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death.

But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus.

**John 8:51**
 *Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.*

So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death?

In **John 3**, Jesus says "*no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven,*" referring to Himself.

What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly.

Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story.

But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death.

And that's really all that matters.
