teachings.title: Peter slept: watch and pray lest ye deny Him
teachings.summary: Peter denied Christ after failing to watch and pray, and believers who fall asleep spiritually likewise deny Him, so we must stay vigilant in prayer; the Lord's supper is a symbol, not literal blood.
teachings.text:
Here we have Mark's version of events leading to the crucifixion of Jesus. Like most of Mark, it is condensed but packed with narrative and meaning.

Like some of Mark's Gospel, details change slightly from the other three, though all of it is there. The difference in timing and point of view, but the testimony the same. Unlike those who came to bear false witness against Christ before the high priests.

We see the familiar anointing by the woman with the precious oils. Hear of Judas' decision to betray Him because of it. See the last supper feast, Jesus breaking the bread and blessing the wine, saying He won't drink the new wine, fresh juice of the vine, again until He drinks it in the Kingdom of God. And while Jesus says the bread represents His body, broken on the cross, and the wine, the blood to be shed of the new testament, He clearly doesn't believe it is literally His blood, or else why say that?

Christianity is not a cannibal cult.

Jesus goes to pray, exceedingly sorrowful at His fate, but resigned to it. Peter and the others sleep when they should be on watch. Peter swears he would die with Jesus, but He tells Peter of his future denials, knowing all things that must happen.
Judas betrayal with a kiss. The ear of one of the guards cut off. The disciples scatter.

He is arrested. A detail found only in Mark, a boy wrapped in a linen blanket appears and the guards go to grab him, but he runs off naked. It is an odd account but most believe that a young Mark is that boy, his mother's house being in Jerusalem (**Acts 12:12**).

Next we see the false accusations, but Jesus condemned by the truth that He is the Christ. I believe this is important, that they did not turn Jesus over to be crucified for false claims and lies, but they murdered the Son of God for the truth that He was Christ.

In the garden, 3 times Peter swears he will stay with Jesus unto death. Jesus tells him to watch and pray that he be not tempted. Yet three times Peter is found sleeping. Peter denies Jesus 3 times when called out, breaking that vow.

Had he stayed awake, watching, praying, perhaps Peter then would have had the courage to not deny Christ and honor his vows. In the previous chapter, Jesus warns us the same as Peter, to keep watch for Him. To be vigilant and sober and ready for persecution that will inevitably come for those who standfast in His name as we await Jesus return. To pray for the strength to suffer without fear.

And most of us, like Peter, read that admonition in Mark 13, and vow to God in ourselves that we will surely be vigilant, and never back down or deny Him, even unto death. Just as Peter does in the garden.

And just like Peter, many Christians, if not all, have periods in their lives where we fall asleep, spiritually. Where we are accused by the unsaved in Jesus' name, and deny Him. Where our vows of vigilance and devotion are forgotten and abandoned. And when we are reminded of Jesus's words, we fall to our knees weeping, like Peter, understanding how unworthy we are of Christ.

So, let us learn the lesson of Peter, to stay awake and in prayer that we may not fail when tempted, that we remain vigilant for His return. That we won't deny Him when troubles come because we love Him that the world hates.

teachings.title: We slip, but walk in the word daily
teachings.summary: Believers make vows and backslide, but walking daily in the word and prayer builds faith so we are not easily tempted and are transformed by the renewing of the mind.
teachings.text:
This dichotomy of the believer, knowing the sacrifice and given the gift of eternal life anyway through God's unearned grace, through faith in Jesus, often make commitments to turn from sin. To sacrifice our comfort, wealth and possessions, even relationships, to show our love for Jesus. Vows made, despite the Bible's warnings. Good intentions, often gone astray.

We slip. We backslide. We feed the old man, neglecting the new. We have the Spirit inside of us, God's word before us and Jesus by our side, ready to carry us. And yet, for all this advantage, we turn back towards the world.

But, the Bible says if we walk in the word daily. In prayer and supplication. Growing faith on top of faith. Building on the foundation laid by Jesus, we won't be as easily tempted. We won't fail when tested. And we will not fall into sin to be accused of, and rightly punished for, but rather suffer patiently for Jesus' name, and in doing so, be pleasing to God.

So we are called to pick up our cross daily. To *be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.*

teachings.title: The sower: deep roots in good ground
teachings.summary: Jesus used natural things to teach the spiritual, which the natural man cannot discern, and saved believers can be stony or thorny ground unless they grow deep roots in God's word.
teachings.text:
In Mark 4 we see another parallel passage, this time with [Matthew 13](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/5194) which we studied a few weeks ago. (it's repeated in **Luke 8** as well, which God willing we shall see soon)

The parable of the sower is another instance of the nature of creation existing that Jesus, the word of God though whom all things were created, may use it as example to explain the heavenly things of God. The physical to understand the spiritual.

For we who are saved, the greater lesson is how we rightly divide the word, understanding that His words are spirit. That His words are eternal life, and what that means. That creation speaks the word of God for those with ears to hear and eyes to see. Who aren't without deep roots, who aren't choked out by thorns. That we may be fertile soil and bring forth fruit after our kind, 100 fold.

*And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them*.

Jesus used clearly discerned pictures of the natural, the physical, to help us understand the spiritual, the unseen, that we who are seeking God's truth or who have received the quickening of our spirit may receive faith, which the Bible says *is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.*

He uses the seen to give us insight to the unseen. This is what I was getting at [yesterday](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/6127).

But to the carnally minded all things are physical, literal. Materialists see Jesus parables as Nicodemus did; taken to absurd levels or autistic literalism and missing the actual spiritual application.

This is what the Bible means by "*the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned."*

The natural man is earthly. They rely on the wisdom of man. They lean unto their own understanding. They are those by the wayside where the word is sown and *Satan cometh immediately, and taketh* it away.

And as we see in the parable of the sower, as Jesus explains, there are saved Christians who are the stoney ground. They hear the word and believe, but having nothing to take hold of, being unprofitable, without a church, without reading their Bible, without seeking to learn the deeper things of God, *and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended.*

There are Christians who hear the word and are saved, but are among thorns, the cares of the world. They allow covetousness and lust to choke them out, and become unable to bear fruit. To get more people saved by their example. Unprofitable to God or to others.

We should seek to grow roots, deep in fertile soil which is God's word and His ways that we may win souls to Christ and bring in the harvest for the Lord.

teachings.title: Set your affection on things above
teachings.summary: Saved believers mortify the lusts of the flesh, put on the new man, and show it in honest dealing, godly homes and diligent work done for the Lord.
teachings.text:
Paul's focus shifts to now-familiar themes. If we be saved, children of light, then seek the things of Heaven. The word of God. The glory of Jesus. The resurrection to come and being raptured, caught up, into the clouds with Him in glory.

For this cause, we should mortify our members against sin of the flesh, even as Jesus preached (later in today's Matthew study), "if an eye offend thee, pluck it out." We who are heirs keep our bodies in submission and our thoughts to what's pure, good and holy.

Lusts of the flesh, lust, which is the longing for what's not yours, worshiping in the Idolatry of covetousness. As it is written, in **James 4**:

*From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not. Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.*

These sins are the reason for God's wrath upon the children of disobedience to the Gospel, but we are children of the light, the shining city in the hill. The light we have inside is a reflection and magnifying of the love God shines on us, so don't hide it, but hold it high for all to see that they might be partakers with us. Putting off anger, wrath, Malice, blasphemy, filthy conversation, the behavior of the unsaved that acts as a bushel to hide our light and turn some away from the truth within us.

We put on the new man, have honest dealings with one another ("Let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay" - also Matt 5), doing everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, in thanks to God the Father by Christ's name.

And if we are in the new man, and we have put away the lusts of the flesh, if we mortify our members, having honest dealings with one another, edifying with songs of praise and teaching the doctrines of God in psalms, our light shining as a guide to the truth for others to follow, then what does this look like?

Wives submitting to their husbands, husbands loving their wives, children honoring their parents, fathers judging their children righteously, not in wrath, not frustrating them, but as God the Father has loved you.

And, at work? Heartily and without malice or anger, do what you're asked, because we work for God, already rewarded with the kingdom of which we are heirs. Diligently and honestly setting out to complete what is required of you, with joy and a meek spirit and the confidence of your salvation.

Those who do wrong will have their reward, just as you will for your faithful service. God is not a respecter of persons, and master or boss or elected leader, all alike will face His wrath for their transgressions. That's not on us to determine. It is on us to account for ourselves in all that we do, because we do it in Jesus' name.

Many bristle at this. Be the best husband, wife, child, employee, neighbor, regardless of whatever else. Being blameless. Not dimming the reflection of the light that you walk in. *If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

teachings.title: Put off the old man, put on the new
teachings.summary: Grown in the unity of the faith, believers walk not as the reprobate who are past feeling but as new men convicted by the Spirit, putting away lying, wrath and corrupt communication.
teachings.text:
And so with that unity of faith, in the knowledge of the Son of God, *That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive; But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ.*

And so we should walk in that truth, live the love we have received. Not as others in the world who are captive by the *vanity of their mind*. The foolish doctrines of man. The ignorance that comes from *the blindness of their heart*. Not walking as the reprobate does, *being past feeling,* given over to *lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.*

In grace, through Jesus, we have a new man, created by the Spirit, and that Spirit convicts us in our sin, where the reprobate is past feeling, we are made all the more sensitive to God's will, a new man made with righteousness.

And so Paul encourages we put off lying, wrath, stealing, envy, corrupt communication, that is speech that tears down rather than edifying others. Speech that puts blame on us and hinders others faith, we shouldn't engage in.

So, with our conscience quickened, *grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption. Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.*

teachings.title: Lovest thou me? Feed my sheep
teachings.summary: Like Peter going back to fishing, saved believers drift into the world, but Christ restores them to feed His sheep and win souls, and each should follow Him without comparing himself to others.
teachings.text:
The final chapter in the Gospel of John is a kind of postscript to John's account of his time with Jesus during His earthly ministry and after His resurrection, a personal recounting of one of the appearances of the risen Christ, and a redemption arc for the apostle Peter.

Now, during this time, after having been shown their faith wasn't in vain, that Jesus is the Christ and the Son of God, but prior to His final ascension on Pentecost, it seems that some of the disciples, Simon Peter chief among them, grew restless absent their Lord. Jesus appeared unto them but wasn't the ever present fixture leading them He had been for the past 3 years. Yes they were saved, yes they knew they had salvation, and yes they knew God's word was true, and yet when left to their own devices, Peter and the others returned to their old ways. Gone a fishing.

This is something many if not most newer Christians experience, or even young Christians brought up in the faith. The rush of joy and the zeal for our Lord gives way to our habits and old life, or, without direction fades to mundane tasks of this world instead of living for the God who bought them.

As David, a man after God's own heart wrote: *Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation; and uphold me with Thy free spirit.* It happens to the best of us. That level of zeal is difficult to maintain at times.

Peter, one of the greatest Christians, who did so much for the Lord experienced this, and his leadership role lead him to take others along with him, back to the everyday life they'd left behind following Jesus. Not backslidden in sin necessarily, but back to the grind of the world. Carnal but not sinful. More aimless than lost. And here Jesus intervenes.

After an unsuccessful night of fishing, Jesus appears on the shore and in a familiar manner to earlier stories in the Gospels, He directs them to cast their empty nets another way, and they are amazed at the fill of the catch.

I think this is both real and a picture of the ministry to come in the great commission and the disciples being "fishers of men." That where there's sparsity of "fish" among the Jews, Jesus is showing them that casting a wider net out in a different direction, to the Gentiles, that the nets will be overflowing and yet not burst. As many fish as they can haul in.

Jesus dines with Peter, John, Thomas and the others, feeding them bread and fish He provides, over the fire He built. A picture of things.

The risen Christ is a bodily resurrection, Jesus eats. He's not a ghost or spirit, but risen in the flesh.

After they eat, Jesus tempts Peter three times with the question "*Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?"* And Peter, three times, swears that he does, and that Jesus knows that he does. Just as Peter had denied Jesus thrice before the cock crowed just weeks earlier, Jesus has given him a chance to redeem himself, and direction for his life if he truly loved Jesus. "Feed my sheep."

This is the direction given to all saved believers, to be part of that royal priesthood. To be His disciples. To share the Gospel and win the souls of those lost sheep. To be fishers of men. It's a personal and touching form of the great commission.

Jesus indicates to Peter where his discipleship shall lead, and John as narrator explains to the reader that it's to a martyrs death that glorified God if Peter follows Him. If he feeds His sheep.

With that understanding, Jesus says "Follow me," and Peter does, with John coming along.

Here we see another instance of Peters personality, why Jesus named him a stone. Peter, processing the death he should die for his following Jesus and feeding His sheep turns and points to John and says basically, "what about him?" It's classic Simon Peter.

Jesus' reply, "*If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me."* is a gentle rebuke and reminder that we aren't to worry so much about how other saved Christians walk their Christian life, but rather concentrate on our own. If one does nothing, that's not excuse for ourselves.

teachings.title: Unto whomsoever much is given
teachings.summary: The nearer a believer draws to God the more blessings He gives, and the more is required of him, yet His yoke is light.
teachings.text:
I think, for me at least, this is one of the hardest things about living a Godly Christian life. We talk about how the more spiritual you become the closer you draw yourself to God the closer He draws to you, and the greater the gifts He bestows on you in reward for your faith. We received salvation, then we received blessings upon blessings, we received knowledge and wisdom, answers to prayer. But *unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.*

The stronger you grow in your faith the larger the burden you're expected to tow. But even then, His yoke is light in comparison to the glory we are given in grace.

teachings.title: Missed opportunities and restoration
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Sin and self-will make us miss blessings God offered, yet the saved can still be reconciled and used if we turn and walk in His paths.
teachings.text:
And of course the practical application for Christians today that we should take away from this is that concept of missed opportunities. Of promises made by God that we just miss out on because of our own choices. Ways that we could be used by God and blessed by God, and anointings to His purpose, what could have been... All undone by sin and stubbornness and self-will.

And even if we have made mistakes in our past that could have made things turn out different had we done the right thing, there's still reconciliation with God because we are saved. There are still opportunities that He has for us because he can use anyone for His purpose. If we turn from our wicked ways, and walk in His paths, and hold His judgments, we can be restored and do great works for the Lord.

teachings.title: Spiritual triumph wounded by pride
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Like Hezekiah showing off his treasure, believers often fall hardest through pride right after God has blessed them.
teachings.text:
Hezekiah, who had expressed so much faith and appreciation in God's mercy, saving him from death and granting him 15 years longer to live, crashes out when the envoys from Babylon visit him to congratulate him for his miraculous recovery.

And instead of praising God and giving Him all glory and honor for it, shows them instead his wealth and treasure.

This is a cautionary tale for Christians. At the moments of our Christian walk, where God has blessed us, and we have been humbled enough to seek the truth, and given opportunity to serve Him, is often the moment we fall the hardest.

Spiritual triumph, wounded by pride. Our blessings are to give us opportunities to praise and sanctify the Lord to others who don't know His grace and mercy. And yet we not only hesitate to give Him the glory, we often take credit for ourselves.

This will, as we know, come back to harm Judah, as their wealth will be remembered and covered by Babylon as its empire grows. Isaiah prophesies their captivity and Hezekiah's sons serving the Babylonian king.

teachings.title: Blessing should humble us
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Israel turned to sin in the abundance God gave when they humbled themselves, so believers should let blessing humble them and stay grateful in good times and bad.
teachings.text:
Again, Israel, represented by Ephraim, is preached against for their sins, and Hosea prophesying their coming destruction. The word of the Lord says that when they humbled themselves, trembling, He was merciful and gave them blessings in abundance. But that in their abundance, they turned from Him to sin.

God again compares them to a cloud without water, a morning cloud that rises up to be burned off in the heat of the day. Morning dew that evaporates as the sun rises. Chaff that blows away easily. Smoke that rises and dissipates.

As James describes our own short lives on this earth; *Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.*

But Hosea is preaching to a nation, and God has been longsuffering towards it, and yet they continued in a downward spiral of sin.

When we are blessed by the Lord, it should humble us. Not make us exalt ourselves. Not grow comfortable. But learn to be grateful in good times and bad, always turning towards the Lord. Humble ourselves, because it is by His good pleasure.

*O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself; but in me is thine help.* Christ Jesus, the only begotten Son. That in Him shall there be a King.

God reminds them, they demanded a human king, despite His warnings. And in His anger He gave them Saul, and now all these generations later, it has availed them not. The Lord took away their king in His wrath.

Israel is as a baby who won't leave the womb, despite their mother's travail. And so her sorrows are multiplied upon them. Samaria will become desolate, for she rebelled against her God.

teachings.title: Uzziah's pride: stay humble
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Uzziah's pride over God's blessings cost him everything, reminding us that God's rewards are given so that others may see and believe, so stay humble.
teachings.text:
Uzziah allowed pride in himself for the victories and blessings given of God, to put himself where he ought not be, and it cost him all that he had, living out his days as a leaper, being buried in the field of his father's, and not their sepulcher.

When we do great things for God, and are rewarded openly, we should remember that the rewards are not primarily for our benefit. Yes God wants to bless us, yes we will see success when we set our eyes on doing His will. But the real purpose is that others may see and believe.

Just as wrath against the ungodly, and chastening of backslidden believers reveals the truth of God to men.

Stay humble.

teachings.title: Hezekiah's pride after his recovery
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: After God delivers us we are prone to grow proud and comfortable as Hezekiah did, so we should praise the Lord for His mighty acts and stay humble.
teachings.text:
But a story of an Old Testament saint wouldn't be complete without an example of their sin. For all have sinned and come short of the glory of God. And Hezekiah was no different.

The king of Babylon sends his regards, having heard of hezekiah's illness. And the recovered Hezekiah entertains the servants of the king. The Bible doesn't tell us that Hezekiah praised the Lord for his recovery, but rather showed them all of the riches of his kingdom, the city, his household and in the Temple.

His sin is pride. Boasting of his riches while just a short while before he was on his deathbed.

This is possibly the most common thing that I have experienced myself and witnessed in others; a great triumph of the Lord acting miraculously in our lives, followed by a low point where we forget the trouble we were in, and grow comfortable, taking it for granted.

It is so easy for sin to creep in when this happens.

One of the ways to avoid it is to not only go to God in our troubles and with supplications, but to praise the Lord for when He acts mightily in our lives. Bragging on him rather than ourselves. Staying humble.

Because of Hezekiah's sin, Isaiah comes to him and tells him that God has judged and that all of the treasures he had shown off to Babylon would be carried away there. And that his son s will be eunuchs to their King.

Hezekiah accepts the rebuke and the judgment. And is thankful that it won't be in his day. But that small comfort isn't worth the moment of sin.

Judah will soon learn a lesson in humility. And while God won't destroy them yet, because of his own interests and his promise to David, they will be made desolate for 70 years.

teachings.title: How sin compounds: David and Bathsheba
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: David's sin began with neglecting his duty, showing that skipping prayer and the word leaves us open to temptation and that unconfessed sin compounds.
teachings.text:
The famous story of David and Bathsheba, and the King's gravest sins. Coveting, adultery, lying and murder.

 David not being with his men in battle during the time for war left him opportunity for sin. Idle hands are the devil's tools. His gaze falling on another man's wife and her nakedness, compounded by the covetous nature of the lust it stirred in him. His use of his station to bring her in unto him to lay with her. All stemming from that initial dereliction to his duty.

A Christian who sins often finds themselves in that situation by a similar set of circumstances. We are to crucify our flesh daily and walk in the Spirit. The Bible tells us that we should wake in the morning in prayer. Beginning the day getting right with the Lord.

But David tarried in bed, rather than in battle. And rather than refresh himself in the Spirit, thinking of the things of the Lord, he wandered.

When we do that, blow off our commitments, "take a day off" from prayer or study, we often wander, too.

Temptations that we would not normally experience present themselves, and with our minds not on the spiritual things of God, we can give in to them.

Of course David's actions have consequences. Our Father often lets those consequences of our willful sin have repercussions that are for our admonition and instruction. A chance to make it right. And yet often our sinful nature leaves us making it worse.

David seeks to cover up Bathsheba's pregnancy by sending for her husband, Uriah. Hoping the Hittite would take the opportunity of coming from the front lines to Jerusalem to visit his wife and lay with her, covering up the pregnancy.

But Uriah has more honor than that, and refuses the comfort of home while his fellows are encamped for war. His commitment to his duty contrasting with David's initial dereliction.

David tries again, all but ordering Uriah to his home, sending a feast from his own royal kitchen, and still Uriah stays with the guards and servants.

David's attempts to get Uriah to do the wrong thing fail, so the King takes more desperate measures to cover for his sin. He orders his general, Joab, to send Uriah into the hottest of battles, that he may be smitten dead. David goes from a momentary lapse in duty and honor to premeditated murder.

This is how Christians backslide. This is how sin compounds.

teachings.title: Driving the Jebusites from Zion
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: David driving the Jebusites out of Jerusalem pictures driving sin from the heart, which is never permanent while we live in the flesh, so we must crucify ourselves daily.
teachings.text:
If you remember from **Joshua 15**, the Jebusites had been a remnant of Canaan that the Israelites had failed to remove from the land.

*As for the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.*

Even unto the days of the prophet Ezra, centuries after David took Jerusalem from them, they were in the land, teaching their abominations to the children of Israel, along with other nations God had commanded to be destroyed.

**Ezra 9:1**
*Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.*

But we see that under David, they were taken from the heart of Zion.

This is a picture of the nature of sin in the Christian life. David is representative of Israel getting right. Walking in the Spirit. Accepting and doing God's will. Driving sin from your heart.

As we see, this isn't permanent. As long as the flesh lives, we sin. And if we turn away from walking in the Spirit, doing what's right in God's eyes, it can fester and destroy us. We must crucify ourselves daily. Seeking the will of God.

teachings.title: Be sober, be vigilant after a victory
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Right after a victory of faith David nearly sinned against Nabal and then took more wives, showing temptation comes hardest when we grow complacent after God blesses us.
teachings.text:
It is interesting that just a chapter after David had trusted in the Lord, by passing on the opportunity to slay Saul and end his exile, showing great faith and patience, David reacts so strongly to the railing of Nabal.

Not only had David humiliated the king, heaping coals on his head, and gained more favor in the eyes of the Lord by not rebelling against the appointed leader over him, despite Saul's murderous heart, David had shown the Christian spirit to his men who wanted him to kill the king. Being a great example to them, and by extension to all of us who have read this.

But sometimes, especially after a victory in the Christian's life, we face temptations. The world turns harder against us. We become less guarded against our own sins, and fall victim to our flesh, just as we should be growing more in the Spirit.

Sometimes it feels like we are determined to sabotage what God has wrought in us, and the Devil is all too happy to give us the opportunity to stumble and fall, that he can accuse us before the Lord.

Sometimes we catch ourselves. Other times our passions run so hot, we need another saved person to act as our better angel, advising us against the evil we are set to do, as Abigail does here for David.

And often, even if we turn from the worst that we might do, we settle on a lesser sin to scratch that itch within our flesh. The thorn in our hearts.

Abigail, a godly woman and beautiful, was loyal to her wicked husband. She didn't betray Nabal or allow David to take him off her hands, rather she saved his life. She did right by the Lord and by her husband and it worked out for her that the Lord destroyed Nabal.

But David is married, and yet seeks her for his wife. While Abigail does nothing wrong. Being a window, David falls into sin. And not only with Abigail, which may have been a great love story, but with yet another woman, making Abigail a sister wife to Ahinoam. David's sin affects her, and will lead him to greater sin with Bathsheba, and eventually will serve as a bad influence on his son Solomon, who will have a thousand wives and concubines.

This is why we can't rest on our victories, we can't become complacent just because we have done the right thing, and God has blessed us for it. We should always keep in mind **1 Peter 5:8;**

*Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour*

teachings.title: A battle is not the war
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: After God gives a restored Christian small victories, spiritual enemies rally, so we must be more vigilant and wait on Christ rather than lean on our own understanding as Saul did.
teachings.text:
As we saw in chapter 12 when Samuel told the people of Israel that God had appointed them a king, despite that not being His will, that the people convicted of this sin asked for forgiveness and the sacrifices were offered and the Lord reiterated His promise to them for salvation. That if they simply turn to Him and appreciate what He's done, He will be their God and they will be His people.

And so the Philistines which had occupied parts of Israel setting up garrisons, were afflicted by the small standing army Saul had assembled. Jonathan and Saul each liberating cities from the garrisons which had been set up in them by the enemy. Small victories that then provoked the Philistines into assembling a mighty army.

In a similar way, Christians who have sinned and gotten right with the Lord may experience small victories and regained ground in their Christian life. God may have us live with the consequence of our sin, but He does help us to win battles against the things that had led us there.

But like the Philistines who rallied a great army, our spiritual enemies often do the same. Their garrisons may be removed from places in our heart, but that doesn't mean that the battle is won. It's times like that where we have to be more vigilant to obey God's word and to trust in Him.

Saul didn't learn that lesson. He leaned on his own understanding. After having provoked the Philistines into a massive retaliatory response, and seeing the fear of the people under him, Saul disobeyed the word of God doing what seemed right in his own eyes.

We have to be careful not to undercut whatever progress God has given us. In a like manner we need to be even more vigilant as we see success given us by God.

Sometimes we get a false confidence in our own abilities, giving ourselves more credit that we deserve. Not understanding that a battle isn't the war. That we need to wait on Christ Jesus, our high priest, rather than making our own way. Often we can fall further and cause more trouble for ourselves in the long run. Sowing seeds of failure in our haste. Backsliding further than we had when God last delivered us. A cautionary tale.

teachings.title: Gideon's ephod became a snare
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Gideon let success lead him to make an ephod and draw Israel away, a trap for successful Christians and preachers whose pride undoes their work.
teachings.text:
However, he does ask for tribute. The gold earrings of the men slain, which when taken together was a substantial weight of gold. And while judging Israel the rest of his days, back in Ophrah of Manasseh, he takes the gold of his spoil and makes himself an ephod. A golden vestment of the office of the high priest.

This is the snare of Gideon. This causes the children of Israel to go a whoring.

Some interpretations of this make the ephod an idol that is worshipped, but it seems unlikely that Jerubbaal, aka Gideon, a smasher of idols, "the accused of Baal," would set up an idol and there's no indication that they worshipped the ephod itself.

It is more likely in my opinion to mean that Gideon, despite his declining to be a king, allowed his popularity and fame to make him seek to usurp the place God chose, Shiloh, and the office of the high priest to whom the Ephod crafted by Moses belonged. And rather than go to Shiloh for spiritual matters, many in Israel came down to Ophrah and Gideon.

The number of wives and sons he produced showed that he did take advantage of his glory, despite deferring the glory of the victory to God. The spoils he took as tribute became a snare, and caused the Israelites to go whoring, away from the commandment of the Lord.

So we see, even Gideon, full of fear. Requiring signs. Witnessing the miracle of their defeat of a troop of over a hundred and fifty thousand with 300 men, let his success go to his head. Leading him to sin.

This is a trap some very successful Christians fall in to. Who have been used mightily for God, and done great works for Him. For all their humility and understanding that it was not of them, pride eats away at their character. God's success begins to seem to them to be a partnership. And their *idea* of what God wants take the place of what God actually wills for them.

We can apply this to great modern preachers of the word, who have won thousands of souls to Christ, and then, building an empire from the success, sow the seeds their own downfall.

And the people who they helped forget these men, after they've died. And their children turn to wickedness. Worshiping Baal as the Israelites do. The children of these great soldiers for God not turning out to be godly men, but wicked, like Gideon's son, Abimelech.

teachings.title: Beware the sin of Achan
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Like Achan, believers are often tempted to covet right after God gives victory, so we must stay on God's path even in success.
teachings.text:
The spiritual application of this story, like much of the accounts of Israel from Egypt though the promised land, can be applied to our lives as saved Christians. Sometimes, even as we are delivered by God from our enemies, or having received blessings by our obedience and reward, our hearts turn to covetousness. We are given a temptation to sin. The devil loves to bring a test before us when God is in the process of rewarding our faith in Him. When we are the most comfortable.

Many times in the Christian life, you will find that you've made it through something by walking in the Spirit and trusting in God, only to stumble at the finish line because the relief turns to complacency. Satan looks for ways to accuse us and what better time than victory?

The lesson of Achan can be a valuable one, to not depart from the path God laid out for us, even in victory, because it can undo all the good God has done in our life, and lead to our destruction. The devil hides temptations even in the smallest victories of our lives. How much more the temptation when the odds seem overwhelmingly against you, and yet you persevere in the Lord.

Beware of the sin of Achan. Don't let the devil snatch defeat from victory.

teachings.title: Quail until it come out at your nostrils
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: When a backslider runs back to old sins God often gives him his fill until it is loathsome, chastening every son He receives.
teachings.text:
In that spirit, we can appreciate God's chastisement of the Hebrews, giving them the meat they crave, in abundance.

*Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days; But even a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome unto you: because that ye have despised the Lord which is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt?*

If you have experienced this, where you backslide and fall away from walking in the spirit, longing for the old life you left behind when you were born again, and starve the new man to feed the old, you've witnessed this same thing.

Phone calls or texts from an old drinking buddy. A woman at work suddenly seems interested in you. The gang from high school wants to get together. The dealer you used to score from you run into unexpectedly. It is more than a test. It's often a lesson of excess in the thing you were lusting after, and you find if you should stumble back into sin, that it doesn't hold the same appeal. That you can't enjoy it. Even if you run greedily after whatever it is you missed about spiritual Egypt, your time in bondage, in short order you'll see it as repulsive and gross. You will have it coming out of your nostrils.

Some prefer that misery. Even eating the metaphorical quail long after it has spoiled and sickened them. But for many Christians it is a wake-up call and a reminder of how good we have it walking with the Lord.

*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.*

Thank God for His love and correction.

teachings.title: Liberty from sin to walk in the Spirit
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Salvation by grace without works frees believers to be sanctified by the Spirit, which is why faithful Baptist churches bear the fruit of separated lives.
teachings.text:
This is the practical application of the law, and the spiritual application for those of us at liberty from sin in Christ, we see the pattern of what is right in God's eyes, that we may be sanctified by Him through the Spirit.

Because of the weakness of the flesh and the failing of sinful man, we need a savior. We need Christ, and through the grace of God, we are given Jesus to do what we couldn't. That by faith in Him we have remission of sin and peace with God. And in that peace, paid for entirely by the blood of Jesus, we can then be sanctified by the Spirit.

We are to standfast in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free. Not being entangled again with the yoke of bondage. Our unrighteousness done away with by the grace of God to His glory. His mercy being a revelation from Heaven through we who are saved that others may see and come to the knowledge of the truth, and repent towards God. Believing on Christ, to be set at liberty as well.

Despite some, who have crept in privily to spy out liberty, and who slanderously report that we say "let us do evil..." The liberty we have from sin, the blessing that God will not impute sin to us, is to allow us to then walk in the spirit and not fulfill the lusts of the flesh. To strive for the mark that God calls us towards, that we may be conformed to His use, that His will be done. That we be sanctified. That we be holy because He is holy. And in that sanctification, we can bring others to Christ, being a light unto the world as Israel was to be to other nations.

This is why, if we take an honest look at those who preach salvation by grace through faith, without works, without depending on our own selves to turn from sin, or change our lives, or "make Jesus our Lord," but by acknowledging the truth of God, we see so many who are living for God today.

We see those set free in Christ turning from sin, walking in the Spirit, doing great things for the Lord. Not sanctification to gain justification, but sanctification to become vessels fit for His use. That we may be blameless before men. That we may be justified before men, who may say, as in **James 2**, show me your faith by your works. That we may lead others to the truth.

And so, you see independent fundamental Baptist churches that are soul winning, studying to be approved, comparing that which they received with scripture to see if it is so. Engaged in the edification of the local church and reaching out to the poor, the brokenhearted, that they may find peace with God.

Fundamentalist Baptists are often the most separated, actually allowing the Spirit to work effectually in them to remove thorns from their hearts, and to feed the new man, starving the flesh.

This is not to say all Baptists or even a majority of Baptist churches are perfect. This is not to say that just by being Baptist, you become justified or holier than anyone else, or that only a Baptist Church can achieve this.

But the fruit of the more stedfast Baptist churches is undeniably a more separated people doing great works for the Lord.

teachings.title: The spirit willing but the flesh weak
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Saved Christians are dead to the law in the spirit, but the old man still reigns in the flesh, so we do what we would not until the redemption of the body.
teachings.text:
And so, building on the implications of our faith, the law and grace, Paul comes to the matter of our flesh, in this world before the resurrection, but after our salvation and the quickening of our spirit in Christ.

Christ, in whose death, we die also to the law, freed then to the Spirit, married to Him in grace. Just as the woman described by Paul is free from her marriage vows at the death of her husband, we are free from sin and death with Jesus. And baptism is a like figure representing this. We are born again, in the Spirit.

But not in the flesh. That's the lively hope we have, Jesus being the first fruits of the resurrection with the same promise to us who believe. That we will shed this corruptible body for incorruptible. The dead in Christ and those that are alive and remain at His coming, all will receive glorified bodies that know not sin. Chapter 8 of Romans will delve a bit more into this, but then the question for Christians is; in the meantime, what?

Our new man, inside, spirit quickened by the Holy Ghost, sealed unto the day of redemption, knows not sin. It can't, being dead to the law.

For as Paul explains, with the commands of God to tell us what is righteous and holy, there is no sin.

He says he was alive once without the law, we all have been. Innocent children who don't know there is a right from wrong, do no sin. But when the knowledge of the law comes, and they in the flesh choose sin, the spirit dies to the law.

Had Adam and Eve not had the commandment in the garden, they wouldn't have sinned in eating the apple. Had the laws of God not come onto Noah and then Moses, showing us His light, we wouldn't know our flesh of the old man leads us to darkness. The law itself is holy and true. And being saved, our spirit is willing but our flesh is weak.

The old man still reigns in our members. Our flesh.

Sin takes advantage of the law to show we lust in the flesh. Not that the law is evil, but we are.

And like Paul, we do what we would not. We don't do what we should, despite wanting to. Without the newness of spirit we can't.

*For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not.*

As Jesus admonished the Apostles who were to keep watch as He prayed at Gethsemane, who fell asleep multiple times;

**Matthew 26:41**
*Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.*

teachings.title: We sin every day
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Sinless perfection is impossible in the flesh, but walking in the Spirit through prayer, scripture, church and soul winning makes the flesh easier to mortify.
teachings.text:
It is important to know as a Christian, we are not perfect and sinless perfection isn't possible in our flesh.

We all are sinners. We all deserve death and Hell but in Christ we are given His righteousness that we may be given justification before God.

We sin, every day. But unlike the unsaved (which we were and should never forget the mercy we were shown, that we not think too highly of ourselves before the unsaved), we have the Spirit within us, and our own spiritual new man cries out to do good.

But to the flesh, we are called to sin.

What do we do? The Bible says if we walk in the spirit, feeding that new man, praying, studying scripture, going to church to be edified with the congregation, practicing true religion which is care for the poor, widows, fatherless, and most importantly sharing the Gospel with others that they may be comforted as we are by the promise, that the flesh becomes easier to mortify. To subdue.

teachings.title: Our sanctification is not about salvation
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Walking in the Spirit reveals more sin and gives grace to escape it, a refining that makes us useful vessels, not a means of salvation.
teachings.text:
And, if we walk in the spirit we will also learn more about the holiness of God and His law, and in that knowledge come to see more things that are sinful. It is impossible to feed the new man with the things of God and not come to be convicted by the Spirit that things we thought not sin, actually are. But the great mystery of that dichotomy is that, despite the knowledge increasing our occasion for the flesh, we have the grace and power to escape from it.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

It is a refining process. One that removes thorns in our flesh we didn't know we had. This process of sanctification makes us more valuable vessels for God's will. It makes us better able to serve His Gospel. To have real fruits of the spirit. To win others to Christ, and further, to instruct and guide babes in Christ to maturity that they may be able to better serve God as well.

This is the point of our Christian walk.

It's not about you. It's not about finding yourself, or happiness or whatever new age and pagan selfish nonsense our flesh comes up with to lead us away from the spirit.

We are saved already, and justified by the perfect work of Christ Jesus that we believe on. Rejoice. In His blood we have overcome.

Our sanctification isn't about salvation. It is about becoming acceptable tools in God's shed. To be workmen who aren't ashamed. Good and faithful servants.

teachings.title: The fruits of the Spirit are not automatic
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Even Paul struggled with sin, so good works and victory over sin are a daily choice to walk in the Spirit, and when we fall we confess and are forgiven.
teachings.text:
And just one more point that I've touched on here but needs to seriously be stressed; the fruits of the Spirit don't come automatically.. Just because we are saved doesn't mean that we will do good. Just as it doesn't mean we will stop sinning.

Paul, who many consider the greatest Christian of all time for his understanding of God's word, writes of himself here in Romans chapter 7;

*But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.*

Writing in **1 Timothy 1:15**
*This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.*

Paul and the other authors of the epistles write to be edifying to the brethren, that they *should* do good, that they *should not* do evil. That we *should* walk in the spirit that we do not fulfill the lusts of the flesh.

This is a choice. As Jesus says;

**Luke 9:23**
*And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.*

It's a daily choice. It is on us to reject the temptations of the flesh by walking in the spirit.

But it is not automatic. Even Paul struggled with sin.

So many people beat themselves up for failing to stop sin in their life. For falling short. But what does the Bible tells us? That all fall short.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

And so we are instructed; *Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.*

And when we stumble, confess to God who has adopted us as sons, and He will forgive us and help us with our infirmities.

Don't allow the men of this world to judge your walk, and in doing so place stumbling blocks and snares for you. Those hypocrites have their reward. Instead, every day make a commitment to walk in the spirit, do for others, what you can. And give glory to God for His righteousness and mercy, in Christ Jesus. The rest will sort itself out.

teachings.title: Shall we continue in sin
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Grace is no license to sin; baptism pictures our death with Christ so we should walk in newness of life, though holiness is not automatic as Lordshippers imply.
teachings.text:
**Romans 6** builds on the conclusion of the doctrine of the law of grace, and the implications for that liberty which we have in Christ. That we are no longer dead in sin with the judgment against us in unrighteousness, but born again a new man in the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ.

Having proven this, that we are justified before God by faith, and standfast in His grace, what then?

Shall we sin that grace may abound? If it glorified God to be forgiven our sin, would it be to His glory that we sin all the more? (Again, as some slanderously reported about the apostles, and those who continue this smear today, calling the glory of God "cheap grace" and "a license to sin")

Again, *God forbid. How should we, that are dead to sin, love any longer therein?*

We are free, in Christ, that when we are baptized as believers, it is into death with Christ, just as when we rise up from the water, it is a picture of our rising with Him into eternal life.

Even so, we should walk in newness of life.

If we are picturing the image of Christ in our baptism, death, burial and resurrection, then our old man, our sinful nature after the flesh should be considered nailed to the cross with Him. *That the body of sin might be destroyed.*

Being dead in Christ we are risen with Him, and risen, death has no more dominion over Him, or us through Him. We are dead to sin but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Paul is really hammering this point home because it is not automatic that we who are saved turn from our sins. That the new man's presence doesn't preclude the old man's lusts of the flesh from warring in our members. Our eyes and tongue betray us. Our feet are swift to sin.

If we automatically became holy by our salvation, this wouldn't have to be taught us, and it wouldn't be given us as a reminder in nearly every epistle. If we were given to "show fruit" to prove we are saved, as Lordshippers and other hypocrites suggest, it wouldn't be necessary to explain the old man vs the new.

teachings.title: Who is on the Lord's side
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: At the golden calf some never truly believed, some like Aaron backslid, and a remnant stood with God, so we should not be cocky but fear God's scourging of His sons.
teachings.text:
But, again we see the parallels to spiritual salvation, and the application of these things that serve as our examples. That many when led up out of bondage to sin and to the wilderness that is our earthly life, fall away having believed in vain. Never truly having faith. Turning immediately to other gods and to sin. Others, like Aaron, who have faith and accepted God's grace, backslide and go with the crowd, falling into sin. Still others like the sons of Levi, stand back, a loyal remnant of God.

Like the parable of the sower, there are some seeds sown that never take root, others that have shallow roots but are taken away by the cares of the world. And some falls on fertile ground and with deep roots produces much fruit.

It is easy to look at the Israelites, throughout the Old Testament, as a uniquely wicked and ungrateful people, who don't love the Lord, their deliverer, as they should.

But we shouldn't get too cocky in our own conceits. Because none of us live up to what we should. All of us fall short and with a stiff neck of our own will, stand in defiance of the Lord who bought us, putting our own will before His. Christians today who sit down to eat and drink and rise up to play.

We should consider the fate of those 3,000. God will scourge every son He receives.

It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Living God.

teachings.title: Lest the people repent when they see war
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: God guides new believers away from the worst trials early, and remembering His strong arm keeps us from turning back to the bondage of Egypt, as the parable of the sower warns.
teachings.text:
And so commanded God to all of Israel. To commemorate the day He freed them from bondage and brought them out to the land He promised their fathers, and gave ordinances regarding the feast of unleavened bread, the removal of all yeast and leavening from the home for 7 days, and the consecration of the firstborn males, in remembrance of the slaying of the firstborn of Egypt and as a picture of the Christ to come.

Leaven represents sin in the Bible. Egypt, bondage to sin. This is done in remembrance of God, just as the Lord's supper took the place of Passover, and Jesus took the place of the lamb without blemish. And so going forward, Israelites were to offer sacrifice of the first born, and in place of their first born, to sacrifice them.

Jews today claim the bar mitzvah, the purchase of sanctification by use of silver shekels, is the equivalent of the blood sacrifice required by God, because they don't worship Him or follow the Old Testament at all. They worship moloch, and follow the traditions of men.

The idea of parents instilling in their firstborn male the knowledge of Him, and what He has done for Israel is important. God needed them to retain knowledge of Him and His Promises in mind throughout generations, that in the days of Jesus, a remnant may be saved.

God, with a fiery pillar by night and a pillar of smoke as a cloud, by day, took the Israelites and the mixed multitudes our, towards the Red Sea, that they not pass through the land of the Philistines, *Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt*.

We see this in newly saved Christians lives, all the time. There is an effort by God to guide us away from the worst tribulation in the beginning, that our faith grows, so we don't immediately turn back to sin. To bondage of the law.

We know from the parable of the sower that even this period of the newness of the joy of salvation isn't enough for many. That the joy and relief can give way to the cares of the world.

*Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them.*

Not everyone who is saved is fertile ground. Many fall away or become offended by and by. That is why the Apostles were so intent on edification. On walking in the new man.

Even David, the apple of God's eye, felt this:

**Psalm 51:12-14**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

But by keeping in memory the strong arm of the Lord that has lifted us out of bondage by His own works, by the atonement and sanctification given us by Christ's blood, His death burial and resurrection, we will not repent towards Egypt, but press on to the promised land.

teachings.title: We melt down the treasure God provided
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Like Israel turning Egypt's gold into the calf, saved Christians who forget the bondage God freed them from turn their blessings into idols and excuses to sin.
teachings.text:
I find it interesting that in spoiling Egypt, where the people gave the Israelites their gold and treasure, would ultimately become grievous sin in the wilderness, melted down to form the image of the calf the Hebrews worshipped while Moses was on Mt Sinai with God.

Is that a picture of the blessings we have as saved Christians, which by not staying with the word of the Lord, not walking in the new man with the remembrance of the bondage God freed us from in Christ, that we risk turning to sin; into idols?

How often we forget our deserved fate. How often we forget what should have happened to us based on our choices, and spared the worst of the consequences by God in His mercy through Christ Jesus.

I don't know a saved Christian, no matter how backslidden and carnal, who when pressed won't admit that God saved them physically from the most grave of consequences they rightly deserved. Moving things in our life in such a way that we were delivered from the fruit of our sin, as we gained faith. But many forget when it's not present in their mind. Many take their blessings for granted and turn their comfort into an excuse to sin.

There are people who have relatively easy lives and yet never come to peace with their life and the choices they made. And so they are miserable.

We who are saved are blessed, that we can come to terms with it and understand what a blessing things actually are when you consider how bad it could be given the choices we've made.

The humility and perspective we gain by understanding just how pitiful our position was that we trusted in God and called upon the name of the Lord, should allow us to see the bondage He freed us from and appreciate the wilderness He's led us through on our way to the promised land.

God spares us by saving us from ourselves. His hand is constantly upon us. Like the Hebrews. His light, guiding us in the darkness. His bread, His word, come down from Heaven to feed and nourish us like manna.

And like the Hebrews, we often complain at the hardships we must endure to get ourselves back to the place God has intended for us had we not sojourned in Egypt. Had we not chased after sin.

We forget where we were. We forget how we escaped. We forget how the blood of the lamb upon our hearts, as it was upon the doorposts, spared us from destruction.

We melt down the treasure God provided, and, *as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.*

teachings.title: It is written: resisting the devil by the word
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Jesus overcame Satan's temptations not by His divine nature but by clinging to every word of God, the pattern for how we resist temptation.
teachings.text:
Luke chapter 4 picks up with Jesus after His baptism in the Jordan and by the Holy Spirit, having been proclaimed by the Father "His Son, in whom Im well pleased."

The Gospel says, Jesus was led of the Spirit to the wilderness, and there to fast and be tempted by Satan, 40 days. It is often overlooked that the three instances given here and in the other Gospels are not the only tests of the devil Jesus suffered. He was tempted 40 days.

Jesus hungered. He thirst. He was weary. He was alone. Without shelter. Cold at night. Hot in the sun of the day. In all ways tempted as we are. But without sin.

And Jesus was led of the Spirit to this temptation, He was not given a pass, was not brought to the temple in Jerusalem to preach the Gospel to an adoring throng of people. He was brought to desolate places where the prince of this world would tempt Him.

Satan, the accuser of the brethren, seeking to corrupt the Christ, and derail God's plan of salvation for the world, tested and tried Jesus that he may go before the Father and say, "your Son is not worthy to be a sacrifice. He is not without blemish." But Jesus withstood Satan, and in doing so, gave us the pattern for dealing with temptation in our lives.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

The Bible says Jesus was tempted as we are. Knows our infirmities and understanding, shows mercy on us. We are not given more than we can handle. If we reject Satan, God will provide us a way.

That way is found in what Jesus used to resist Satan. The word of God.

So understanding that Jesus did not have some special means to supernaturally avoid succumbing to sin, it wasn't His divine nature that saved His human flesh from falling, but His doing His Father's will, and clinging to the word.

Jesus was hungry and weak, and the devil said to turn a stone to bread. A temptation of the flesh. To satisfy the immediate need to please ourselves physically.

And Jesus replied *It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.*

Note His use of "it is written." That man loves not by bread. Not by the needs of the flesh. That there is more to this than satisfying our physical desires but that we live by *every word of God*.

He quotes scripture to put of the devil from Him. Every word of God is all we need to live. (The presupposition is that, in order to be true, we have access to every word of God. Thus the preservation of His word). This having double meaning, as the manna in the desert was a picture of Christ, Jesus who is the bread of life come down from Heaven, and He is the Word of God made flesh, through whom eternal life is given to all who believe.

And Jesus, using God's word, rebukes Satan.

Then, tempting Jesus with power, Satan offers Him the thrones of this world, of whom Satan is god. Given power to influence kings and regents. The spirits that bring wickedness to high places. Overseeing the principalities of the rulers of the darkness of this world. By supernatural means, he takes Jesus to the top of a mountain and shows Him all the lands of man in the world. The devil says to Jesus, worship me and I will give you an earthly kingdom, ultimate power.

And Jesus, again citing scripture rejects him; *for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.* And again the power of the knowledge of God's word saves Jesus from temptation.

Finally, frustrated, Satan places Jesus upon the spire of the temple in Jerusalem. Hundreds of feet in the air. And says to jump, because the scriptures say that God the Father would not suffer to see even His foot dash against the rocks. That God would send angels to stop Jesus from even stubbing His toe, so surely they would catch Him.

*And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.*

teachings.title: Turning to scripture to resist the devil
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Just as Jesus resisted Satan with scripture and trusted the Father to provide, we can resist any temptation when we turn to God and stay in His word.
teachings.text:
Again, using scripture, Jesus turns aside Satan and his temptations.

And the devil departs having failed to stand against the word of God. In Matthew we read; *Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.*

By faith of this Jesus endured, that God the Father would provide. That He loved Him and was true. Not slack in His promise. By turning to scripture, Jesus resisted sin, and was rewarded for His trust.

This is the pattern for our lives. The path we follow, led by Christ. When the Spirit leads us into the wilderness. When we are weak, and tired and hungry. When we are in peril, as Jesus upon the steeples of the Temple. When we are at our lowest physically and mentally, Satan will come to tempt us. And when he does, we can know that none of what he offers us to sin, none of the temporary satisfactions of the flesh, are beyond our means to resist as long as we turn to God, stay in His word, and have faith that our needs will be met by Him Who loves us.

teachings.title: Esau sold his birthright for pottage
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Carnal Christians who trade their blessings for fleshly pleasures are like Esau, keeping sonship but losing blessings here and in the kingdom.
teachings.text:
Issac, at 60 years old, finally becomes a father. In an echo of his own birth, Rebekah is as barren as Sarah was. Yet God intervenes, and the couple conceive twin boys.

As God says to Rebekah, there are two nations striving within her. One shall be strong, and the elder will serve the younger.

Esau, the first born, hair red as the pottage he'd sell his birthright for. Red is the meaning of Edom. Jacob, second born, holding on to Esau's foot, as they are taken from their mother.

*And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.*
*And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.*

God wastes no time on irrelevant details. Isaac's life story is briefly skimmed over. Only the details of the inheritance and blessing matter to the story God is telling. Of the elder serving the younger. Of the law and of faith.

And so, we come to adult Esau and Jacob, men established as a hunter, and a man of the field, while the younger tends flocks, living in tents. No great hero and hunter, proficient with weapons like his elder brother, but a plain man.

Jacob makes a red pottage, a lentil soup. Esau, hungry and tired, saying "*Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint*."

Most interpret this to just mean normal hunger. Not truly fainting or starving in a serious sense. Just ravenous from being out in the field hunting, and wanting to please his flesh by eating the pottage.

Jacob says he will feed his brother in exchange for his birthright. And despising his birthright, that is not caring about it, willing to trade it for a momentary satisfaction of the flesh, Esau agrees.

Paul uses this illustration in **Hebrews 12** regarding fornicators among the believers, who have the inheritance but lose the blessings that come with the birthright we share in Christ Jesus for the same momentary satisfaction of the flesh. That later, though he repented of giving away his inheritance by law to his younger brother, having a change of heart too late, and losing the eventual blessings meant for him.

Christians who live carnally, after the flesh, despising their birthright received through Christ, losing blessings of God for their own morsel of meat, a simple bowl of pottage, are like Esau. And while we still retain sonship, and gain a share in the kingdom, the blessings we lose here in this life and in the time to come are lost or diminished, regardless of how tearfully we may regret it when our flesh dies. It's a grave warning.

We know, having hindsight what a fool Esau, now Edom was. Yet how many times do we do the same, for much less than even a bowl of lentils?

teachings.title: How to become a vessel meet for the master
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: We sanctify ourselves by fleeing youthful lusts, following righteousness, avoiding foolish questions, and gently teaching those in error so they may come to the truth.
teachings.text:
And how does one sanctify themselves? How can we as believers be more than a wooden or clay pot, but become tools for God's glory?

*Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.*

*But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.*

*And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;*
*And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will*.

We study His word. We know the answers to good questions that we may give meek and ready reason for the hope we have. Being patient. Charitable, loving people with the same grace shown us by God. Not striving, or argumentive, but gentle that those who are in sin come to the truth, and be saved.

This is the meat of the word. It is next level stuff, not easily obtained, but that we must seek to be further transformed for the master's use. Praying for the wisdom and faith to grow in discipleship. Letting go of the cares of this world, that we may live in honor and glory in the next.

teachings.title: The whole armour of God
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Honouring parents and working faithfully is possible because we are equipped with the whole armour of God, so walking in truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation and the word we need not fear the wicked.
teachings.text:
And so we honor our parents, the first commandment with a promise from God, that in doing so we are blessed. We work diligently and with all humility and fear, because we work for God. And we are to remain humble and honest in our dealings, if we are bond or free.

We can do this if we remember we are outfitted with the whole armor of God.

*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

Girding our loins with truth, the breastplate of righteousness, your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, *wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked,* the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit *which is the word of God.*

We are equipped with these things, when we walk in them. And if we walk in them, we should have no fear of the wicked.

We are prepared with truth, not dissimulation, protected from blame by being righteous, prepared to give good answer for our hope everywhere we go, with the good news of God's peace with man in Christ Jesus. Our faith a shield against all attacks, no matter how fiery. Protected with the sure knowledge and confidence of our salvation. And armed with the sword of the Spirit, the word of God, which is quick and powerful, *sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

For, *If God be for us, who can be against us?*

teachings.title: The whole law is love
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: The whole law is loving our neighbour, even our enemy, as Christ did, which none of us can do perfectly, but staying in the word and prayer brings forth the fruit of the Spirit in our walk.
teachings.text:
And what is the whole of the law? Paul again, echoing Christ who quoted Leviticus; Loving our neighbors as ourselves. In all things. And as Jesus taught in the parable of the Good Samaritan, your neighbors are those you meet along the way, even your enemies. And what does loving them look like? Sacrifice of time, material wealth, comfort, status, gain, health, even life to aid them in their need.

Can any of us love this much?

Jesus Christ, sinless and blameless sacrificed Himself, yet while we were sinners so that we may be forgiven. No greater love than this. A standard we strive for, to which we crucify ourselves daily to achieve. Our spirit willing, but the flesh is weak.

So how do we shore up the spirit to bring us closer to following Christ? By being in the word. In prayer. In thanksgiving to God for the gift of salvation. And it is reflected  and made manifest in our walk, through love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.

teachings.title: The examples of Israel and the way of escape
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Israel was delivered yet fell into idolatry and fornication and was chastened, as an example to us, and the way of escape God provides from every temptation is found by staying in His word.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his teaching to the Church at Corinth, and reminds them all that their forefathers were baptized unto Moses by the passing through the sea, and by the cloud that followed them as they wandered, the Rock that provided water, a symbol of Christ. And despite this, those saved out of Egypt were backslidden and committed wickedness, as all sin common to man tempts us all.

They committed idolatry and idleness, with the golden calf (**Exodus 32**). They were tempted by the daughters of Moab and led to slaughter by their fornication (**Numbers 25)**. They complained of the Mana and were struck down by the fiery serpents (**Numbers 21**). They murmured and complained against Moses' leadership, and the gainsaying of Koreh was met with instant death (**Numbers 16)**.

These Israelites were faithful to leave captivity, made free by that faith, baptized of a sort, led to the promised land by a cloud and a pillar of fire, fed from the corn of Heaven, they did eat angel's food, and were given the water from the Rock, that was like the living waters of Christ. They ate of the communion the meat, and drank the common drink, and yet they fell to fornication and idolatry, and God did punish them for it, just as believers who are backslidden and castaway are punished by God. *For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.* (**Hebrews 12**).

Paul says these examples are lessons given us by God to learn His ways. God will not allow us to be tempted beyond our ability to resist, but it is up to us to resist, by the path God provides us to escape each test and temptation.

That way of escape is found in our knowledge of the word. By how much time we spend in it. It's why Paul uses examples of scripture to reason with the Corinthians, it's why he reminds us of the lessons from God's word.

If you are facing sin, as thorns in your heart, and you want to be rid of it, or if you are engaging your lusts of the flesh or cares for the world, you will find relief and understanding from God, being in His word. It's the truth. The closer you get to Him the more clear your path becomes and the fewer snares and stumbling blocks there be.

teachings.title: Words are the window to the heart
teachings.summary: The righteous are vexed by the wicked words of the world, and as Jesus taught, what comes out of the mouth reveals and defiles the heart, so believers must watch what they say.
teachings.text:
David's plea for help, like many of the Psalms, comes from the vexation of spirit in dealing with the wicked of this world. That in a world where believers, Christians, are called to be separated and holy as He is holy, the fallen world full of the iniquity of man troubles us. It is the lot, no pun intended, of the believer.

**2 Peter 2:6–9**
