*And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished*

This is a feeling we can all relate to, if you walk in the Spirit.

The vexation is not just bearing witness to the unlawful deeds of the wicked, but in *hearing* them as well.

David says they speak vanity to each other, and flatter, and with a double-heart, speak lies. They pridefully boast. It is the wickedness of words that sees David cry out.

**Matthew 12:34–37**
*O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things. But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.*

Jesus shows us that words are the window to the heart of a man. An evil heart brings forth evil words, and it is those words that condemn them.

**Matthew 15:10–11**
*And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.*

This understanding, that it wasn't the ritual washings and dietary laws, cleaning the outside of the cup -but the heart, and what proceeds out from it though the mouth, that makes a man unclean, is often neglected by Christians, today. But one of the most repeated commands in scripture is to watch what you say.

Proverbs is full of advice to remain silent, to not speak like the fool or the froward. To speak truth in all things. To refrain from vain, useless speech.

But the wicked refuse to hear God's word and follow His way. Men *Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?*

Of course, by admitting they have power over their own tongue, they condemn themselves.

teachings.title: Taking a dog by the ears
teachings.summary: Meddling in others' fights, from church disputes to online drama, is folly, and likewise a godly nation should not join the enemies of Christ in their wars, as Jehoshaphat was rebuked for helping Ahab.
teachings.text:
The last section of **Proverbs 26** deals with strife, and those that cause it with their lying tongue.

*He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears*.

Getting involved in other people's fights, whether it's taking up a cause between two parties in your church, between neighbors, or total strangers, is a foolish thing to do. The warning here leans into the uncontrollable danger, likening it to a dog turning and rending you.

But it also applies to chatroom drama and Facebook fights. It happens online all the time, where the physical stakes are low, and the busybody tendencies are not inhibited by potential violence.

Stay out of contentions that don't involve you. If we are to bless our own enemies and turn the other cheek, then what business is it of ours to join in another's vengeance?

And, while it is blessed to be a peacemaker, it isn't arrived at by stepping in between brawlers or meddling in their strife.

Better to counsel with soft words to the parties separately, than join in as a third member of an ongoing fight. You really don't want to be the reason two warring factions unite out of spite to go after you for your meddling.

This should be applied in context to ruling a kingdom as well. When Jehosaphat, King of the Southern Kingdom of Judah joined the wicked Ahab of Israel in his war with Syria, we see in **2 Chronicles 19**; *Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.*

A godly nation should not join the enemies of Christ in war against their enemies. And Christians shouldn't cheer when their leaders yoke with unbelieving countries to make war.

If two nations of those who hate God choose to go to war, you can pray for God's will to be done, or that His judgement brings peace. You can be indifferent to the outcome, and leave it to God. But don't meddle in their strife, even by egging it on.

teachings.title: Wise in his own conceit
teachings.summary: The man wise in his own conceit has made his esoteric opinions his identity and cannot be moved by scripture, which is why we reject him and shake the dust.
teachings.text:
*Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.*

The fool, wise in their own conceit, is the "special boy." Convinced that they know something to be true, despite clear scripture and common reason, context and consistent application across the text, they are immovable from their opinions.

Their opinions are their own self-identity. They can no more consider they're wrong than deny their own name, because it would destroy the things that make up the very concept of who they are.

The more esoteric or counter to the plain reading, the better, because it allows them to feel superior to those that "just don't understand" their doctrine. They have carefully curated proof texts, and circular arguments and unfalsifiable theories.

Again, this is why we shake the dust, and are told to reject them.

teachings.title: Answer a fool according to his folly
teachings.summary: Proverbs 26:4-5 means we should not argue with a fool but rebuke him with scripture and then reject him, because a man wise in his own conceit is beyond hope.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 26** continues the collection of Solomon's sayings, prepared for King Hezekiah, the 12th generation descendant of the wisest man ever to live. These sayings return to the more rapid fire style of earlier chapters, and focus heavily on the warnings against fools, liars, sluggards and talebearers.

In order, vs 1 compares the honor given a fool to unseasonable weather. Snow in summer, rain at harvest. It should bother us as Christians when the foolish and froward get honor and praise by this world. We should see it as unseemly. It happens all too often, and vexes the heart.

Curses without cause shall not come, curse not at all. It's vanity, generally speaking. The cause rarely rises to the level of the curse, and if it did, God will repay. Better to bless, and give it up to the Lord.

The rod on the fools back serves the same purpose as a bridle, to direct the stubborn fool and keep him in line. Corporal punishment for foolish and malignant behavior is a good thing, and better at correction than jail, onerous fines and probation. Stripes serve a purpose, and it's cruelty that our society has abandoned this corrective in the name of progress.

Vs 4-5 bring a seeming contradiction;

*Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.*

The understanding here is that when a fool is arguing foolishness, debating their false premises, bickering back and forth makes you as much a fool, no matter how correct you are.

But to not answer a fool in his folly leaves him *wise in his own conceit*. The instruction then is to rebuke, not argue. To correct with authority (from scripture especially), and, as we've discussed, shake the dust. A **Titus 3:10** situation.

To be "wise in your own conceits" is to be dug in or convinced of your false or nonsensical beliefs. It could be some weird doctrine that they've heard and taken to heart, repeating it as fact. It could be the conclusion of their own ignorance applying twisted logic. It could be lies and rationalizations they use to deceive themselves.

It often is an identity they've adopted and the presuppositions and shibboleths that come with it, something we see in people taken in by special boy theology. They are constantly looking to provoke arguments and to get people into endless debates, that go no where.

Verse 12 explains precisely why; *Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.*

Whatever the conceit may be, the fools are entrenched in them. And so, *after the first and second admonition reject.* You've better hope convincing a fool of the truth than changing their mind.

Using a fool as a messenger is foolish. It will undermine and damage what you sought to accomplish.

teachings.title: Cast not your pearls before swine
teachings.summary: Fools despise wisdom, so whether online or soul winning door to door we should give our piece, reject the heretic after admonition, shake off the dust and not be trapped in debate.
teachings.text:
Next, we are told to not speak wisdom to the fool, for they despise it. They do not value wise words, or that which is holy;

**Matthew 7:6**
*Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.*

Jesus' words against giving the word of God to dogs and swine, the sodomites and the reprobate, is an escalation to the proverb. Just as we will see, arguing with fools and the wicked is vanity in later chapters. It is important to keep in mind, especially today with the Internet culture, where endless debate and the need to prove someone is "wrong on the Internet" can become a hazard. A snare I struggle with.

**Titus 3:10**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.*..

As Jesus instructs the Apostles, shake the dust. When we are out soul-winning, going door to door with the gospel, never get into arguments with the unreceptive or the mockers or blasphemers. You simply let them oppose themselves and move on.

Remembering that the foolish despise wisdom is a great way to train yourself to not be trapped in debate, but to say your piece and move on. Their own blood is on their own head. Wash your hands of it.

teachings.title: Reprove not a scorner; shake off the dust
teachings.summary: As Christ and Paul taught, we do not argue with scorners when giving the gospel but shake off the dust and move on, while instruction to the wise makes them wiser, each man bearing his own guilt.
teachings.text:
Solomon then gives this instruction; *Forsake the foolish, and live.* He says to not reprove a scorner, to not rebuke the wicked. This is echoed in the way Christ gave to His disciples when sending them out to the lost sheep of Israel;

**Mathew 10:14** *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet*.

As Paul instructs Titus;

**Titus 3:10** *A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject*

These men oppose themselves.

Peter writes that we should not argue with scoffers; *Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing*.

**1 Peter 3:16** *Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

When we are out in the hedges and highways, compelling all to come to the wisdom of God, by His gospel, we aren't there to argue. To debate. We are not supposed to waste our time with scoffers and mockers and scorners of the truth. We are supposed to shake the dust and move on.

But, if we give instruction to the wise, they will be wiser. Those seeking the truth will hear us. They will understand that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

And by His wisdom, our days are lengthened, our life increased.

It is on every man to bear this. To the wise, for themselves and to life; for the scorner, to themselves unto death.

This is individual soul liberty. We carry our own guilt and are responsible. But by faith we enter into His grace.

teachings.title: Strawmen and the Titus 3:10 rule
teachings.summary: Like Elihu putting words in Job's mouth, bad-faith debaters reframe what you said, so keep to what the Bible says and reject such a man after the first and second admonition.
teachings.text:
Elihu continues to accuse Job, and again, builds a strawman to do it. Job never uttered the words "My righteousness is more than God's" anywhere in the book.

Job repeatedly defends his own personal integrity and blamelessness before God, while fully acknowledging God's supreme righteousness and power.

**Job 9:2** *I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?*

In his statements, Job repeatedly recognizes no one can claim perfect righteousness with God. But Elihu puts words and intent into Job's mouth to attack him.

This is also a very common tactic online, especially with young theology bros. They learn the proof texts and apologetics for their presuppositions, and can only apply them to certain expected responses. They need the person they are "debating" to fall into the trap of defending the false representation of their own argument, so the special boy can pounce.

One reason this is so common is the prefab doctrines and canned arguments work against the unstable and unlearned. Good faith Christians take the bait, and so the argument is derailed into being about what the special boy needs it to be, so that his regurgitating is effective.

Which is why it is very important in these situations to know what the Bible says, and to keep the discussion focused on that. And to remember the **Titus 3:10** rule;

*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.*

The second they enter into putting words in your mouth, or reframing what you've said in a dishonest way, they are in bad faith and cannot be reasonable. "So you're saying...." only works if it is actually an honest assessment of what was being said. Otherwise, it is an insult.

teachings.title: Swear not at all: be doers of the word
teachings.summary: Judah's zeal-filled oath carried a burden God held them to, so it is better not to swear but simply do the word, since God respects faith rather than promises.
teachings.text:
Continuing the theme from yesterday's reading, we see that those who seek the Lord diligently are blessed. Even when the nation has gone the way of Baal, if they humble themselves and repent towards the Lord, He is faithful to forgive them.

Here all Judah takes an oath, and promises to serve the Lord with all their hearts. And the word of the Lord comes upon the prophet to encourage them to continue in it, because of they break the oath, the Lord will certainly forsake them. The Lord granted them peace all around.

But the oath made in their zeal also carries a burden, God holds them to their oath.

 *But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.*

Jesus said it is better to swear not at all. To just be doers of the word. Don't promise to seek God in all things, just do it. As we will see in the next chapter, it isn't the well intentioned promise that God respects, but faith.

teachings.title: Promises in zeal we cannot keep
teachings.summary: Judah's open-ended oath bred hypocrisy and Asa still left the high places, showing we should rely on God's mercy rather than make promises in the flesh we cannot keep.
teachings.text:
The promise to kill any who did not seek after the Lord the way the people swore to, was not from the Lord, but their own imagination.

While reprobates and sodomites in the land were driven out, and the law was kept for abominations, and idols destroyed, the open ended oath left a lot of room for hypocrisy.

Asa destroyed the images of his own mother, which was good, removing her as queen mother (a position that isn't respected in Biblical accounts, sorry Caths), he failed to remove all the high places. None of us are perfect and paths to be perfect will fail and prove us liars. Better to rely on God's mercy, than make promises in our excitement, that we in the flesh cannot keep.

teachings.title: Don't make a vow you cannot keep
teachings.summary: God will exact the price of any vow made in His name, so it is no sin to refuse to vow, and plain honesty with yea and nay is the better way.
teachings.text:
*When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee. But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.*

**Matthew 5:34-37**
*but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil*

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation*.

**Ecclesiastes 5:4-6**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?*

**Exodus 20:7**
*Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.*

People who "swear to God," who make promises to God they cannot keep, who make promises to others based on the righteousness of Christ, swearing on a Bible, and all other manner of ways to vow a vow, need to be careful. God is very clear that He will exact the price for your vow. So don't make one you cannot keep.

There is no sin in refusing to vow in His name. And as Christ tells us, being honest in all your dealings is a much better policy. Let your yea be yea and your no, no.

teachings.title: Should New Testament Christians take vows
teachings.summary: Christ and James command not to swear, so believers should live consecrated lives daily without vows, keeping an honest testimony as a witness for the gospel.
teachings.text:
But should we as New Testament Christians take vows?

**Matthew 5:33-37**
*Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.*

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.*

We are already called to live consecrated lives in service of the Lord. Separated unto the Gospel. And as such, are supposed to be dedicated to the purposes of God without vow, but as His.

And in doing so, we see that the more important thing is that our testimony be without question or ill repute. Blameless. Honest in our dealings that when we say to someone the reason for our hope, we are a good witness for the Gospel that they might be saved.

And while times of fasting or dedication to a specific task for God may be something we do for specific favor, or time offered in service for thanksgiving, we should live separated lives daily, with joy and thanksgiving.

**Psalms 61:8**
*So will I sing praise unto thy name for ever, that I may daily perform my vows.*

teachings.title: Swear not at all: let your yea be yea
teachings.summary: Believers have no need to make vows, because an honest man keeps his word with a plain yes or no, fulfilling the spirit of the law.
teachings.text:
As for vows and swearing to God before men, Jesus says in **Matthew 5**:
*33 Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:*

*34 But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne:*

*35 Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.*

*36 Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.*

*37 But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.*

We have no obligation to make vows, to give earnest, and to do these things before God. The law being a schoolmaster brings us to the truth that Jesus is conveying; that a just man doesn't need to prove by vow what his word is, because by being honest in all things, and keeping it to yes or no, and meaning it, we uphold the spirit of the law and its intention. Men will believe us or not. And our vows to these things, be it God, or your life or heaven or things of the earth, all are His and we have no real right to put them up for earnest.

teachings.title: Correct false teachers with love from scripture
teachings.summary: Instead of striving in debates, believers should meekly correct error from the misused scripture and pray for those zealous without knowledge, since faith comes by hearing the word.
teachings.text:
Now it's important to note a few lessons for us, when we interact with unsaved people offering up false doctrines and using out of context scripture as "proof text."

This is a lesson it took me a while to learn, because we are trained in this era of social media to engage in an argument, to prove our side and own the other side. To enter into striving and debates about the law, answering foolish questions and other things that the scripture explicitly tells us not to do. It often leads to wrath, and wrath to sin. It's why the Bible tells us not to do it.

And getting into a back and forth volley of proof text scriptures with someone who's unsaved is unprofitable and vain. Rather we should correct them with love from the scripture they're misusing, showing how it doesn't mean what they say it means using the word of God.

Keeping in mind they may be under a strong delusion, spiritual blindness which is a supernatural thing God does to some. It's why they can't see what you show them the contradicts their predetermined ideas.

Rather, like Paul says of the Jews, lamenting:

*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.*

*For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

Many of these people are well meaning and have a zeal for God, even if it's in ignorance. We should pray that God opens their eyes and brings them understanding from his word, knowing that *faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*
(Note, faith doesn't come from vain traditions of men but by His word, scripture. The Bible)

teachings.title: Meekness as strength against enemies
teachings.summary: Like Jesus silencing His tempters, believers should answer enemies with blamelessness and scripture rather than railing, letting their own hypocrisy expose them.
teachings.text:
Finally we see the murderous Jews attempting to tempt Jesus into saying something they may use to justify His death, and once again, Jesus silences them by their own hypocrisy.

This is the proper way to deal with such matters. Not reacting and railing, but trusting in God, being blameless and allowing their own internal contradictions and corruption to hamstring your enemies. Using scripture when needed. Forcing them to persecute you directly for His name's sake and for the word.

When we spiral in anger and get drawn into debate, all we do is give them the hook to hang us with. Instead, Jesus shows us how petty and foolish they are, exposing them.

This lesson in meekness as strength is often lost by believers. It's good to be constantly reminded of throughout the Gospels.

teachings.title: Reject a heretic after two admonitions
teachings.summary: Strivings about the law and genealogies are vain, so after a heretic is shown scripture twice we should reject him rather than argue from pride.
teachings.text:
And, once again, God repeats for emphasis that we should avoid foolish questions, Jewish fables, endless genealogies, and strivings about the law; *for they are unprofitable and vain*.

Debates and silly theological questions and talmudic arguments about the law help no one. They can lead to heresy and blasphemy. They can be a snare and a stumbling block to those seeking truth. Be determined to know nothing but Christ and Him crucified.

As far as those who endlessly strive about these things? They are heretics.

*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.*

If you've shown them clear scripture, two times, and they still insist they are right, then shake the dust. It's not worth it to answer a fool in his folly. It's why I have the pinned rules in my chat. Sincerely asked questions, met with polite consideration when answered is one thing, but demands to go back and forth with their natural man idea of scripture is vanity. Useless. Helping no one, and may give you cause to sin and them to accuse.

*Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself* be satisfied, instead of having to prove them wrong. That's your pride, and it helps no one. (I have fallen in to this trap. It's so tempting)

Grace be with you all. Amen.

teachings.title: Avoid vain babblings and science falsely so called
teachings.summary: The rich are to give freely, and believers entrusted with the gospel should avoid vain disputations with scorners and heretics, which are a bad witness.
teachings.text:
Finishing up, Paul advises that Timothy lay charge to those who are converted to the faith and already rich in wealth to be ready to hand it out to those in need. To do good works with that they've been blessed. To despise their riches here and store up rewards for Heaven.

As Jesus told His disciples, it is harder for a rich man to enter the Kingdom than for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle. And because to whom much is given, much more is expected, they should be encouraged to do as much as possible for the brethren, edifying the church and giving glory to God.

Finally, Paul warns young Timothy, his son in Christ, a ward of the Gospel, to

*Keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith.*

We are entrusted with the Gospel of reconciliation. The doctrines of how to live, discipleship, prudence, fidelity to God's law and hope in His promise. To preach and to teach this to every creature. Saving who we can, by mercy or by warning of the fire.

We should give good witness to this faith that we have been entrusted, the surety of which is our now quickened spirit, and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit inside us. A ready and meek answer for our hope to all who we give witness.

We are to avoid the vain, that is unprofitable babblings of those seeking to debate us, to engender strife and disputations of the faith. Not to give answer to fools. Not to get into arguments with gnostics, and their science, falsely so-called. This includes debating atheists on creation, for example. We are warned repeatedly against answering a fool in their folly.

**Proverbs 9**

*7 He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked man getteth himself a blot.*

*8 Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.*

*9 Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.*

It is a bad witness to get caught up in disputations with a heretic. (Of this, I am chief)

**Titus 3:10-11**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.*

(This is primarily the reason for my pinned rules for the channel. To keep myself from sinning, being drawn into debates with fools. It's also why Twitter is such a snare.)

teachings.title: What corrupt communication means
teachings.summary: Corrupt communication in Ephesians 4 means speech in wrath, envy, backbiting and false accusation, not merely vulgar words, and legalists who fuss over a stray word while backbiting have it backwards.
teachings.text:
Some take the admonition against corrupt communication to be simply not to use vulgarity, lewdness or potty talk, but while all those things *can be* the type of corrupt communication Paul's writing about, it isn't what he means. In this context, he's regarding the things we say in wrath and anger, envy, strife, backbiting, tale bearing, railing, false accusations, etc.

Not the words used, as if a naughty word has power to corrupt, but the means and meaning of what's being said.

Is it edifying? Does it leave you blameless to share the good news without embarrassment or hypocrisy?

That's the meaning, and while a cuss word can be something that can be corrupting in this context, it isn't always and discernment should be given. Jesus wasn't using corrupt communication when he said "Raca." When scripture says "ass," or "pisseth."  When Song of Solomon gets a little spicy.

Overly legalistic types lose their mind at a stray vulgarity while accepting hypocrisy, backbiting and railing, being holier than thou.

teachings.title: Yielding to rulers, the example of Mordecai
teachings.summary: A little folly ruins a wise man's name, and it is better to yield to a ruler than flee or fight, as Christ, the apostles and David did, while Mordecai's refusal to bow brought slaughter.
teachings.text:
Chapter 10 sees a familiar format, where the wise Preacher goes down some rabbit-trails with proverbs. We've obviously seen some scattered throughout the book, and so it isn't surprising. Holy men moved by the Spirit gave utterance to truth, because the word of God *is* truth.

Vs 1, continues from the final verse of **Ecclesiastes 9:18**, that wisdom is better than weapons, but one sinner destroys much good. Here, Solomon compares how one dead fly ruins a sweet savoy ointment, the same as a little folly ruins a wise man's reputation.

Recall **Ecclesiastes 7:1** *A good name is better than precious ointment.*..

It is difficult to build a good reputation, it takes time, understanding; walking in the fear of the Lord. And it can all be thrown away by one act of sin. Think of all the great preachers brought low by their sin. (And as children of God, when we sin in secret without repentance, one of the ways God will chasten you is to make sure your sin is found out)

David, a man after God's own heart, sinned greatly in secret, but Nathan reminded him that the Lord knew, and so David suffered for his sin.

We always talk about Solomon's wisdom, but temper it with the understanding that he was backslidden and allowed his strange wives to worship false gods. Of course He knew better and believed the truth, but he succumbed to the same temptation as Adam. Pleasing the wife, rather than God.

It is a sobering reminder that our heart is in our hands. Wise man's heart is in his right, but the fool's is in treachery, in his left. And a wise man can become a fool in a single act.

And when a fool walks in his way, his folly will always reveal itself to others. In deed or in word, it becomes obvious that they are fools.

Vs 4, he transitions to a Biblical truth, that if a ruler comes against you, justly or unjustly, it is better to yield than to flee or fight. We see it time and again, the greatest example being Jesus of course. But the apostles who willingly went to judgment to further the cause of Christ, even in death. We see it in the Old Testament where Jeremiah warns the people of Judah to stay put and trust the Lord. Those that fled to Egypt were slain in the way. Those that rebelled were put down. We see the example of Daniel and his friends, Joseph in Egypt,

David while being pursued by Saul, had opportunity to kill the king, and refused and continued to appeal to his reason.

Vs5-7 Solomon recalls an evil he has witnessed where rulers give honor to fools, and treat servants as princes. While we are not to be respecters of persons, we shouldn't give dignity to full of foolishness or rebellion.

Tying vs 4 with 5-7, I can't help but think of Mordecai from the book of **Esther**. Where rather than yield to the king's prince, Haman, he continued to disrespect him...even as the plot to kill the Jews was known to him.

Jesus says in **Matthew 5:25**
*Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.*

We are to give honor and tribute to whom it is due. The entire affair that led to the slaughter of 75,000 people could have been avoided by simply and meekly apologizing, and bowing.

And the King put Mordecai on a horse, and rewarded him, despite his unwillingness to yield to authority. Haman reacted with evil, but there are no good guys in the story.

Vs 8 and 9 reflect the understanding that we saw in **Proverbs**; that treachery and iniquity will come back to bite you. It echoes the proverbs against moving landmarks, or setting traps for others, that God's justice will see to it that you will receive the recompense for the evil you do to others.

He then compares wisdom to the sharpening of a blade, noting the dull blade makes work harder. Wisdom sharpens, making work easier. And we can make each other wiser, sharper, with advice and counsel.

**Proverbs 27:17**
*Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.*

Of course the sharpest sword is the word of God.

teachings.title: Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men
teachings.summary: Rehoboam sought a multitude of counsel but followed the young men over the old men who served Solomon, and lost the kingdom for lack of the wisdom his father wrote.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Proverbs 24**, we seek the knowledge that is a treasure, given freely by God, and we seek the strength that increased knowledge brings.

We should seek wise counsel in war, and the safety of a multitude of councillors. It isn't wise to leave things to a committee, but rather, as a leader, seek options and opinions from other wise men.

Ironically, for Solomon's son, Rehoboam *when he went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king*, Jeroboam the son of Nebat, exiled to Egypt, returns to challenge his anointing.

**1 Kings 12:3-6**
*That they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying, Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee. And he said unto them, Depart yet for three days, then come again to me. And the people departed. And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?*

He wisely sought counsel in this crisis. He hears out the old men, the hoary heads who the wisest man ever to live relied on. The very men Solomon was referencing throughout Proverbs. However, the young king sought others, a multitude of counsel, but lacked the discernment to ignore what his untrustworthy heart told him seemed right, and listen to the older men. Verse 8;

*But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, and which stood before him.*

Had he kept all the wisdom of his father, applying all the sayings he received, the splitting of the kingdom may have been avoided.

Jeroboam devised evil. He was a mischievous person. He was a scorner, leading false (or exaggerated) charges against the deceased king, winning the fools with lies in an evil cause. And so Rehoboam fainted in the day of adversity. His strength was small. And a kingdom was lost, along with the sealing the ultimate end of the northern 10 tribes.

teachings.title: The hoary head is a crown of glory
teachings.summary: Honouring the old man is both wise and a command of God, since long life usually brings the fear of the Lord, knowledge and good counsel.
teachings.text:
Again, Solomon gives lessons on the sluggard, less a warning here, and more an observation of their ways.

The lazy will complain it's too cold to plow in the spring, but then beg in the harvest as winter begins.

Then he advises his son to not love sleep, because that leads to poverty. A diligent man, who opens his eyes and works, he will be satisfied.

He warns of spending an inheritance foolishly, with haste. The blessing of it wasted too soon.

He reminds us to honor the old man, that while the glory of the young may be their strength, the beauty of the old, his gray hair. The hoary head is a crown of glory. For a man to live long on this earth and to prosper, they will likely have gained a healthy fear of the Lord, acquiring knowledge, having a soft answer, just measures, love of wisdom, learning from reproof. Not given to wine or strong drink. Full of good counsel. Respect your elders, in other words. It is not only wise to give honor to elders, but it is a command of God.

**Leviticus 19:32**
*Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the Lord.*

teachings.title: Don't act like you invented the doctrine
teachings.summary: Elihu repeats obvious truths while boasting of his wisdom, and Christians should pass on even basic knowledge with humility, since it is of the Lord.
teachings.text:
The young man, Elihu, continues on his monologue, accusing Job of being unrighteous, unwise and wicked.

Repeating many of the charges leveled against Job by the three friends, while proclaiming his own wisdom, Elihu's understanding is shallow and, as the reader knows, untrue.

There are some valid points made about God not being a respecter of persons, holding the kings and the common man to the same fate of death and judgment. All the accusers of Job have said some right things. What makes Elihu's portion so obnoxious is that he is regurgitating obvious points, while proclaiming his own wisdom in knowing them. A lack of humility Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar maintained.

Again, for Christians, this is an example of what not to do. Even if you have knowledge, it is of the Lord. The more basic and obvious, the more humility you should have in passing it on. Assuming that commonly held wisdom is already understood by those you are dealing with. Not pontificating and acting like you invented the doctrine. That your ability to recite dogmas makes you an intellectual, rather than a parrot.

Elihu haranguing Job, says that he hopes Job suffers even more than he has, that he not only deserves it, but more that Job is in rebellion against God for even questioning why this happened.

The misapplication of wisdom, the lack of maturity and grace, the presumption and pride, these traits make many young people look foolish in the eyes of their elders.

teachings.title: Do not be as Elihu
teachings.summary: Elihu is a picture of the pride of youth with false humility, and young men and babes in Christ who rush to give their opinions to their elders should learn real humility from him.
teachings.text:
An angry young man has entered the conversation, Elihu. And the Bible tells us his wrath was kindled 4 times. The young man is angry at Job, the thinking the poor man suffering before him had justified himself, rather than God. He is angry at Job's friends, who accused Job but didn't answer him when he defended himself.

He says "I am young, and you are *very* old." Starting off with a false humility, claiming to respect his elders, that he held off from giving his opinion until they were done, but now he must share his opinions.

He was chomping at the bit to tell his elders off, who are very old (not just older).

Elihu is rash, while counting himself reserved. He is rude, while claiming to be patient and respectful. He is a picture of impertinent youth.

Four times we are told Elihu is angry, and three times he tells the men that he is going to give his opinion. An opinion no one asked for.

Young men, do not be as Elihu. He waited on the elders, it's true, but not out of respect or seeking after wisdom, but to bide his time so he could give his opinion. He is a special boy.

He wants Job to know, God thrust him down. He wants the friends (who didn't hesitate to accuse Job), to know they are weak and afraid to say it. To condemn Job utterly.

He describes his need to unload his opinion as wine fermented in a sealed cask, the gases exploding the seams.
*For I am full of the matter.* He cannot wait to tell them what he thinks.

He rationalizes and spiritualizes his rashness, by saying he won't give flattering titles to them, won't show them respect they are due, because his maker, the Lord, wouldn't like it. Convenient!

The pride and arrogance of youth is what he is actually filled with. How often do we see this in chatrooms and even in churches?

Young men with no experience, babes in Christ, convinced they know more than their elders. Who can't wait to tell them their opinions, because the older people just don't get it, in their eyes.

As we will see, Elihu actually offers little to the conversation. It really is just his pride.

If you are like Elihu, if you jump in to give your opinion thinking your newfound wisdom and knowledge, repeating things you recently heard, thinking you are blowing minds, stop. Consider him, and this lesson. You aren't a special boy, and you have limited understanding. Have real humility, not the fake kind Elihu shows here.

teachings.title: Young men, honour the hoary head
teachings.summary: Young people mocked Job in his calamity, but young Christian men should honour and learn from their elders, knowing the troubles of age will come on all.
teachings.text:
Having established that he was respected and honored for his ways, Job says he is now the byword, the laughing stock of the young men. Not only young men, but the worst of them. The sons of base men, those that are outcasts from society. The worst people.

All from the calamity allowed by God.

If Job's own friends aren't willing to show him grace in his predicament, strangers certainly won't. And the pride of youth, likely full of resentments against him, glory in Job's downfall.

Young people should show more honor for the elders, and respect for the hoary head should include understanding that bad things that come with age will fall on all of us, God willing. That death will come, but before that many ailments, disabilities, embarrassing conditions, circumstances that just are unavoidable.

Youth often comes with lack of understanding, a lack of awareness and a back-of-the-mind fear of it happening to them, that combined makes them very unsympathetic to the old.

Young Christian men especially should seek to learn from their elders, not mock them.

teachings.title: Gravity before office, not after
teachings.summary: Deacons and respected men must already be grave and sober before they are named, so young Christian men should put away the world's arrested development and seek sobriety, humble service and kindness.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 3:8-13**
*Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless. Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus*

Many men in Christ today say, "well I am not a pastor. I don't have to do much, I can coast on helping with chairs after the service. The deacons and elders at the church have always been there. They do the heavy lifting."

Respected men of faith in the church don't put on this gravity like a coat when they get named. It isn't a longevity award. You must be these things before you are ever even considered for leadership. And it should be your guide and goal as a young man.

The world has made arrested development into a virtue. Being unserious as a way to comport yourself. This retards the growth of a Christian man.

We see it in ourselves, certainly. An immaturity that must be tamed and brought under control. It's fine to joke and laugh, but in its place. Sobriety and gravity are what we should strive for, coupled with grace and mercy for those who have no one to deliver them.

With kindness as the goal. Not lordship.

Like Job, respect that comes from putting on God's righteousness and judgment. From living out your faith. You gain respect and influence by being a doer of the word, by being a humble servant. Not a prideful boaster.

In chapter 32 we will meet a young man, Elihu, who we will see is offended by Job's defense, and seeks to have respect given him, the wrong way. But for now we should reflect on Job's example, and the application for our own lives.

teachings.title: Older men, mentor the young men
teachings.summary: Middle-aged Christian men, even those who think past sin has disqualified them from office, should accept God's forgiveness and be an example to the young men in their church.
teachings.text:
If you are a Christian man in your middle age, and aren't contributing to the mentioning of young men in your life, especially your church, give an honest assessment between you and God as to why that is, and make a commitment to be.

Some men, especially who grew up outside of the faith or backslidden and making disqualifying mistakes, don't see the point of stepping up. Many are divorced, or engaging in some kind of sin that they are ashamed of. They think they are a broken vessel, that cannot be used by God.

You might never be named a deacon or a church officer. You might not hold a title or be given some kind of imprimatur, but your quiet strength and aged wisdom can still be used mightily by God. Humbly accept the grace God has given you, know you are forgiven and seek to be used in whatever capacity God has planned for you, anyway.

We all have a talent to edify. Submit yourself to those with authority, and stand as an example to the young men around you.

teachings.title: Mordecai's pride and rebellion
teachings.summary: Mordecai's refusal to bow to Haman was proud rebellion against authority God told the captives to submit to, like Saul's stubbornness.
teachings.text:
**Esther 3**, set after her marriage to the king, shows Haman that Agagite advanced over the other princes, to be second in the kingdom. The king commands that he be bowed to and revered for his position. Given tribute and honor as due.

God commands the same for us. We are supposed to submit to the authority He places in our lives, so long as the authority doesn't ask us to violate the higher power.

Bowing to the King and his chosen was custom. The servants and guards and others at the King's gate obeyed.

Mordecai did not.

The servants at the gate ask Mordecai the Jew, *Why transgressest thou the king's commandment?*

He doesn't answer.

*And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.*

Now Haman was an Agagite, a great grandson of Agag.

Agag was the king of the Amalekites when Saul as king of Israel was commanded by Samuel on behalf of the Lord to slaughter the Amalekites. Saul spared the king, and when he doesn't obey God, the Lord comes to Samuel saying He repented of choosing Saul, who did not honor His word and obey. And so the kingdom would be taken from him.

Saul, in this story, is a picture of the Jews, how they waxed worse and worse in disobedience, and so had the Kingdom taken from them.

Samuel himself executes Agag. But first he preaches against Saul;

**1 Samuel 15:22-23**
*And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.*

It is interesting that a Amalekite was placed in this position, and a Jew rebels against his authority.

The Jews in captivity were told to get along with the powers it be. Repeated warnings like this;

**Jeremiah 29:4-7**
*Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon; Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished. And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.*

Mordecai's plot to elevate his cousin Esther to be queen was successful, and his decision to then stalk the king's gate, paid off in the assassination plot he revealed to Esther, securing her the throne through deception.

And so his rebellion against the king seems borne of arrogance and pride. Stubborn. Rebellious as Saul's rebellion against God.

teachings.title: Daniel's meek appeal to authority
teachings.summary: Daniel shows how to honour authority without compromising faith, against today's rebellion that is as the sin of witchcraft.
teachings.text:
The captivity of Judah, long prophesied, begins. And the Lord gave Jerusalem and her king to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. And with it much of the vessels of Solomon's temple, brought to Shinar, and the house of Nebuchadnezzar's god. This will be important later, after the captivity ends under Cyrus of the Persians.

And among the captives, those of David's lineage, of Judah, were brought into the service of the king as eunuchs. In hopes the highborn would have better intellect and ability to learn the Babylonian tongue, Chaldean, as well as its learning and ways, to better serve the king.

We meet *Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah*, and they are given Chaldean names; *Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abednego*.

(I still call the three Rack, Shack and Benny. Old habits die hard)

In a show of magnanimity, the king allows the eunuchs to eat of his meat and drink, the food apparently offered to his god. With the intent that they grow to be nourished enough to stand before the king and serve him.

But Daniel asks the prince of the eunuchs, his overseer, if rather than defile themselves with the meat and drink offered to idols, if he and the three others may eat pulse, that is lentils.

Daniel, meek and faithful, doesn't rebel against the authority in his life, and yet doesn't compromise his faith and love of God. He instead asks permission.

When the prince of the eunuchs explains that it would get him in trouble if they seem to be less healthy than those who ate the king's portion, Daniel offers him a compromise; feed them 10 days and try them. If they aren't any worse for it, then honor this request.

Many people today hate the idea of submitting to authority. They want to riot in the daytime, and seek to use their faith to justify their rebellion.

They say they won't pay taxes, despite Jesus saying to render unto Caesar. Despite clear commands to render duty and honor and tribute to those set above us by God. Men refusing to submit to any authority. Refusing to join a church and submit themselves to a pastor. Who slack off at work, and constantly disrespecting their bosses.

This encourages the feminism that tells wives to rebel against husbands, and children against parents. Ultimately, it is rebellion against God.

The Bible says  *For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry*.

But what if authority over you asks you to do something that would offend God? Daniel shows us how it is done.

Meekly asking to be tried, the overseer agrees and after 10 days the four are healthier looking than all the other eunuchs. Daniel honored the authority in his life and pleased God. An example for us to follow.

teachings.title: Learning to serve that we may rule
teachings.summary: As heirs we learn to rule by serving, obeying parents, husbands loving and wives submitting, and obeying even wicked rulers while keeping God's word as final authority.
teachings.text:
And so, knowing we are sons, heirs, princes to a Kingdom, a better country which we seek, seek it diligently. And if under tutors and governors, schoolmasters until the day appointed, then we are to learn to better serve when appointed in that day.

And we learn patience. We learn right judgment. We learn the law and the will of God that we may better serve those entrusted to us in the Kingdom, by serving those we are given in this world.

We serve God. With our whole heart, soul and mind, we are to love Him. And if we love Him, obey His commandments.

As children, we are given to obey our parents. Commanded so, but with promise that we will live long upon the earth if we do. Honoring them, not just with obedience but in caring for them when they are old. Supporting them in their end years. Paying honor.

God doesn't say "if the parent is good." He doesn't say if they are believers, it is then saved or unsaved.

We are told to love our neighbors as ourselves. The whole of the law and commandments is fulfilled in this. How? In service. With hospitality. Grace and charity. Putting their profit above our own. We learn to minister that we may rule justly. We are to be holy because He is holy. And how can he trust us with much when we squandered the talents we were given?

How can we rule others, when we are rebellious and wicked?

We become husbands, and expect wives to submit, as they should, but men are to submit to God, and love their wife as Christ loved us, who did so unto death.

When men don't submit themselves to God, when they don't love their wives as if they were their own flesh (which they are, joined together by God), then wives no longer submit.

Wives are to submit to the husband, and when they don't, their children see and learn to rebel. They no longer honor their parents.

When a nation has rebellious and seditious men, unfaithful women, unruly children, then they are punished by God.

And God uses the ministers of government to hand out His punishment, that the nation either repents, or is destroyed.

And while the unregenerate people that make up the majority of the nation may wax worse and worse, we who are a light unto the world, are told to obey the higher powers. To seek to find ways to please even wicked kings, but always keeping the word of God as our final authority. And by doing so we may be punished. We may be persecuted. We may be thrown into a fiery furnace. Or a lion's den.

We may be like the son of Israel, Joseph, sold into captivity and then thrown in prison for being faithful when tempted by the Pharaoh's wife. But these things are done so that the glory of God may be revealed, and more are drawn to the truth. And to the Lord goes the increase.

As the prophets were slain. As the Apostles were martyred. As Christ Himself died that the glory of God could be revealed.

And so we obey God. We love our wives. Our wives submitting, teach our children. Our children in honoring us learn to fear God. Fearing God and in faith they do great things. And if the evil spirits that rule this world, the principalities that we wrest with, not of flesh and blood, but spiritual, if they seek our lives for it, then rejoice. It will be to the glory of God, and our rewards will be greater than we can convince of.

teachings.title: The spirit of rebellion
teachings.summary: Rebellion against God-ordained hierarchy is Satan's spirit, yet we never obey a command to sin, and like Paul and Silas our obedient behaviour can win our persecutors.
teachings.text:
"But I don't like it. I don't like being told what to do. I am obviously better, morally, intellectually, in every way, than my parents, than my boss, than my rulers."

The same spirit of rebellion that Satan loosed into the world.

God created earthly hierarchies for His purpose. To shape the clay as the potter sees fit. To make vessels fitted for destruction and fitted for honor. Who is the clay to question it?

Now if your father tells you to lie, or steal. Or to dishonor God, worship idols, to kill. If he tells you to disobey a higher authority, we have no obligation to.

Like Daniel, we do have an obligation to show them an alternative way. God's way.

*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

And so, with every authority. There's never an occasion to partake in another man's sin. There is always a way out, even if that way is to sacrifice yourself that another may not sin, or that those who witness understand the right path, and may be converted by your conversation; which is in the Bible, our behavior.

*Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear*.

Paul and Silas, in Philippi, offended the Jews and were brought before magistrates, given stripes being scourged, and thrown into prison for the Gospel.

*And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.*

And, in their chaste conversation, in their behavior that showed their faith, when an earthquake came and tare down the walls of the prison, they remained, obedient to the charge.

And the Philippian Jailer, scared not only for his life had they escaped, but afraid of the God they held their faith in, brought them out, and said, *Sirs, what must I do to be saved?*

*And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.*

They even remained in prison that the magistrates who had ordered them released in private, would have to come to release them publicly, to the magistrates' shame.

And the church of the Philippians was born and grew, and did mighty things for God, because of the obedience of Paul and Silas. To God and to government, even the government that unjustly persecuted them.

teachings.title: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's
teachings.summary: God uses the persecution of believers to convert even rulers, so paying taxes and suffering wrong is a trifle next to eternal treasure.
teachings.text:
And this is a pattern we see, God using the persecution of believers, even of Christ, to give the increase. God uses the weak things of this world to confound the strong. And in doing so, they are often converted.

Nebuchadnezzar believed, and repented of the evil He would do. Kings came around to free all Judah from captivity.

Publicans, centurions, even some Pharisees, all men with power and authority came to believe, and in doing so were given the same spirit we are. To be good ministers, to rightly judge.

Paul, despite his being able to be released when arrested in Jerusalem, rather went to Rome in chains that he may minister the Gospel to the house of Caesar.

This world isn't ours and the things of it are at best wood, hay and stubble, but the treasure we seek is of Heaven and incorruptible. Things of eternal value.

And when we look at the eternal, this mortal life is given perspective. And rendering to Caesar what is Caesar's is a trifling thing. Paying custom and tribute; taxes, is nothing. God provided us what we have and will again. Even from the mouth of a fish.

And if we are defrauded, Jesus says to not only let it go, but offer more. They take your coat, give them your cloak also. If they force you to walk a mile, go two. If they strike you, give them your other cheek that they may see what they are doing for what it is, and make the decision in your defiance to either strike again, or in shame back down. And perhaps by your chaste conversation be converted. By your stripes they may be healed.

teachings.title: Created for His pleasure
teachings.summary: As Christ, equal with God, submitted to the Father and was exalted, we must submit to God's will and to earthly order for His pleasure.
teachings.text:
The glory and Majesty of the Lord God, by Whom all things were made for His pleasure, and before whom we are not worthy. Who in His magnificent power and wisdom, is perfect and holy.

And it is this same God, to whom only the hinder parts could be seen by mortal eyes, Who when He passed Moses could not bear to witness, and the flow of Moses face from being in His presence made the children of Israel turn away in shame. God who is worthy of praise and service. Serving with fear and trembling at His perfect will set before us in His word. So much so, our submission unto earthly hierarchy is done in submission to Him that set all things in the heavens and upon the earth, to please Him.

As Christ, who thought it not blasphemy to declare Himself equal to God, submitted Himself to the will of the Father. So we must submit ourselves to doing what we are created for; giving pleasure to God.

For Jesus is the equal of God, but submitted unto God, and there by was given glory and is exalted above everything:

**Philippians 2:6-11**
Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

**John 6:38-40**
 *For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

teachings.title: Doing the will of God from the heart
teachings.summary: All submission, of husbands, wives, children, servants and citizens, is ultimately submission to Christ, as Christ submitted to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 6:6-9**
*Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free. And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him.*

Submission to God is to do His will. His will is knowable in His word, and through His Spirit. In all things giving glory to God, knowing He is holy, and true. That we are created to give Him pleasure in all that we do. To honor Him as He is honored in Heaven.

Hallowed be His name.

For who are we? Where we there when He placed the stars in the heavens and made the leviathan? When the lightning was formed and the thunder of His wrath was made?

God, appearing in a whirlwind to Job asks similar questions of righteous Job. He asks these things of the created who is questioning his Creator.

And Job, having been subject to this glory of God and His Majesty, replies;

**Job 42:1-6**
*Then Job answered the Lord, and said, I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee. Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not. Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.*

Husbands submit to Christ. Pastors submit to Christ. Wives submitting to husbands are submitting to Christ. Children honoring parents are submitting to Christ. Servants working diligently are submitting to Christ. Masters, or bosses, who rule justly are submitting to Christ, members of a nation submitting to authority do so, as they are serving Christ.

And in all things Christ submitted to God the Father, that He may be given the world as His footstool, and exalted above all of creation.

teachings.title: Honour to whom honour is due
teachings.summary: We are to honour unsaved parents, husbands and rulers and live peaceably with all men by faith, without joining in their sin, rather than rebelling out of fear.
teachings.text:
It is also worth mentioning that God can use unsaved people, people who are wrong on doctrine but in position of authority, to do His will.

Jethro as Moses' father-in-law was to be honored. His advice, considered and heeded. We sometimes see brothers and sisters in Christ struggle with that, where their parents are unsaved, sometimes wicked. Occasionally reprobate. And how does one honor them and honor God?

The same question comes up with husbands with wives who won't submit to Christ or to their husbands, godly wives with unsaved husbands who treat them poorly, and other hierarchical conflicts, such as submitting to government when it is wicked.

God's word is clear and consistent. That we are to as much as possible live peaceably with all men. To submit to the higher authority with meekness and faith, always keeping God as the head, that we don't cater to evil ourselves or join in another man's sin.

People hate to hear that. They want to rebel constantly and be in open defiance of the order of things in this world. Only refusing to budge on the clear fundamental teachings of God, but also giving honor to whom honor is due, and paying tribute to whom tribute is due, and trusting God in all.

*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.*

*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

People are afraid to live by faith. Fear is the opposite of faith. It kills faith. It undermines and leads people to sin, rather than trusting in God to deliver us.

Like the Israelites in the wilderness, people forget what God has already done for us, and so we are easily led to sin, fear and wrath.

But if we walk in the Spirit, continuing in prayer and studying the word to be approved by God, faith grows, and with that faith, judgment and discernment which all work together to keep us from being afraid and reactionary.

*And the just shall live by faith.*

teachings.title: The Lord met him and sought to kill him
teachings.summary: Moses' uncircumcised son shows that letting unsaved or carnal family hold us back from God's will makes us lukewarm and brings God's chastening.
teachings.text:
*And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the Lord met him, and sought to kill him.*

That escalated quickly!

Moses sought to return to Egypt to lead the people out of captivity with the word of God that they may believe and signs and wonders that they may know, but his own son he had not brought into the covenant of Abraham.

Zipporah cuts the foreskin off their son and casts it at Moses' feet. Angry that she had to tend to this bloody business, maybe even angry that she was being uprooted to go with him back to Egypt. Maybe their son wasn't circumcised because she opposed it, and backslidden Moses went along to avoid this kind of confrontation with his wife.

That's the application I take from it, the final excuse many of us have against doing God's will for us is the anger and confrontation we will have with loved ones. The division of family Jesus warned about in the gospels. But it is clear Zipporah isn't happy about any of it.

We may be similarly hindered in our Christian walk by loved ones and relatives who aren't where we are spiritually. Who may be unsaved or have the cares of the world in their hearts. Who put the carnality of life before serving God. And at some point, God will seek our lives for being castaway, for putting their objections over God's will. For our being half in and half out. Lukewarm.

teachings.title: Live blamelessly; be persecuted for His name
teachings.summary: Unlike partisan cries of hypocrisy, Jesus lived blamelessly so He was persecuted only for righteousness, and we must avoid sinful rage so that persecution glorifies God.
teachings.text:
One mistake many make in politics, especially among conservatives but it is widespread, is the constant screaming of "hypocrisy!" against opponents. But it is done in hypocritical manner for cheap partisan gain. It isn't sincere. And it just becomes an impotent exercise in "They are the real [bad thing they accuse us of]!"

Because both "sides" are hypocrites, they cannot effectively use the other's hypocrisy, and it just becomes empty gestures. If anything, reinforcing the hypocrisy of each side, justified by the hypocrisy of the other.

But Jesus' intentions are pure. He is doing the will of the Father. And while, yes He is blameless in a way none of us are, His example is ours to follow.

We as Christians are commanded in scripture to live blamelessly, to as much as possible live in peace with all men. To render unto Caesar. To give custom and tribute and honor to those in position to receive it, knowing we are heirs to a better country, an eternal kingdom.

Jesus showed the way, giving them nothing to accuse Him with, so that, in the end, it was His righteousness that they persecuted Him for. That it was their own wickedness that brought Him to the cross.

In a like manner we should strive to live in a way that is blameless, making our stand in the word of God. Doing His will. Calling out evil and giving the gospel to the poor. Judgment to the fatherless. Protecting the widows. Giving comfort to the brokenhearted.

And so, of tribulation comes and persecution with it, we be persecuted for His name's sake that God receives the glory.

That when they come for you, it is because of their wickedness, not your own. And joyfully receive tribulation knowing that God will repay them with wrath, and you with eternal reward.

This is a difficult thing for many, even saved Christians who have done much to sanctify themselves. There is a pride and arrogance that gives a place for wrath, and righteous anger turns to sinful rage. It allows the wicked to claim the moral high ground. It is why they tempt us constantly with degenerate culture and unjust treatment. The gaslighting and humiliation ritual. All manner of provocation, designed to get us to fall that they may accuse us, and, in their twisted view and by the judgment of this world, justify their hatred.

But their hatred is of God the Father and His judgment, Christ in His righteousness, the Holy Spirit and His conviction of sin in their hearts.

We are just the totems of their hatred of God. And by giving cause to accuse us, they bring a bad report of God's people. We aid them in justifying their hatred of God.

And so, we can choose to stand on the rock of the word and not be moved, rejoicing at the persecution that comes knowing it brings glory to God and shows the unbelieving His power, and exposing those who oppose Christ, or we can be petty and foolish and prideful that the unbelieving will see our persecution and think, "Good. They deserve it."

Pray we have the faith to do what's right that God may glory when the devil comes to tempt us.

teachings.title: Ye cannot serve God and Mammon
teachings.summary: There is no prosperity gospel; part of the cost of discipleship is giving of our wealth without fear or greed, laying up treasure in Heaven.
teachings.text:
This is a theme Jesus has been hammering home; the cost of discipleship.

Jesus said we must be willing to hate our family for His sake, and willing to give up our lives. To love others more than ourselves. To not worry for earthly things like food, shelter, raiment. To be willing to forsake all in service to others, that the Gospel be shared.

And, to use what wealth we have in that same service to Christ. *Lay not up ye treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: for where your treasure is, there will your heart be.*

Of all the warnings of the costs of true discipleship, of truly following Christ, this one against Mammon, love of money, not only giving up trying to be rich and gaining stuff, but giving away the stuff you already have, is the hardest for most people to face.

There is no "prosperity gospel." God provides what we need and knows our needs even when we don't. We may even be blessed with wealth but it's not our own. We are supposed to give all, and yet most of us don't even want to give a 10% tithe to our own church.

This can be greed, and it often is. Jealously guarding our treasure here. That it's where our heart is, not Heaven.

But for many, it's fear. Fear of doing without. Fear that God won't take care of us. That if we give away that which is extra in our lives that others benefit and by our works, God be glorified, we will suffer need. This fear grips especially tight in times like this where the debt economy, inflation and taxation and other worldly pressures weigh heavily upon us.

We may not be called to forsake everything we own. But we are called to at least consider it and do it where appropriate, in the measure called for. To be hospitable. Charitable. To do unto others without thought of ourselves and our own comfort.

In two more chapters we will see the rich young man sit down with Jesus and say in all things he is righteous before the law, and Jesus will say ok, sell everything you have and give it all away to follow Me. And the rich young man will walk away. He was being shown the error of his thinking that he was righteous by his works, and most of us won't be called to forsake all. God knows our limitations and infirmities. But we are called to give. To be as wise as this worldly unsaved steward. To not serve Mammon while claiming to serve God.

teachings.title: Willing to die but not to be inconvenienced
teachings.summary: Christians who claim they would die for Christ will not give a little time to Bible reading, church or soul winning, so we must honestly count the cost and strive to do more.
teachings.text:
The emphasis on discipleship that Jesus keeps preaching, the cost and expectations that he has for us to truly be called followers of Christ, not just saved from hell but laying up treasures in Heaven, should have us all feeling convicted. That we're not doing enough.

Most saved Christians will tell you that they would gladly lay down their life for the cause of Christ. That rather than deny Him, we would suffer death in His name. Knowing we have eternal life and knowing that it was a gift, we would gladly lay it down. Out of love and gratitude for the grace that was shown us.

And we may sincerely mean it, although it's easy to say, knowing that it's unlikely to ever come up. It's a cheap hyperbolic brag. Our lives are not our own and having the comfort of the blessed hope of eternal life means that threats of death are threats with Heaven. But even so we know it likely will never be asked of us and so it's easy to say.

But how many saved Christians are willing to lay down 15-20 minutes of our morning to read the Bible? How many saved Christians are willing to go to church once a week, let alone three times a week? To go door knocking and soul winning? To give what extra they have in wealth and in time to the service of others that God may be glorified in us?

How can we expect to seriously be willing to go to our death for professing the name of Christ if we won't be inconvenienced a little bit here and there?

I speak this to my own shame.

And understand there are unsaved people, people working their way to heaven with the false gospel of works, who do more to help those in need than actually saved Christians today.

 I'll tell you truthfully there are reprobates who for wicked reasons give of their time and their money, that benefit the poor and the needy, more than some saved Christians are willing to do.

Count the cost of discipleship. Understand that Christianity isn't just an identity, a scene, a cheap ideological category to cosplay as, the way political and cultural identities are used today. It is not a set of arguments that we have prepackaged for us to spout off against others who have absorbed and regurgitated the ones they've consumed.

Way too many of us who claim to be saved treat it that way. I say this out of love. I say this to chastise myself as much as to motivate you.

When I count the cost, and reckoning my efforts, I find I do the bare minimum for Christ, and sometimes less than that. If you're honest with yourself, you'll find the same.

There are people like this unfaithful servant who do favors for others that they may gain in this life, and in doing so bless other people more than saved Christians who profess the Gospel and have the spirit within them. Strive to do more.
