If you can't be bothered to take up the great commission, and don't go out to share the gospel in the ministry of reconciliation God has commanded us to do, don't you dare act offended when it comes up from the pulpit. 

Even if you're struggling to not have seconds and thirds (and fourths, and a little slice of pie, mmm pie), say "AMEN!!!" when the preacher teaches against gluttony.

If you cuss, if you gossip, if you can't help but share that meme you know you oughtn't.... whatever it is, don't you dare countersignal hard preaching. 

By all means get right, be convicted. But if you ain't right, at least be man enough to admit it is wrong and support the man of God who is calling out sin!

teachings.title: Peter's denial and ours
teachings.summary: Uses Luke 22:62, Galatians 2:11-14 and 2 Peter 2 to show that even mature believers can deny Christ under social pressure, yet Peter went on to preach boldly.
teachings.text:
**Luke 22:62**
*And Peter went out, and wept bitterly. *

There are times in every Christian's life where the story of Peter's betrayal of Christ hits hard. New Christians, who have just accepted the gospel and been saved, turn to their unsaved family and friends, and at the slightest pushback and mocking, get embarrassed and deny Jesus.

Older, more mature Christians even, will keep their faith hidden in social settings or in the workplace. 

We may miss opportunities to go soul winning with our brothers and sisters, in part because of the fear of judgment. That you will be accused by scoffers as Peter was, and so preemptively decline to go. 

We all have a regret of not sharing the gospel in a time and place where we are given the opportunity by God to proclaim the faith that saved us. 

We may weep bitterly by the hospital bed of someone close to us, incapable of knowing the truth because we never shared it. 

The Apostle Peter's story in the gospels is very real and relatable. But it doesn't end at the crowing of the cock that morning. 

The risen Christ appears to Peter again during the 40 days between Easter and the Ascension. Peter, unsure of his calling and, I think, ashamed of his betrayal before the Son of God, decided to go fishing.

**John 21:1-4**
*After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself. There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.*

And as Jesus prepares them food, and eats with them, He gives Peter, who denied Him 3 times, the opportunity to affirm his love of Jesus 3 times. 

**John 21:14-17**
*This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead. So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. *

Peter always loved Jesus, and trusted Him, but his shame for the denial of his Lord in His hour of death made him feel distant and alone. Jesus gave him the opportunity to work through that shame and realize his love for Christ is greater than his shame at letting Jesus down. 

And Jesus says at each affirmation, *feed My sheep*. Serve others. Win souls.  Care for the flock.

The answer to the shame we feel when we deny Christ or the opportunity to share Him with others, isn't to go fishing. To return to the world. But to return to the work of the ministry of reconciliation we all have. 

Soul-winning when you are down bad, and ashamed, when prayer feels a little empty, when Bible reading is falling off, when you know you gotta get right, even if you aren't backsliding, per se, is the way to show yourself the love of Jesus you have. It is restorative sharing with others the love He has for you, and them.

Peter's story doesn't end there, either. In Acts we see him boldly proclaiming Christ, calling Jews to repentance and faith towards God. Enduring beatings and imprisonment to preach the gospel. Of going to the Gentiles with the truth when called by God. 

And even then, Peter isn't perfect. Even as an elder of the faith, he still occasionally felt the pressure to conform to the world. Here, he is called out by Paul.

**Galatians 2:11-14**
*But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?*

It is something we can all fall into, even as older more mature Christians. 

That's why, when Peter writes his epistles, his encouraging message to believers to holdfast their faith, even when facing scoffers, mockers, false teachers, etc...to be like Christ when we are reviled for His sake - is so powerful. Like most good preaching, he is talking about his own struggles, to edify others. 

**1 Peter 2:21-23**
 *For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously*

Being ready to testify of the hope we have even as men falsely accused us, mocking and scoffing our faith, to have the mind of Christ:

**1 Peter 3:13-16** 
*And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

Even as Noah suffered the scoffers and blasphemers of the pre-flood world, as he prepared the ark, those spirits in Hell that Jesus went and preached to, showing those that trust the Lord shall not be ashamed;

Those *spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. *

Peter says the flood that destroyed those wicked people is a like figure to the baptism of the believer, showing the same faith and confidence Noah had to build the ark, saving his family.

*The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.*..

Our obedience in baptism, to publicly proclaim our faith, similarly shuts the mouths of those scoffers, that our conscience is clean in Christ. 

 **2 Peter 2:1-3**
*But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.*

Verse 7-8, *how God delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

Speaking of a believer who didn't share his faith, just Lot still was delivered from their filthy conversation, just as God promises to deliver us from the same mockers and unrighteous people.

*cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet.*

**2 Peter 3:3**
*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.*..


And so let's learn from Peter's slip ups and mistakes, and take heart in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

**2 Peter 3:18-19**
*Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.*

I think many of us like to think of ourselves as Paul, but if we are honest, we are a lot more like Peter.

teachings.title: Christmas decorations, Jeremiah 10 and Romans 14
teachings.summary: Says Jeremiah 10 does not condemn decorating a house with plants, and applies Romans 14 so that believers do not despise or judge one another over keeping the season.
teachings.text:
Annual reminder that **Jeremiah 10** does not condemn decorating your house with plants, and that God decorated His house, the Temple, with firs and box and pines. 

**Jeremiah 10**
*Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel:

2 Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.

3 For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe.

4 They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not.

5 They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good.

6 Forasmuch as there is none like unto thee, O Lord; thou art great, and thy name is great in might.

7 Who would not fear thee, O King of nations? for to thee doth it appertain: forasmuch as among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like unto thee.

8 But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities.

9 Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the workman, and of the hands of the founder: blue and purple is their clothing: they are all the work of cunning men.

10 But the Lord is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation.

11 Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens.

12 He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.

13 When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.

14 Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

15 They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish*.

**Isaiah 60:13**
*The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.
*
The Bible doesn't teach against the use of plants as decoration. It shows us God uses evergreen trees to beautify His temple. 

A tree isn't a graven and decked image of a god. No one bows and serves a decorative house plant, they beautify their homes with them. No one worships a pine tree except pagan "druid" LARPers. 

Even the most secular reprobate consumerist, who strips Christ from Christmas and makes it entirely about snowmen and reindeer and coveting things, doesn't look at the plastic tree covered in lights and tinsel in the corner of their living room and thinks, "I shall worship this." They don't even "venerate" it. 

But that hasn't stopped some from judging believers in respect to holy days, and teaching doctrine of men for commandments. 

There are plenty of reasons to not want to participate in traditional Christmas trappings, especially as they have become in the modern, consumerist world of greed. The lie of Santa, the works-based system that you have to be good, "repent of your sins or you don't get a present!" The profane and the blasphemous way our Jewish-subverted culture has secularized it all. 

But most believing Christians see the season as simply a feast celebrating the miracle of the birth of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Most take the season to reflect on scripture, the great mystery that God was made flesh, to give thanksgiving to God the Father for His Son, to sing Psalms and hymns praising Him. And decorating their homes, eating special meals with family. And giving gifts to one another in the spirit of grace, just as God has given to each of us.

If you don't want to worship Jesus this way, and if you are convinced of yourself that it is a sin, then you should not do it. 

And regardless of your conviction, **Romans 14** should apply;

*1 Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.

2 For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs.

3 Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him.

4 Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

5 One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.

6 He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord; and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it. He that eateth, eateth to the Lord, for he giveth God thanks; and he that eateth not, to the Lord he eateth not, and giveth God thanks.

7 For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.

8 For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's.

9 For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living.

10 But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

11 For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

12 So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

13 Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way.

14 I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.*

No one should judge someone who doesn't want to celebrate even the most faithful of Christmas celebrations, and no one should judge those who do. They certainly shouldn't abuse **Jeremiah 10** to justify their doctrines of men to level railing accusations against people who just think it's a nice thing to do, while keeping Christ as the center of their lives.

teachings.title: Knowing God's will starts with the basics
teachings.summary: Says those who claim a special walk with Jesus but spend more time online than in the Bible or church will never find the deeper things of God.
teachings.text:
Oftentimes, people who say that they have learned how to have a special relationship and walk with Jesus, so that they can listen to God and discern his will, spend more time online than they do reading the Bible. And most don't go to church.

If you claim to want to know God's will for your life, and you don't do the basic things layed out in the Bible, then you'll never figure out the deeper things that He has in store for you.

teachings.title: Eating candy and conscience
teachings.summary: Applies 1 Corinthians 10 to what is sold or given at Halloween, eating without asking question for conscience sake unless another's conscience is affected.
teachings.text:
Here is my policy on eating miniature Butterfingers, Whoppers, Milky Ways, etc...that may come into my possession today and tomorrow 

**1 Corinthians 10:25-30**
*Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake:
For the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof. If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake. But if any man say unto you, this is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof: Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man's conscience? For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks?*

teachings.title: Long hair on men and the scripture
teachings.summary: Explains from 1 Corinthians 11 why long hair is a shame to a man, and that a disputed length must still meet the stipulations of the passage.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 11:14-15**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him? But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.*

Had someone in the comments to this come sowing doubtful disputations over the idea that there's nothing wrong with men having long hair. They were apparently ignorant to the scriptures, and he wanted to argue the point. 

He asked what I would consider "long." I gave shoulder length as the cut off line, shorter than for men and longer than for women. He tried to offer the old "that's subjective! Cultural standards are relative!" argument. 

And so, I asked him what length he would suggest fits the scripture?

He fled the chat. 

But the truth is, there could be some debate over the specific length, the name of the neck for men. Shoulder blades for women. Their waist perhaps. A man's natural neckline. 

So how do we rightly divide then? By looking at what facts we do have, and applying the word of God. 

We know that **1 Corinthians 11:14-15** says there is a length that is acceptable for men and women. That on a man, nature itself tells us that too long is a shame. That on a woman, her hair should be as a covering for her head. So these points are stipulated:

- That nature tells us it is a shame for a man means that it is not relative to style or changing with the times. It is observably true, in all times, because God says we may know it. 

- Men having effeminate hair being shameful is generally considered past the shoulder. 

- Women must be able to cover their head. So, not shorn or short. 

So, while one could debate the shoulder length line, your alternative interpretation must meet those stipulations. Unless you can, you should probably not come into a chat, guns blazing, or you'll end up leaving as a fool.

teachings.title: Choose life
teachings.summary: Reads Deuteronomy 30 and Joshua 24 and urges the reader to choose life, embrace truth and follow Christ.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.

But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

From the beginning, God has offered us a choice. Without that choice, the evil in this world makes no sense. As the Calvinists teach falsely, their god is the author of evil. But our God provides us the choice between good and evil, life and death. 

Throughout the Bible, from Adam and the tree, through even the Millennium Reign, God allows man a choice. 

Of those that choose life or choose death, God may elect some to serve a purpose. To perform a task. To serve as an example. But the choice of life and death stands before all men. 

When the unsaved ask, "If God real, why bad things happen?" We have the answer; because man chooses death over life. 

Calvanism has no answer other than to profane God and blame Him as the heathen do. 

Without that choice, none of the scriptures make sense, none of the judgments of God are righteous. It all becomes a play, a Punch and Judy show of cruelty. 

Choose life. Embrace truth. Pick up your cross and follow Him. 

**Joshua 24:15**
*And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.*

teachings.title: Salt of the earth
teachings.summary: Reminds saved Christians that they are the salt that preserves the world and must not lose their savour.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

Remember that we are the salt of the Earth, as saved Christians. We are the thing that preserves the world. If we lose our savor, If we no longer act as the salt, the world is good for nothing. It will rot. Become rancid. Trodden by men. 

Stay salty my friends.

teachings.title: Gifts of the Spirit: their purpose
teachings.summary: Lays out from Romans 12 and Matthew 6 and Mark 10 that gifts given by grace are talents lent to serve God and bless others, with a reward in this life and the next.
teachings.text:
**Romans 12:5-9**
*So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another. Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether **prophecy**, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or **ministry**, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on **teaching**; Or he that exhorteth, on **exhortation**: he that **giveth**, let him do it with simplicity; he that **ruleth**, with diligence; he that sheweth **mercy,** with cheerfulness*.

By the grace bestowed on us by God, our talents are lent to us that we may serve Him, and by doing so profit others. 

As we've discussed, knowledge and wisdom are gifts of the Spirit, the knowledge of God's word and wisdom of God found in it; the understanding of spiritual things of God. 

And so the gift of prophecy, stems from that that is preaching of the word. Many confuse prophecy with prediction, being a seer, but absent the visions of what was to come given prophets of old by God, prophecy primarily is simply telling others, preaching, the words of God. 

To the extent that one has the gift of preaching, it is from knowledge. And with the knowledge comes wisdom. It helps lead others to Christ and strengthens the faith of those who have already believed. 

And the spiritual discernment gained from the knowledge, understanding and wisdom of God revealed in His word, allows us to tell truth from lies, and "see the Future," by recognizing the consequences and the inevitability of God's judgement that comes from man's sin. 

It isn't being a seer. It isn't looking into a crystal ball or having a revelation in a dream. It is knowing and understanding God's word and recognizing His will, and applying it to your surroundings and seeing things the way He sees them. Morally, and also temporally. The long view. Thinking past ourselves and our time, to see the holy judgment of God, and be at peace with it. 

And so, with the gifts of knowledge, wisdom, prophecy, comes the gift of teaching. Discipling others. Edifying the weaker in faith and knowledge. Helping them to become more useful to God, and so to others. 

The ability to teach the spiritual things of God, with all patience and longsuffering, is a wonderful gift. Sharing the fruits of the Spirit, the word of God, bringing others to see the simplicity of Christ, the understanding of His judgements, growing in faith and losing fear and cares of the things of this world, fearing only God, learning sanctification and separation, to better serve others. It is a ministry full of rewards. 

The gift of exhortation, encouragement and good cheer towards all, secure in the knowledge of the truth and full of faith in God, that others who are troubled or fearful or uncertain, caught up in the cares of this world, the brokenhearted, and help them gain the same spirit of comfort and hope, grounded in faith towards God. Being *ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear*.

There's the gift of giving, the blessing of being put by God's divine appointments into the position to give to others, to minister their needs. Be they physical needs; clothing the naked, feeding the hungry, comforting the sick or brokenhearted, judging the fatherless that they may come to see the mercy and judgment of God in Christ, or spiritual; giving the gospel, preaching the word, edifying the brethren. This is possibly the most precious gift we are given outside of being able to win a soul to Christ. The blessing of being given the chance to help someone else, brings unexpected blessings upon us. 

We are called to offer the right judgment of God on all those we've been blessed to be put in positions over, all leadership and hierarchy being of God. We are to love, show mercy and  rule with cheerfulness. Not as if they are a burden, but recognizing the blessing it is, that we be better servants of Christ.

God rewards those who diligently seek Him. We are given knowledge, wisdom and the ability to preach and teach His word, that we are able to exhort and edify, and comfort the afflicted. To give freely, to judge rightly, in love and mercy, revealing the glory of God by His mercy towards us, that others may come to believe. 

I feel that it is in these moments, where God uses us and the talents given of the Spirit, that He as the potter has fit us to, is how He rewards us in this life. The blessings that follow our being a blessing to others, is wonderful. God's glory revealed through us.

**Mark 10:29-30**
*And* *Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.*

**Matthew 6:19-21**
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

**Hebrews 11:6 **
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**1 Corinthians 3:7-15**
*So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.

Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour. For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

All this to establish the mechanism and purpose of gifts given us by the Spirit. That by the grace of God, who rewards those who seek to know Him, understand His will, given through the Spirit, and by His inspired word, that we may be blessed with opportunities to help minister to others, that we may be blessed in this life and rewarded in the next. 

It is the awesome will of God, manifest in us. 

Tomorrow, God willing, we will break down some of what it's not. And how many misunderstand and misuse the idea of gifts of the Spirit to teach weird and sometimes damning doctrines of devils.

teachings.title: Giving thanks: any day honored to God is acceptable
teachings.summary: Answers a claim that Thanksgiving is pagan by pointing to Romans 14 and the verses that call believers to give thanks in everything.
teachings.text:
JK don't listen to Judaizing vipers who say things like this. They are fools. 

**Any day** you esteem in glory to God and thanksgiving for the blessings He has provided, honoring Jesus, or celebrating His perfect work that is our salvation, is acceptable to the Lord. 

**1 Thessalonians 5:18**  
*In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.*

**Philippians 4:6 ** 
*Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God*.

**Psalms 107:1** 
*O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever*.

Happy Thanksgiving to all my brothers and sisters in Christ. God is great, Amen.

teachings.title: Lot and the Corinthians: sanctification does not decide who is saved
teachings.summary: Explains sanctification and separation as service for edifying the brethren, and shows from Lot in 2 Peter 2 and Paul's greeting in 1 Corinthians 1 that sinning believers are still called saints and righteous.
teachings.text:
The point of sanctification and discipleship is to edify the brethren and the point of separation is to be more useful to God in winning souls and being a blessing to others by being blameless and as much as possible, peaceful with all men. 

If you have been blessed to be able to devote more time and more energy to the word, to winning souls and ministering to the faithful as a servant of God, healing the broken hearted with the baptism of faith in Christ, rather than hold it as a standard of piety like a hypocrite, use the opportunity to bear fruit with gladness, longsuffering and patience and receive those weaker in the faith that they can, by your ministering, be disciples that they may do great things for the Lord.

**2 Peter 2:6-8**
*And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

Just Lot, that righteous man, with a righteous soul, who is celebrated in the New Testament by God as such, dwelt among the filth in ACTUAL SODOM, the most wicked city ever to exist, where there was only one just man. 

But some yahoo with a works salvation false gospel is going to call Lot a "believer" with scare quotes, and imply he is less saved somehow, less of a "Christian" because he had to be physically carried out of Sodom by angels, while another guy has a double wide on a hobby farm and so he's more righteous somehow. 

Hypocrites.

**1 Corinthians 1:1-9**
*Paul called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both their's and our's: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ; That in every thing ye are enriched by him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge; Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you: So that ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall also confirm you unto the end, that ye may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Paul is writing to the church of God in Corinth, to those who are called to believe saints, who received grace of God through Christ, and peace with the Lord, sanctified in Him, and Who shall confirm them unto the end; eternal life.

He says that they are blameless in Christ. That being confirmed unto the end, he is assuring them that they are once saved, always saved. The testimony of Christ confirmed in them. 

Paul is writing this epistle with *Sosthenes our brother*, the same Sosthenes who, in Acts 18 accused Paul before the Roman magistrate Gallio, the deputy of Achaia, Because *Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.*

Sosthenes was Crispus' replacement as chief ruler of the synagogue, and when he brought Paul before the deputy to accuse him, Gallio ignored him and the Greeks beat the rabbi. 

The next time we see him, Paul is calling him a brother in Christ. He's recorded in this epistle as the scribe for the Apostle. 

Really consider all of this, and then understand the context of why Paul is writing to them, to chastise them for multiple sins and divisions. Pride and even fornication amongst them, worse than even the heathens. A list of sins he calls them out for. 

Paul, who persecuted the fledgling churches, helping to kill the saints, dictating to a man who was once the chief Rabbi in the synagogue of Corinth and who had accused Paul trying unsuccessfully to have him punished by the government, to a church full of divisions and boasting, a man sleeping with his stepmother, and all kinds of other issues in the church....

.... And he opens it with that greeting!. 

Go read it again. 

He doesn't question their salvation. He doesn't make them doubt it. He reaffirms the gospel by which they've testified, and through which they've received the grace of God and been called to be saints. Who were not lacking spiritual gifts. 

Really makes you think. 

Really puts things into perspective, especially when you have someone claiming to be a man of God, berating believers as being insufficiently pure enough for him. Who don't meet his standards. Questioning their salvation when he himself preaches a false gospel.

Hypocrite.

teachings.title: God hates: righteous anger and leaving vengeance to the Lord
teachings.summary: Collects Psalms and other verses showing that God hates the wicked, and teaches that believers may hate evil while leaving wrath to God and handling a wronged brother biblically.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 5:5** *The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity.*

**Psalm 5:6** *Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man.*

**Psalm 11:5** *The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth*.

**Psalm 26:5** *I have hated the congregation of evil doers; and will not sit with the wicked.
*
**Psalm 31:6** *I have hated them that regard lying vanities: but I trust in the LORD.
*
**Psalm 10:3** *For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the LORD abhorreth*.

**Psalm 53:5** *There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them.*

**Leviticus 20:23** *And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.*

**Leviticus 26:30** *And I will destroy your high places, and cut down your images, and cast your carcases upon the carcases of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you.

Deuteronomy 32:19 And when the LORD saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.

**Proverbs 6:16-19** These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

 **Proverbs 22:14** *The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.*

**Psalm 139:21** *Do not I hate them, O LORD, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?* *I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.
*
**Zechariah 11:8** *Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me.*

**Hosea 9:15** *All their wickedness is in Gilgal: for there I hated them: for the wickedness of their doings I will drive them out of mine house, I will love them no more: all their princes are revolters.*

**Malachi 1:2-3** *I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.
*
**Romans 9:13** *As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.*

God hates. And He calls us to abhor that which is evil that we may love the good. 

A lot of the anger and frustration that you feel is righteous. It's justified. They are legitimate grievances. And it's okay to have that hatred. But God also tells us to leave the wrath to him. That vengeance is His. 

But that doesn't mean you can't hate them that hate God. And that doesn't mean you can't protect your family and community from them, In a legal peaceful way. And no one stopping you from winning souls which brings people to our side. Brethren for life. 

There are so many things to do and be done before it ever comes to violence. Why in the world are we letting them talk us into it?

And on the same topic, You can hate a brother with cause. There are remedies for it, and if they ask for forgiveness sincerely you have to give it to them and you don't mention it ever again. And if they don't and they don't respond to your biblical outreach to them, You just don't have to have anything to do with them anymore. 

Of course, that's with cause. And after you've considered what you might have done differently. And being repentant for whatever it is you might have added to the situation.

teachings.title: Sanctification is not justification: works that bless others
teachings.summary: Distinguishes sanctification and discipleship from justification, noting that works God leads believers to are a blessing to others and that fruit inspectors who judge them are not walking in love.
teachings.text:
People who conflate sanctification and discipleship with justification, or take a Calvinist view of discipleship, that says you *will* show works, almost always they mean personal works of self-improvement. That you clean up your life or you're not saved. 

And the ironic thing is that those saved by Christ alone, not of anything we've done in the flesh, and who walk in the spirit know that the works God brings us to aren't of ourselves. They're almost always a blessing for others. Most you don't even realize you've done and few people if any recognize it, beyond maybe the person you helped. It is in these acts that we come to grow in love, and the thorns of our heart that leads us to sin are removed. 

But that's a personal choice to choose separation and doesn't affect a person's salvation. 

Hypocritical fruit inspectors never gain that spirit of love from being blessings to others because they are always comparing themselves to others, to justify themselves before men and God. Being holier than thou makes you resent and look down on others. Not love them. 

And so, they aren't used of God, they aren't even saved. The good acts they do or the leaf they turned over are in vain. Filthy rags. And the thorns of their heart remain. Their later end is worse.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 1: God Hates and God Loves
teachings.summary: Collects verses showing that God loves the world yet hates sin, and explains that true love hates evil, loves enemies with mercy and pleases God rather than men.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 6**
*16 These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

17 A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,

18 An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief,

19 A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Psalm 45:7**
*Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows
*
**Deuteronomy 16:22**
*Neither shalt thou set thee up any image; which the Lord thy God hateth.*

**Psalm 53:5**
*There were they in great fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: thou hast put them to shame, because God hath despised them*.

**Deuteronomy 12:31**
*Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.*

**Deuteronomy 25:16**
*For all that do such things, and all that do unrighteously, are an abomination unto the Lord thy God
*
**Revelation 2:6**
*But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate.*


**Amos 5:15**
*Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish judgment in the gate: it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph*.

**Psalm 51:17**
*The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

**Psalm 139***
19 Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God: depart from me therefore, ye bloody men.

20 For they speak against thee wickedly, and thine enemies take thy name in vain.

21 Do not I hate them, O Lord, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?

22 I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.*

**Romans 12:9**
*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

**Matthew 5:44**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you
*
**Proverbs 25**
*21 If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

22 For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.*

**Luke 6:27-38**
*But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you, bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you. And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not to take thy coat also. Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again. And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise. For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them. And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same. And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again. But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven: give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.*

It is without contradiction that God loves the world, hates the sinners, despises abominations, expects us to hate those who hate Him, to hate evil in order to love that which is good, to love our neighbors and to show love and mercy to our own enemies, even if it is to spite them. 

This is a fully mature understanding of love that isn't self-directed feel goodism. 

Love is the magnification of the love God shows us in salvation, the love He showed in Christ Jesus. The sacrifice and seeking the profit of others above our own. To serve. And it cannot exist without hating those who hate Him and despising the things God despises. 

**Galatians 1:10**
*For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.*

**John 12:43**
*For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.*

**Colossians 3:23**
*And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men
*
This is God's promise;

**Proverbs 16:7 **
*When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.*

Those who say love is not judging bow down always to the pleasing of men who despise God and His judgment. They call good evil and evil good. They do the will of man not God, because they don't believe the promise that He will overcome our enemies. Man pleasers. Yet they do nothing to show true love, which is prudent judgment, and presenting the truth of God with mercy and grace. Hating evil, cleaving to that which is good.

teachings.title: Faith Upon Faith
teachings.summary: Explains that beyond saving faith there is the faith that hears what God's word says, believes it and obeys, so that faith grows from faith as one trusts what is clearly written.
teachings.text:
There are "other" faiths beyond saving faith. Faith that builds upon faith. For example, the faith to listen to what God's word says and believe it, and implement it in your life. 

When He says to do or not to do something whether it seems foolish to you or not, but there's clear scripture and so you have the faith to obey? You get so many rewards. 

The Bible says with daily reading the wisdom of God will be given to you, that includes things that help you quit sinning, avoid temptation, gain blessings, get opportunities to give the gospel and win people to Christ... You have to have the first faith to have the next faith, and so on, and that's how Faith grows in you; trusting in the Lord and what is clearly said in his word. Living faith to faith.

Every time one of the Old Testament figures puts their faith in something, it is based on something God said to them and their believing it. 

Make sure you don't believe on your own internal feelings about something or what seems right in your eyes, but things that God says in His word.

teachings.title: Chastened by the Lord
teachings.summary: Shares being gently but clearly chastised by the Lord over an incidental act, and quotes Hebrews 12:6-8 that the Lord chastens every son He receives.
teachings.text:
I was chastised by the Lord today for something that was an incidental act, that I didn't think anything of at the time, in a way that was mild but clear, bringing me into remembrance of it and realizing I was wrong. 

Amen. 

*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

It really was minor, and the chastisement was more embarrassing than anything else. But it was clear and great.

teachings.title: Witnessing with a meek and blameless life
teachings.summary: Describes how to speak biblical standards from credibility, loving people, crediting God, being honest at work and praying for bosses and coworkers. Notes that people will respect you, ask about Christ, or persecute you, and all three are acceptable.
teachings.text:
I don't have enemies, per se. Normal people like me, toxic people, haters of God run from me. Because I try to love everyone I meet the way I would like to be, by them. Being understanding of their fears and being a rock among them, full of joy and thanksgiving. Being understanding that most people have problems and trauma and are afraid, all the time. Telling them why you are how you are. Crediting God. Glorifying Jesus. 

It pours hot coals on the heads of the enemies of God. They hate it. 

But if you establish your faith and morality in a credible way, not as a kook or needless scold, then you can say true things, upholding biblical standards from a position of credibility and emotional and spiritual maturity, so maybe some listen. 

They might not all agree, but they're going to either respect you, ask more about Christ, or persecute you, and all three are acceptable outcomes. Being blameless makes it easy too. 

Be honest at work, pray for coworkers and bosses. Even the douchy ones. Appreciate what they do, even if it's not up to your standards. Even if you have to correct them constantly. Even if you don't get the credit. 

Labor for God in all things. It pays dividends. It creates pleasant work environments. It emboldens others to speak of their faith. It sends reprobates spiralling.

I openly speak out against fornication, divorce, adultery, porn, sodomy, transvestites, castration and mutilation of children, the corruption of this world. No one laughs. No one really pushes back with more than a "yeah, but this is just how it is" or a halfhearted "we can't go back to the past." No one gets offended because I'm not being aggressive or fearful, but coming from a place of understanding that comes from following God's word. People generally react well to it. The law of God is written in their hearts. They still have a conscience, least they be reprobate.

They've been hardwired to be triggered by certain ideas by linking them with dangerous-seeming individuals. To be afraid when God or the Bible comes up. To be afraid because of those who have given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme. 

Be meek, honest and blameless.

teachings.title: Living as the new man so people will listen
teachings.summary: Draws on Paul's second letter to the Corinthians to say that people are drawn to Christ by a believer who lives in the new man with joy, honesty and humility. Describes trying to live in a way approved by God and open to the scrutiny of men, so that others become open to the gospel.
teachings.text:
Just as Paul is writing to the Corinthians in his second epistle to them; if you want to attract people to your cause, in this case, Christ and the ministry of redemption (which should be our primary goal), you have to live in the new man, in joy and confidence, changed by your faith and humble and loving in how you approach people, reflecting the light of the Spirit that's within you. 

The same goes for defending your nation. You can be against something, but it has to be in relation to what you are *for,* and coupled with a living example of why everyone should also be for it.

To this last point, I try, emphasis on try, with the help of the Holy Spirit and staying in God's word, to live in a way that can be approved by God, and can be scrutinized by the conscience of men. (See the study on 2 Corinthians that's ongoing here)

Because I do, however imperfectly, people trust me. They ask me why I am so positive. They know my word is good. My yea means yea. They see me handle tribulation with peace and without fear. They see my charity in caring about them. They see me handle success with humility and meekness, giving glory to God. And to some, it wins them to being at least open to hearing the Gospel. (It repels toxic people, like garlic to a vampire).

I try to live my WN the same way. Unashamed, honest, pro-my family, community and people. So that when I speak against the things being done to us, people listen. When I name who it is doing it and why, they don't freak out, but consider it.

teachings.title: Restoring the joy of salvation
teachings.summary: Uses Psalm 51 to encourage believers who are overcome by the world, worry and fear. Says it is fixed by turning back to God in faith and prayer, and like David singing praises and sharing the good news.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51
**
*12 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

13 Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

14 Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

There's many our guys who are believers, living right, and still overcome by the world. Relationships with family,  being vexed by the wicked conversations of the world, work and money, inability to find a girlfriend, let alone find and keep a wife, caught up with fear and constant worry, often for good reason and rationally so, but for the joy of Jesus and the knowledge that He's overcome all, and we through Him have as well. But sometimes that fades, and the world and the old man creep in. 

But it is fixed by turning towards God, in that first faith and prayer to build upon it. 

And like David, sing praises unto the Lord and share with others the good news that's healed you, so it may others. Amen

teachings.title: Turning to God is what saves a nation
teachings.summary: Says a nation turns around when believers repent of worldly living, fear and covetousness and call on the Lord alone for salvation. Urges trusting God in his time rather than politics, and confessing known sin and returning to his word daily.
teachings.text:
By the way, this is why turning towards God saves a nation. And it takes believers who actually acknowledge God and recognize who Jesus is and count on him alone for their salvation, to turn towards God. That alone will fix it. 

It's not the unbelieving majority, living in sin. God expects that, but they're our fault, for not reaching them with the Gospel. And as Christians live worldly lives, carnal lives, so to the heathens get ever more wicked. 

It's not the reprobates. Their blood is upon us because we don't make their blood be upon them. They're our fault as a nation if they aren't given biblical punishment. So we cannot blame either the unsaved or the twice dead. It is us. It's our sins that are dragging our people down. The inequities of the believer, those who call themselves by His name. That's what damns the nation and the only way to turn it around is for those of us who consider themselves saved Christians to repent of worldly things, cares for the things of this world, fearfulness, covetousness and fornication and turn towards God.

Not make it a scene that you belong to. Not make it a club. Not a LARP or trying on identities. But calling upon the name of the Lord as the sole propitiation for your sins to be forgiven, and then live in the gratitude of the spirit, born again, meet for good works. If we all did that..we Christians..we could be a great people again blessed by God.

Literally you living for God will make other people in your life live for God and then, it ripples out touching lives exponentially. I've witnessed it happen. I've lived it. 

It's real. 

>It's real. 

Can I get an amen?

If any of this pricks any of you, then put down the phone and in prayer, go to God and confess what you know in your heart is wrong and turn to his word every day, with gratitude and love for your creator and savior. In constant prayer, as far from the things of the world as you can be, living for him

**2 Chronicles 7:14**

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

**Proverbs 3:6**
 
*In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.*

teachings.title: Faith without works in James 2
teachings.summary: Explains that James 2 is not about salvation but about faith that offers nothing to people in need. Urges believers to help those around them and not to be respecters of persons.
teachings.text:
Oh yeah, I remember what I was going to say. 

Even sincere Christians can fall into this trap, by the way. The thoughts and prayers and proselytizing, rather than helping is exactly what James to is talking about when it says that faith without works is dead. It has nothing to do with salvation it has everything to do with this tendency to spout off or passively "care," and offer nothing substantial to people in need, now.

**James 2**
*14 What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

15 If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

16 And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?

17 Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone
*
Be mindful of allowing your faith to be of no use to anyone, but instead help people around you in need. Bring it alive. And don't be a respecter of persons. Condescend to the lowly. Be a good judge to the fatherless.

teachings.title: Watch
teachings.summary: Sets the warning of Proverbs 7:18-20 beside the call to watch in Matthew 24:42-44 and Mark 13.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 7:18–20**
*Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves. For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed.*

**Matthew 24:42–44**
*Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.*

Christians are called to watch for the return of Christ, being good and faithful servants, and not letting the delay of His return lull us into sin.

**Matthew 24:46–51**
*Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods. But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

This is why we preach separation unto the Gospel, being a holy people and working to do the will of the Lord, so that when we are found approved in that day. 

But the evil servant is like the foolish woman, calling others to sin. 

**Mark 13:33–37**
*Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is. For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch. Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping. And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.*

teachings.title: Forget thy father's house: the bride of the King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45 pictures believers as the bride of Christ, called to love Him above family and nation as a wife leaves her parents, and to look not to earthly lineage but to the spiritual children they win to the gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 45**, the messianic wedding song, we transition from the King to the bride.

At His right hand stands the queen, decked in gold from Ophir, (a site somewhere south-southwest of Jerusalem renown for its gold).

Her ornamental beauty, provided by the King, to set apart the bride. The honorable women, the church.

As a picture of believers, we see the Kings great desire for the beauty He has bestowed. He is truly Lord and we worship Him.

*Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house*

We are called to hear the appeal from Heaven, to consider and incline our ear (*faith cometh by hearing*), to forget our people and our parents, and to become His.

**Luke 14:26–27**
*If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.*

We are called out, to be His above our family or national bonds. To "hate" here doesn't mean to dislike intensely, as it does today. It means to not love as much, to not prefer over another. To love Christ more than even your kin.

**Matthew 10:35–37**
*For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household. He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.*

Just as a wife is called to separate from her parents and cleave unto the husband.

**Genesis 2:24**
*Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.*

Becoming the bride of Christ, cleaving unto Him, placing our love for Him above others. A wedding is a picture of this relationship that we have. It is given as a parable, that we may better know Him.

In our status as His, the great of every nation shall show us favor. Perhaps in the Millennial Kingdom, certainly not in this life. But when we have come into the inheritance, they will respect our rule because Jesus is their Lord, and we are His.

We are arrayed as a burden in gold and fine embroidery, the white garments of purity, the righteousness of Christ that covers us.

*With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought: they shall enter into the king’s palace*

**Luke 15:10**
*Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.*

This is the celebration of salvation. And the future wedding supper we are called to.

*Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth.*

We will not look to our earthly heritage, the genealogies and lineage, but instead at those we have won to the Gospel, as children who rule and reign with Christ. It is our godly heritage, the spiritual children we present to Christ.

Looking forward to the future of those we have helped come to repentance. This is our vow to our Lord and Savior.

*I will make thy name to be remembered in all generations: therefore shall the people praise thee for ever and ever*. Amen

teachings.title: The Bema seat and wood, hay and stubble
teachings.summary: Explains that bad works at the Bema seat means worthless works for the kingdom, not a list of confessed or covered sins.
teachings.text:
At the Bema Seat, "bad" or wood, hay and stubble, does not mean God pulls out a list of your confessed or covered sins to punish you for them. It means he evaluates the things you did that were worthless for the Kingdom. Things like time wasted (arguing online**👀**), fleshly ambitions (popularity), or religious works done for the praise of men. 

Those works are burned up, resulting in a loss of reward, not a infliction of punishment.

teachings.title: Psalm 45 and the conquering King
teachings.summary: Psalm 45, inspired by the Holy Ghost, prophesies Christ the bridegroom King whose truth, meekness and righteousness are the qualities believers should pursue.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 45** is a doctrine-rich wedding song, that speaks clearly of the Lord Jesus, a bride brought to Him, and the promise of exaltation for the King of Kings.

Of course, the dual nature is both a historic royal wedding song and a profound Messianic prophecy, the Psalms often capture both layers in a way that makes them relevant to our lives as believers. It is a testimony to their divine inspiration.

The same inspiration described in the introduction found in verse 1.

The author says his heart is inditing a good matter, meaning fit to burst with the understanding he is speaking of. His *tongue is the pen of a ready writer.*

God has given him the idea, the words, His inspired, God breathed need to speak and record the word of God, that is bubbling our of his heart.

Jesus said *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh*, be it the evil of the Pharisees or the inspired word. Whether the penman, or those who have committed the word to our hearts.

**2 Peter 1:21**
*For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

And so, moved by the Holy Ghost, given the word of God, the ready writer gives us a song of romance and prophecy. Deeply layered and rich, as only scripture can be.

A similar song to Solomon's, messianic prophecy couched in a romantic allusion.

Verse 2 begins the description of One, fairer than all men, full of grace, blessed forever by God. The Christ. His chosen. The groom, and King.

Girded with His sword, the most mighty. Almighty. A name of God given this person. All glory and majesty are His.

Riding majestically, and prosperously, upon a horse to battle.

**Revelation 19:11-13**
*And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God*.

He has the word of God proceeding from His lips. Destroying the enemies of God with His sharp sword. The strength of His right hand, teaching *thee terrible things*.

What a picture that's painted. What a powerful, Almighty Son of God. Who comes to smite the enemies of His Father, and rule with a rod of iron, but His prosperity is in His truth and meekness and righteousness.

The terrible things, are in this context, the fearful lessons of the Lord. And these are grounded in those three qualities. The truth of the word, the meekness of our Savior, His righteousness in all things.

For the Christian, these three qualities are what we should pursue. We should gird ourselves with the sword of Truth, knowing His word in our hearts, ready to deliver it.

**Hebrews 4:12**
*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

Living in meekness, a servant. Condescending to men of low estate, that they may be saved. Putting our heart to The afflicted, the widow, the fatherless, the poor. For the meek shall inherit the Earth.

And living in righteousness. Doing right things by the judgment of God found in His word. Cleansed by the blood and carrying the righteousness of Christ within us. Being holy, as He is holy.

*Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

Truth, meekness and righteousness means loving what is good and hating wickedness. This is the inheritance of the Lord and the perfection of it found in Christ Jesus.

**Hebrews 1:8–9**
*But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.*

teachings.title: Ye are the salt of the earth
teachings.summary: People are saved by faith alone, but nations are judged by Christians' works, so America's decline comes from believers losing their savour and not turning from wickedness, which is not persecution for righteousness' sake.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 37**, God promises that the wicked shall be cut down like grass, while those that trust in the Lord and do good shall dwell in the land and be fed.

This is a crucial detail in the Christian life, and the fate of our families and nation. The conditional understanding, that those who trust in the Lord, His people, the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus, are given the opportunity to have life, in abundance, though obedience to the commandments of God. To do good.

We are given eternal life by faith in Christ Jesus alone. Trusting God. But our lives on this earth are judged by the good that we do.

People are judged by faith. Nations are judged by Christians' works.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

It is a popular verse, quoted often from pulpits across America. And it shows that there is a solution to the chaos and depravity affecting our society, and that solution is not found in consuming political commentary or voting. It is turning towards God and away from evil, as His people.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

Salt is a preservative that keeps meat from spoiling. It not only stops the rotting, but improves the flavor and texture of it when cooked. When tried by the fire.

We are to be that salt, and when the Christian loses his savour, we see that we become useless, and are left to be trodden down, and rightfully so.

This is in contrast with the earlier verse;

**Matthew 5:10–12**
*Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.*

We often hear Christians complain about being vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked, and who treat the inevitable trodding down caused by our lack of commitment and separation, as persecution for righteousness sake. They are not the same.

In fact, many Christians live as the world, not doing good that they may dwell in the land, and act surprised when the wicked prosper and our nation is flooded with strangers, bringing their idolatry and paganism with them.

They act as though they are being persecuted by politicians and corrupt leaders, while in reality we are the cause.

We become fearful and resentful, fretting about evildoers and being envious of the workers of iniquity.

We ignore God's prescriptions for what ails us, and so we forsake the promises of safety and provision He has given us.

teachings.title: Submit to His judgment and go to church
teachings.summary: Psalm 26 presupposes going to church; avoiding God's judgment leads to skipping church and backsliding, which brings harsher chastening.
teachings.text:
Fundamentally, **Psalm 26** is an encouragement to purify ourselves and avoid hypocrisy while recognizing the evil of men, that we may go into the assembly sanctified.

But this also presupposes that we are to go into the assembly. That we are not to forsake the assembly. That we go to church!

We have an obligation to bless the Lord among the brethren. To gather and sing praises towards Him. Because He has judged us, found us wanting, and yet while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. That in God's lovingkindness, He made provisions of grace to redeem and reconcile us.

For this we should want to sing His praises. But often, if we don't allow God judgment willingly, if we don't purify ourselves, if we gather with dissemblers, and allow our own hearts to mislead us, and justify ourselves despite our sin, we may find ourselves forsaking the assembly, not going in to the congregation, skipping church.

Our conscience may be pricked, and there will be preaching against sin. It is easier to backslide when you do. And the feedback loop compounds, until you are among the vain persons.

If you don't willfully seek the judgment of God in your life, He will still judge you. And in a backslidden state, a Christian can be caught up with the bloody men, and lose their life. Not their eternal life, certainly, but cut short in this one.

Seeking to avoid the refiner's fire of God's judgment can result in far greater pain and loss in His chastening than in the embarrassment and humbling of ourselves when we get right and submit ourselves to His ways.

Be ready daily to submit to His judgment. His mercies are new each morning. It's never too late to get right while you're on this side of Heaven. Allow God to judge your walk, and stand in your integrity, that you may enter gleefully into the congregation.

*That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.*

teachings.title: Cast thy bread upon the waters
teachings.summary: Since we know not what tomorrow brings, give liberally and sow the word at every opportunity, boldly preaching Christ, and it shall not return void.
teachings.text:
The Preacher, Solomon, is beginning to wrap up his homily. He has built his case, that while life is vain, and full of vexing things, toil and tribulation, that God blesses us to enjoy the fruits of our labor. And that God blesses the wise and prudent more than the wicked and fools.

The chapter begins with an appeal to generosity. Casting your bread on the waters. Giving liberally to others, and guarding against an uncertain future. It will return to you in like measure. And you can't take it with you. Who knows what tomorrow may bring?

Whatever will be will be. If the clouds bring rain, or a tree falls in the forest with no one to see, it still is what it is. And so is life. Natural events occur without our ability to predict or change.

**James 4:13-15**
*Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.*

We should then make the most of it, and God willing, enjoy the blessings He provides with thanksgiving. Hospitality. Generosity. Charity towards all, regardless of the conditions we find ourselves in.

Don't wait for a perfect opportunity to do right and live well. *He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.* Take what you are given and act.

We don't understand the miracle of life, the ways of God, let alone the ideal circumstances for our best laid plans. Remember, time and chance happen to us all. Death comes for us all.

Sow your seed in the morning and evening and at every opportunity, and give the rest to God.

Spiritually, this includes the seed that is the word, and laying up treasure in Heaven. Be ready at any opportunity to give the gospel.

**Isaiah 55:11**
*So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.*

Jesus is the bread of life. Cast His word on many waters, and see it return again unto you. Boldly preach salvation in the name of Jesus Christ. Be a cheerful giver with what you have in this world. Be it food or wealth or the truth of Christ.

teachings.title: Better not to vow than not to pay
teachings.summary: God takes vows seriously and wants sincere prayer and humble service, not rash vows, long showy prayers or boasting of works to be seen of men.
teachings.text:
**Ecclesiastes 5** sees a brief detour in the sermon, a rabbit trail of wisdom stemming from Solomon's preaching.

Verse 1 is an oft-quoted favorite of pastors; a reminder to take church seriously, to come to hear and learn in the house of God, which Paul tells Timothy in **1 Timothy 3:15,** is *the pillar and ground of the truth.*
