Luke 17 continues the portion of the Gospel where Jesus preaches and teaches, making His way to Jerusalem. Here, again addressing His disciples Jesus says "*It is impossible but that offenses will come."*

Understand that in the Bible, "offenses" refers to causing another to sin. To place a stumbling block in another's path, giving them occasion to sin. Jesus says it is impossible but that we be offended. That there will be stumbling blocks and snares and temptations brought before all men, including we who are saved. It is inevitable. "*But woe unto him, through whom they come!"*

Jesus says woe unto the person offending, the person laying snares and stumbling blocks. The person tempting another to sin. Woe unto them, that it would be *better that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea than that he should offend one of these little ones*, speaking of the children brought before Him, as we see in the other Gospels.

We tend to understand and focus on the direct application of this teaching, regarding sodomites who target and corrupt children, grooming them with abuse, guile, alcohol, corrupt speech, into becoming a reprobate like themselves. That they don't reproduce, they recruit and do so by offending little ones.

It is a correct teaching to say that Jesus is telling these reprobate pedophiles that they should kill themselves to make it easier on them in Hell, for the added torment they will receive for offending against a child. It is true. The false idea that the Jesus of the NT is some hippy dippy "all is love" God, somehow different from the God of the Old Testament isn't supported by scripture. He comes in wrath on the day of the Lord, and all in Hell are tormented before His presence.

I feel like the high incidents of suicide in the sodomite community comes from this basic understanding that they are escaping even worse punishment than the eternity in outer darkness, burning in a lake of fire, that they already face. Heeding Jesus' warning.

But there is a broader application to this doctrine, one few of us are willing to apply to ourselves. How often have we in our lives brought offense to another? Even if it were intentionally making someone else angry and wrathful?

It doesn't have to be tempting someone to share our sin. Getting them to drink booze, smoke cigarettes, fornication, to steal. It can be as basic as spinning up fear in their lives by promoting that which you know triggers their outrage, and pushes the buttons that lead them to spiral into fear, and wrath. We have a responsibility not to be a stumbling block for others. Jesus' warning is to us, too.

In all matters, we are to seek the spiritual profit of others. It doesn't do that to aggressively red pill or black pill someone weaker in the faith than you. To "truth-rape" a normie. To put the cares of this world before that of the Kingdom to come. This isn't to say we don't speak the truth, stand for Biblical principles, provide guidance and knowledge that others may better navigate the world and grow in faith. But it does mean we don't try to offend, in the biblical sense of the word. Don't seek to trip someone up to an occasion to sin.

And especially don't bring sin to a child, you should rather join the pedophiles at the bottom of the sea.

teachings.title: Make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness
teachings.summary: The unjust steward shows that worldly men use money wisely for the future, so Christians should use their wealth to bless others and lay up treasure in Heaven, for we cannot serve God and Mammon.
teachings.text:
We are in **Luke 16.** The chapter opens with Jesus speaking to His disciples, again impressing upon them the lessons He must as He makes His way to Jerusalem. Here, Jesus tells them parable of the unfaithful steward.

A dishonest steward is to be fired by his wealthy master for mismanagement of the lord's funds. Knowing he'd be out of a job, and not suited to labor or begging, decides to use his position to make deals with his master's debtors, forgiving their debts that they give him favor when he needs it. Buying their loyalty so when he's fired he can go to them for help. The master sees this scheme and, being corrupt himself can't help but be impressed by the servant's wisdom, his chutzpah and cunning.

And the lesson here for His disciples isn't that these men are good, or saved, but that sometimes the unsaved, in serving Mammon, understand better how the world works. How to win friends and influence people. *For the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.*

And so, Jesus says make friends with your wealth. Spend it to others benefit. Forgive them debts. Gain favor the way the unscrupulous servant has, that those you've helped may hear the Gospel, having had the trust gained, and welcome them in the Kingdom one day.

*He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.*

Your wealth does you no good here. Being stingy, miserly, storing up wealth in this world, is forsaking wealth in the next. In parallel passages the Bible says store up our wealth in heaven.

If a worldly unsaved man understands that he can use his position and wealth, the forgiveness of debts to gain favor with men against his future calamity,  how can a saved man not see it? There's more important things than money. Think of that future and how what you have can gain against our future in Heaven.

So, if we are greedy and niggardly, unwilling to give all charitably that we may do the work of Christ, how can God trust us with actual treasure? Incorruptible crowns? Authority in the Kingdom.

If we can't be just with unrighteous Mammon, how will we expect to be just with others souls?

*Ye cannot serve God and Mammon*.

teachings.title: The law of God is perfect: its purpose, grace and judgment
teachings.summary: Argues from a string of passages that God's law is righteous and unchanged, that it shows us our sin as a schoolmaster, and that the old covenant, not the law, was done away in Christ. Closes by asking whether grace is a license to sin (Romans 6) and urging meditation on the law of God.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:*

**Romans 2:11-16**
*For there is no respect of persons with God. For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.*

**Romans 10:4-10**
*For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them. But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

**Ezekiel 36:25-27**
*Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.*

**Psalm 119:165**
*Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.*

**1 John 5:3**
*For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.*

**1 Timothy 1:9**-**12**
*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,* For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with *mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

**John 16:7-11**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;
Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

**Galatians 3:16-25**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect.

For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.

Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.

Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.*

**Romans 3:10-28**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: Their feet are swift to shed blood: Destruction and misery are in their ways: And the way of peace have they not known: There is no fear of God before their eyes. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.

Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. 

Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.*

**2 Corinthians 3:5-17**
*Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God; Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious? For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth. For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious. Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: And not as Moses, which put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.*

**James 2:9-12**
*But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors. For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all. For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law. So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
*
**Psalm 19:7-8**
*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul;
The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple;
The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart;
The commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes;*

**Romans 7:22**
*For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:*

**Romans 8:7**
*Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.*

**Romans 8:4**
*That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.*
 
**1 John 3:3**
*And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure.*

Now this is a lot of scripture, and I struggled to pare down to only this, but it's to buttress the point, the argument I make; regarding the righteous nature of God and His law, grace and judgement, and especially His love towards us. 

Having established without controversy that God is love, that because He is love by necessity, He hates sin and the wicked who live by sin, because He is holy. Righteous in all His ways. That He is faithful to His promises and consistent in His judgments. That God is not a respecter of persons. That all who have sinned deserve death and Hell. But He is full of mercy and grace, so that God, because He so loved the world, gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believes on Him shall not perish but instead have everlasting life.

Knowing all this, then what purpose is the law? If all sin (and sin, the Bible says, is transgression of the law), and all have fallen short, deserving death, is God's law just? Is His judgment fair? 

This is an argument many make; "God made us imperfect and without knowing it we sin and damn ourselves. How is that fair? And what about those who never hear about Christ? They don't stand a chance. How is that fair?"

But the Bible tells us that the law of God is written in our hearts. That His wrath is revealed to us by creation itself. That we are without excuse. 

The Bible tells us that whether it was the Hebrews given the perfect law of God inscribed in stone, that they may know His will and the glorious covenant given them that if they kept the whole of the law they would be made righteous; or the heathen that had only the nature of God's law written in their conscience, and the revelation of His judgment by the natural law written upon all creation, all fall short. 

**Hebrews 8:6-7**
*But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.*

But the fault of the old covenant wasn't in the law, which is perfect, but, the next verse says, the fault was with them. Thus the need for a better covenant;

*Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

So we see that the law wasn't done away with, but the old covenant. Not because God's law was unjust but because we are. That in His mercy He provided us a new covenant. A better testament. The Gospel of liberty in Christ.

And so the law serves His purpose to reveal to us the truth of our condition; that we are all sinners and in need of salvation. The law serves as a schoolmaster. 

And in these later days, the Holy Spirit has been sent to convict the world, that all may know they've sinned by His reproof. 

Because the New Testament isn't that the law no longer is in effect, but that those who understand they are deserving death repent towards God and believe on the Son that they may be forgiven. Redeemed by His blood, cleansed from sin and made righteous. That we will be judged not by our own works, but by Christ's and His righteousness imputed on us that we may be partakers of the promises made. We are condemned by the law but at liberty in Christ. 

God in His mercy extends His grace to all. 

And so, the law stands. Glorious and just. Unchanging. Perfect. And those who walk after the Spirit, the inward man quickened, we delight in His law. We love His judgments. 

But those perishing and those who may be saved by faith but living carnally, after the flesh. Feeding the old man; hate His judgments. They don't wish to consider His law. Because it convicts them afresh, daily.
The unsaved pricked in the heart by the Spirit, the saved chastened by the Father, who scourges His children. 

And so they say things like "that's Old Testament law. It doesn't count any more." Cope. Picking and choosing which of the 600 plus commandments given by God in the Old Testament are invalid based on their own rationalisation. Leaning on their own understanding. 

But it's hard to kick against the pricks.

But we know the immutability of God, that He tells us *I am the LORD, I change not.*

The Bible says; *For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.*

**Hebrews 6:17-18**
*Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed  it  by an oath:  That by two immutable things, in which  it was  impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us.*

**James 1:17**
*Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.*

**Hebrews 13:8** 
*Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.* Amen.

The perfection of God's law hasn't changed. The numerous commandments given that no man has fulfilled, other than the man Christ Jesus who in the flesh knew not sin. 

Be it the hundreds given through Moses, or the 10 originally written in stone, hewn by the hand of God Himself. Or the summation of the whole of the law in two commandments, given by Jesus. The judgment of God stands. 

Yes, the carnal ordinances, dietary laws, diverse washings and ceremonial sacrifices that served as a picture of Christ to come are done away with in Him. The sabbath and the holy days, finished in Jesus. But these were not the same as the commandments by which we come to know sin. 

The single law of Eden existed for the same purpose, that Adam and Eve having received paradise would know sin, and by free will choose to fall and lose everything, that they would be made righteous in faith in God's promise, given by God's grace, and thus glorifying God.

So, what then? If we understand the nature of God, the purpose of His law, the fallen state of man because of our inability to keep all of the law, even one command, the gift of salvation in Christ and the good news of our liberty from death and judgment, are we who believe free to sin? 

Is salvation a license to offend the immutable and perfect law of God? The Bible is clear;

**Romans 6**
*What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

2 God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?

3 Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?

4 Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

5 For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:

6 Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.

7 For he that is dead is freed from sin.

8 Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him:

9 Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death hath no more dominion over him.

10 For in that he died, he died unto sin once: but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

11 Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

12 Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.

13 Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

14 For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.

15 What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.

16 Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

17 But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.

18 Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness.

19 I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.

20 For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness.

21 What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

22 But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.

23 For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

Understanding this; that we are freed from the debt of sin, purchased by the blood of Christ, we become servants of righteousness. We are free from the burden of the law and no longer slaves to sin, if we walk after the new man. To this end we are called to His purpose. 

Our old man will sin. The lusts of the flesh still exist, even as our spiritual new man is at liberty. But we are encouraged to walk in the Spirit that we may better serve our purpose, which He has crafted us for. 

Yes we are at liberty due to the grace and mercy of God. But we must mortify our members, crucifying ourselves daily. Walking in the word. Feeding the new man. Separation. Sanctification. Love. 

And in doing so, glorifying God.

I don't know if I conveyed what I mean very well. The Bible gives us the nature of God, man, the law, salvation and the perfect judgment of God that stems from it all. That's my point. And from this we can draw the conclusion that His law is perfect. It stands today. It serves a purpose in the New Testament, as much as the Old. It existed before Moses. It will be what rules the Millennial Kingdom. It will be the books by which the dead are judged by before the White Throne. 

It is perfectly fair. It is holy. It is righteous. Despise not the law of God, but meditate on it day and night.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 3: God Is Holy
teachings.summary: Gathers verses on the holiness of God and shows that because He is love He hates sin and is separate from it, and that we are called to be holy as He is holy.
teachings.text:
**Exodus 15:11**
*Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?*

**1 Samuel 2:2 **
*There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.*

**Isaiah 57:15 **
*For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.*

**Leviticus 11:44**-**45**
*For I am the LORD your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. For I am the LORD that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.*

**Isaiah 6:3** 
*And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.*

**Revelation 4:8**
*And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.

***Leviticus 19:2***
Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy.
*
**1 Peter 1:16  **
*Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.*

**Psalm 103:1**
*Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.*

God, who is love, the very essence of love, who because He *is* love, hates our inequities, pride, lying and violence against the innocent, all the sin that we do or invent in our wicked heart. Because of this, God is holy. The Lord is separate from sin. Singular in His perfect ways. Where *we can* love, He *is* love. Where we are called *to be* holy, He *is* holy. 

The Lord God's name is Holy. Rejoice. The angels sing "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty!" Father, Son and Spirit. Each separate and righteous, all one God almighty. 

But holiness is not just righteousness, which is the works of holiness. Like hate of that which is evil is a part of love, righteousness is part of being holy. 

**Psalm 145:17**
*The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.*

Therefore we come to understand the glory of God. He is all powerful. All knowing. Ever-present. There is none like Him, for this He is set apart, and by His love establishes what is evil and wicked, good and true, and thus by His righteousness, He is holy. 

And, the Bible says because He is love, we should love. And because He hates evil, we should hate evil. And because he shows man mercy, we should show mercy. And because He gives to us His gift of salvation by His grace while we were yet sinners, we should show grace to those that sin against us. 

And in doing so, we be holy, for He is Holy.  

Separation from sin is in the acts of righteousness to which we have been called to by a holy God. To be a holy nation. A royal priesthood. To be an holy offering fully acceptable to the Lord our God. 

Bless His holy name.

teachings.title: The Nature of God, Part 2: Hate Is Part of Love
teachings.summary: Shows from John 3:16, 1 John 4 and Romans 5:8 that God is love, and reasons that God's righteous hatred of evil is an expression of His love, so that love cannot exist without hating what God hates.
teachings.text:
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*..

**1 John 4***
7 Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.

8 He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

9 In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.

10 Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

11 Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.

12 No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.

13 Hereby know we that we dwell in him, and he in us, because he hath given us of his Spirit.

14 And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.

15 Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God.

16 And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.

17 Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment: because as he is, so are we in this world.

18 There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.

19 We love him, because he first loved us.

20 If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?

21 And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.*

**Romans 5:8 **
*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
*
**Ephesians 2**
*4 But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,

5 Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)

6 And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:

7 That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus.*

**John 13:34**
*A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.*

**1 Corinthians 13**
*4 Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

5 Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;

6 Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;

7 Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

8 Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.

***Deuteronomy 7:13***
And he will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee: he will also bless the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy land, thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep, in the land which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee.
*
**1 John 3:16**
*Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.*

So, having shown yesterday that the Bible says God *hates*. That He hates and abhors and despises men and evil, that He judges and repays the wicked. That he seeks vengeance and recompense, especially for that which is an abomination to Him. 

But the Bible says God is love. In no uncertain terms He is love. God so loved the world He gave His only begotten Son, Who so loved us that He gave His life for us. While we were yet sinners, He died for us. No greater love is there, according to God's word.

So we must consider that there is no love without hating the things God hates. And if the righteous hatred of God is an expression of His love towards us; if judgment, hate and wrath along with charity, grace, longsuffering and mercy, are all part of God, and God is love, then is there contradiction? No, God is without contradiction, for He is holy, and God is love. 

And so, hate is a part of love. 

*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

This is the biblical definition of love. 

And if the love of God is like a light shining through us, His love magnified by us, then, by seeking His holiness, we will also shine the light of His love through what we hate. What we abhor. By hating the evil God hates, by hating His enemies just as we show love to our own. 

Because the hate of God is an expression of His love. It is a subcategory of the qualities of love. It isn't the opposite of love, it is a form of it. 

Our own hate can be misguided, it can be cruel. It can be wicked. It can be seen in envy and strife and unrighteous wrath. But God's is pure. 

Because God loves the world, because He loves His children, the sons and daughters adopted by faith in His grace, He hates that which is against us. His is a perfect hatred and He tells us in His word what the objects of His love *and hate* are. 

And the love of God is righteous, because our God is holy. 

Tomorrow, we will look at the holiness of God.

I'm laying the groundwork for a thesis over the next several days, so I would ask everyone bear with me, for in the end. God willing it'll make sense. I'm sort of working it out for myself to better explain it.

teachings.title: Our bad report and hardened hearts
teachings.summary: Hebrews warns that saved believers who fall back into dead works can give the lost cause to harden their hearts until it is too late, so Christians bear a grave responsibility to walk righteously so that any rejection is the unbeliever's own fault.
teachings.text:
One of the key points throughout the book of Hebrews is that if we who are saved fall back again to the old ways, to the sin offerings and dead works, to bitterness at reproach, to neglecting our Christian walk, we bring others down with us, who have not received salvation. Who haven't yet come to the saving faith. Who may be pricked by the Spirit and hear the power of God's Word, and so taste of the heavenly calling and fall short by our example. And *thereby many be defiled.*

Especially knowing that there comes a point where their rejection of the truth and refusal to find faith in the hope we have can leave them reprobate. Either in death, or by being turned over to a reprobate mind by God. We give them cause to harden their hearts. To be dull of hearing. To not believe our report.

Our faith alone cannot bring another to the knowledge of the truth. But our lack of faith can lead the lame to stumble, as we bring them to uneven paths, leaning on our own understanding.

Many of us harp on the Reprobate Doctrine because it is an extremely important Biblical truth that far too many are ignorant of, or reject to lean on their own understanding or follow the wisdom of men. There is a point where it is too late for some. And once they are given up and given over, they are twice-dead. Children of Hell, fit for burning.

But this isn't simply for the cursing of those who have been rejected by way of their hardened heart, but a grave warning to those of us who have been blessed by the faith in God's promise and redeemed in the blood of Christ.

Faith comes by hearing the word of God.

So does reprobation. The Bible says they have the knowledge of the truth but don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. That they turn the truth of God into a lie.

If they will harden their hearts and turn away from the truth, don't let it be that we, like David, *despised the commandment of the LORD,* and give *great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme.*

Don't let it be by our bad report.

Rather, if they reject the truth of God and His offer of grace and mercy, let it be because by our righteous conversation. Our behavior. That they see our faith and that we walk the straight paths, and if it offends them so be it. If our separation from the things of this world and the peace we have because of the blessed hope we've attained offends them, then it's their own dull hearing and seared conscience to blame.

This is a great responsibility.

teachings.title: Run the Race Looking unto Jesus
teachings.summary: Believers must lay aside guilt, bitterness and the cares of this world to run the race, receiving God's chastening as a sign of His love.
teachings.text:
Amen!

The pure hard preaching of Hebrews is building to a crescendo. The case made for faith in Christ Jesus, without the works of the law or traditions of man, against the temptations to backslide the way of Judaizers, but towards full faith in a better testament, nearly complete.

The Spirit through the author, telling us the will of God and reminding the hearers of His word the excellency of His faithfulness in keeping the promises and bestowing the blessings on those who came before us.  Those just who lived by faith. The saints named from the patriarchs and prophets, and the unnamed Christians  who for their faith in the promise of Christ suffered mockery, pain and death:

...*others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented; (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.*

Many who endured in faith towards God's word, not seeing the promises but in hope knowing they would be delivered by the Lord, faithful and true.

And so we, who carry burdens, the weight of guilt, of bitterness at correction, of the distractions and cares of this world, which can lead to envying of the unsaved and impatience with God, to sin, to the fornication of putting the pleasures of the flesh before the promise of our inheritance and the blessings to come, Paul encourages us to standfast in the faith.

We have a race to run. A crown incorruptible to receive. The yoke of dead works and guilt for sins forgiven slowing us in our course. We must shed these things, striving for the mark set before us.

And where we slip, where we stumble, know it is God's correction, rebuking those sons whom He loves. Bringing us reproach that we may turn from the sin or shed the burdens that slow us down. For our edification we must not despise the rod of correction given us by our Father, but take joy in that He loves us.

*Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds. Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.*

If we consider Jesus, who literally authored the word that our faith hangs on, and finished it by the work He did, the first fruits of the resurrection assuring us of His faithfulness, if we keep in mind the shame of the cross which He endured for our sin and to do the will of He who sent Him. Our struggles with sin and the weight we carry in this world is nothing.

Cast it off least we be castaway.

teachings.title: Lent, Fasting and the Gospel of Grace
teachings.summary: Contrasts Lent with Biblical fasting, showing that fasting is private and never a way to earn or keep salvation.
teachings.text:
**1 Timothy 4:1-3**
*Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.*


Lent is the spiritual equivalent of making a New Years Resolution, where you publicly vow to give up something that you probably should anyway and usually fail to keep at it for more than a few weeks. 

The biggest difference is the false expectation of God to give someone grace towards salvation (which He gives freely to those that believe on Jesus Christ) for not drinking as much booze as normal, or giving up chocolates or Twitter.  

And then there is the abstaining from meat, rather than simple fasting in a Biblical way.

**1 Timothy 4:4**
*For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving*

**Matthew 6:16-18 **
*Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.*

Fasting isn't a way to earn salvation and it certainly isn't a way to keep it. It isn't meant as a means to purchase forgiveness or indulgences. It is a spiritual act, which like prayer should be done in private, with the intent of bringing you closer to the Lord. And it isn't done by skipping a meal, dessert or having a veggie pizza and fish and chips instead of a burger.

teachings.title: Making an Idol of the Translation, a Man or an Opinion
teachings.summary: Warns that elevating the KJV translation above the God who gave the word, or following a man or an opinion as an identity, is a form of idolatry.
teachings.text:
It struck me the other day when Ruckmanites were arguing that the KJV, which is the inspired and preserved whole word of God in English, providentially collected and translated at the dawn of English being the lingua franca of the world, and the printing press and universal literacy, was more than that, but itself to be seen as a separate inspiration, given to the translators. Implying the book itself was different and special and thus the preservation of the word to that point, wasn't. That God's word hasn't been preserved for all ages in the manner He saw fit and necessary to save those who would answer the call, but only in 1611 became perfect. 

This makes the translation itself an idol. It is worshiping the created more than the Creator who spake it into existence before all creation, and Whose Spirit overcame the prophets and apostles to reveal it. And the defense of the man or men who promote this idea to the point of infallibility is Idolatry.

All the "I am of Apollos," "I am of Paul," "I am of Catholicism," "I am of Luther," "Calvin," "Hyles," "MacArthur," "Ruckman," "Anderson"... whomever, not necessarily a reflection of the man, but the need by others to make the man or their ideas your identity, is a form of Idolatry too. 

We recognize this form of idol worship in politicians and political movements, ideologies, and it's easy to spot in sin, Mammon, coveting things, but we often fail to see it when talking about the things of God as if they were more than the creature God made for His purpose. 

The clay more than the potter. 

And so, rather than praising God that His word is there for us in our native tongue that we may be easily and thoroughly furnished to good works for Him, we can slip into holding up the carnal, the clay as an idol itself. 

**Colossians 3:5**
*Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry*

**Isaiah 44**

*9 They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.

10 Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image that is profitable for nothing?

11 Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they are of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; yet they shall fear, and they shall be ashamed together.

12 The smith with the tongs both worketh in the coals, and fashioneth it with hammers, and worketh it with the strength of his arms: yea, he is hungry, and his strength faileth: he drinketh no water, and is faint.

13 The carpenter stretcheth out his rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.

14 He heweth him down cedars, and taketh the cypress and the oak, which he strengtheneth for himself among the trees of the forest: he planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it.

15 Then shall it be for a man to burn: for he will take thereof, and warm himself; yea, he kindleth it, and baketh bread; yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it; he maketh it a graven image, and falleth down thereto.

16 He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied: yea, he warmeth himself, and saith, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire:

17 And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.

18 They have not known nor understood: for he hath shut their eyes, that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand.

19 And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, also I have baked bread upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh, and eaten it: and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?

20 He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?*

teachings.title: Pay thy vows and plead His promises
teachings.summary: God holds us to the vows we make in His name, yet He delights when we remind Him of His promises in prayer, and in Christ we have boldness and access to ask of the Father.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 28**
*And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God:*
*And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.*

The moment of truth. Will God deliver or will Jacob be killed? And if he puts his full trust in God, recognizing His power, having faith he will be delivered safely to his father's house in peace, he will have to honor his vows.

Sometimes we as Christians, especially when we haven't been walking with Christ, maybe backslidden or just stubbornly trying to fix and control things in our lives, we will make vows to God if He would provide. God holds us to the vows we make in His name.

**Numbers 30:2**
*If a man vow a vow unto the LORD, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth*

**Ecclesiastes 5:4**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed*.

**Psalms 76:11**
*Vow, and pay unto the LORD your God: let all that be round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.*

At the same time, God delights in our reminding Him of His promises, in prayer and supplication. Because God is not slack concerning His promises. He keeps His side of every covenant. And our acknowledging of this and trusting Him to do so brings Him joy and glory. It is not tempting God to remind Him, by our recognition, realizing all He does is in grace and mercy to us, as sinners, that He is true to His word and won't let us down.

And in Christ we have the authority to boldly go before the Father, and all we ask shall be delivered.

**Ephesians 3**

*8 Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;*

*9 And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:*

*10 To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,*

*11 According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:*

*12 In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

*13 Wherefore I desire that ye faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.*

*14 For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,*

*15 Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named,*

*16 That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;*

*17 That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,*

*18 May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;*

*19 And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.*

*20 Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,*

*21 Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.*

teachings.title: Vessels to honour and to dishonour
teachings.summary: In God's great house carnal believers are still saved but earthen vessels, which refutes Lordship salvation and perseverance, and we should sanctify ourselves to be gold and silver vessels.
teachings.text:
And being His, we are as vessels in His great house. Some earthen and wood. Carnal Christians. Who, while believing and part of the Kingdom, in the great house so to speak, but not being sanctified, are less suited to His purpose. He says not to be like they are, but to sanctify yourself that you become as the vessels made of gold and silver, meet for His use. For His good works.

This dispels the false doctrine and damnable heresy of Lordship/perseverance of the saints. We are all saved who believe. And some will sanctify themselves to honor, becoming more useful to God. Others won't be more than earthen pots, and dishonored.

But all are saved.

We should strive for gold and silver. For crowns. For mastery. To be a soldier for God. Enduring hardship for the sake of those who may believe and be saved.

teachings.title: The self-righteous and the wedding garment
teachings.summary: Explains that self-righteous people think their good works make them better than others, when the only righteousness we have is His imputed righteousness. Compares the invitation to the wedding party, where those who come in their own filthy garments are cast out.
teachings.text:
The term self-righteous is literally a designation for the smug, prideful people, puffed up, thinking their good works make them better than others, when we are all condemned in sin. When the only righteousness we have is His imputed righteousness, washed in the blood. 

They are self-righteous and think they are better than everyone else and are going to be judged as they judge, and be shocked when they are found wanting.

We have been invited to the wedding party. The wine and meat are prepared. Fatted calf slaughtered. Everything is ready. He's provided us with wedding clothes. Invited both good and bad. 

And some will come not dressed for the wedding, clad in their own garments, which are filthy rags. And they will be cast out into outer darkness.

teachings.title: Not only saving souls but building them up
teachings.summary: Paul's care for the Thessalonians shows that after winning souls we must edify new believers like our own children to walk worthy of God.
teachings.text:
Continuing to exhort the church at Thessalonica, Paul reminds them of their conversion, repenting towards the Gospel, and of how Paul and his helpers behaved among them, just as they preached the truth of Christ Jesus in Philippi, a city a few hours west, in northern Greece.

It was there in Acts 16, where Paul and Silas are accused of causing "exceeding trouble" by those who protested the gospel being preached, and brought them before magistrates, had them scourged, and finally jailed Paul and Silas. All of which came to serve the glory of God even the more, getting their jailer and his family saved, and planting a church.

And we are told here, that it is this time in Philippi that the members of the church of Thessalonica would recognize how shamefully treated they were for their mission, and understand that they came to them boldly with the word of God, through much tribulation, without guile or flattery, but with the stripes of suffering and still proclaiming the truth. That they were willing to give them not just the Gospel, but give up their own lives to proclaim it, because it is truth, and out of the love they feel towards them that received it.

Paul then reminds them of how, like his own children, he gave them not just the good news of Christ that brought to them salvation and the Spirit, but further exhortation to live blamelessly, as is befitting a saved Christian. To walk worthy of the call they answered, worthy of the God that saved them.

A reminder that it is not just saving souls that we should do, but then building upon that salvation, encouraging and edifying babes in Christ, as we would our own children, to walk a Christian walk. Preaching against sin and towards the path of righteousness. Even in tribulation and contentions by man, but pleasing to God.

Paul compares them and their tribulation and persecution they are suffering to the churches in Judea, and their persecution by the Jews. Following after the churches in Christ, to be likewise afflicted, persecuted by the Macedonians, their fellow countrymen.

teachings.title: The sheep and the goats: charity shows faith
teachings.summary: The charity of the sheep is how their faith is shown and lived, not the means of entering the Kingdom, and the goats' lack of charity reflects their unregenerate state.
teachings.text:
Rounding out the chapter, Jesus gives us a summation of the end, that He will gather His sheep unto Him, and the goats, the unbelieving, be cast into Hell.

Christ's rationale, that those who are His extended charity to the needy brethren, and by this, perhaps unwittingly as it is painted by Him, did so unto Him;

*Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me...Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.*

Again, works-based heresy puts it that it's these acts of charity, which is the love shown others as a reflection of the light of God, the grace He's shown us magnified by our works is the means of entering into the Kingdom, rather than the way by which our faith is shown. How we are separated from the goats as His sheep. As the Bible says in **James 1**;

*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

Religion is the practice of our faith. This is how it is lived.

And note that the sheep didn't even consider the gain, that it was truly Jesus being helped rather than a stranger. It was just what they did. As Paul reminds us; *Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares*.

And to the goats, Jesus says; *Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.* The significance of their not having charity in their hearts from God's grace is reflected in their spiritual condition.

teachings.title: Resentment toward those saved without hitting bottom
teachings.summary: Teaching that one must repent of sins to be saved can make those who came to Christ through deep sorrow resent and doubt believers who came by easier paths.
teachings.text:
I think one of the stumbling blocks for those who have come to repentance via their genuine sorrow for sins, those that hit bottom, so to speak, seeing their lives and relationships destroyed by their own selfish and destructive behavior, and having a rocky path to making things right, is that there are resentments for those who come to the faith by other means.

There are many who are raised Christian, in godly homes, and can't even tell you when they believed.

There are many who, when they heard the truth, accepted it. Absent trauma or drama, and yet saved.

There are those who had long ago cleaned up their act, dealt with their addictions, or put away the anger and hurt at being victimized, say by abuse, physical, sexual or emotional. That turned over a new leaf, and yet only believed on the Gospel years after.

And there are those, caught in the jaws of addiction, struggling to get out, long after repenting of what led them there, but unable to break free, who are comforted by a believer, and asking them, are given the Gospel and while yet, still sinners, in a moment of clarity, believe.

People who crawled through whatever hell on earth to come to salvation, by sorrow for their sin, can look at these disparate cases, and others like them, and think "that person is not really saved, like I am."

And the promotion of the idea that we must repent of our sins to be saved feeds that resentment, and can make a repentant heart grow bitter over time.

teachings.title: Repentance of sin breeds hypocrisy and testimonial pride
teachings.summary: Emphasising what one turned from instead of what one turned to creates a caste of the more saved, fruit inspectors and boastful testimonials, when all were equally damned and saved by grace alone.
teachings.text:
This resentment is similar to the workers who labored all day for the same penny that those late arrivals collected in the parable Jesus tells in Matthew 20. It's sort of the inverse reaction of the good son in the parable of the prodigal son.

It's this attitude that leads to holier than thou fruit inspectors, judging others salvation by their works, being a respecter of persons regarding testimonials, etc.

Before heading in to Matthew chapter 23, it's a good idea to consider how hypocrisy flourishes from the idea of salvation by repentance from sin, rather than repentance towards God and faith in Christ.

By placing the emphasis on what was turned from, rather than the testimony of what is turned to, what the changing of mind has wrought through faith, it creates an almost inevitable form of a caste system within a church. Of respecters of persons, who in hypocrisy see themselves as *more saved* than others.

Just as the apostles asking Jesus of whose sin was responsible for the man blind from birth, or those questioning him about the men killed by Pilate, are those who had a wall fall on them killing them, the tendency and inclination to place the path to righteousness some take over the experience of others is the same form of hypocrisy which Jesus warns us against.

For all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God. For all were perishing before repenting to believe on Christ. For all are deserving of hell, and none are justified by their works of the law.

We are all in the same boat and there but for the grace of God go each and every one of us. Regardless of how relatively easy we came to salvation, and regardless of how we struggle to pick up our cross daily and follow him.

And losing sight of that leads to our focusing on the mote of our neighbor's eye. Of neglecting the beam in our own. Of judging in hypocrisy the Christian walk of others, while neglecting to work out our own salvation in fear and trembling.

This is one reason why I dislike so-called testimonial preaching. Not the testimony of Jesus Christ and the saving power of faith, but the long winded testimonials, almost reveling in past sin, showing you just how down low someone was before receiving the gospel, almost a point of pride of how much they had to dig themselves out to get to where others are mercifully, by the grace of God.

And I have been in churches where this becomes almost a competition of sorts. And where people blessed to have been born into a Godly family, and whose sowing of wild oats was almost incidental, making it out to be that they were low down wretched creatures, by way of showing just how really super duper saved they are, through their "struggle." Who haven't been blessed by God's grace and mercy, are embarrassed by it, for the glory that is heaped upon those with a testimony of a life of sin, turned around.

This is yet another reason why Satan has painstakingly and methodically brainwashed everyone into adding "...of sin" to repentance. It's another way this becomes toxic in even good churches, with the right Gospel.

We should not glory in the fact that those more sinful than we were saved. We should glory in God that he would save any of us. We were all equally damned. We all had to turn to believe the same thing to gain life. One sin or millions. A degenerate life in the swineherd, for a life of ease and comfort of our father's estate.

For all have fallen short of the glory of God and deserve death and Hell.

But God has sent his servants to invite us to his Son's wedding feast, both good and bad, called to repentance. Amen

teachings.title: Do not turn to the right hand or the left
teachings.summary: Uses Proverbs 4:27 to warn against the false either-or choices the devil offers, and points to steadfast faith in God alone as the true path.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 4:27**
 
“*Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove thy foot from evil*.”

Don't get caught up in the false binary presented by the beast. Don't go looking at things through the lens of an either or dialectic. 

The devil offers us two choices, and is fine with you taking the greater of two evils, but is equally satisfied with taking the lesser. 

But the Bible says not to walk on the path of evil regardless of which "side" it presents itself as

The true third position is the path of righteousness and steadfast faith in God alone. It is what will save your nation, it is what will deliver you from the wicked. It is the promise and protection of God the Father through Christ the son, sealed by the Holy Spirit.

teachings.title: There is no liberty outside of Christ
teachings.summary: Says true liberty cannot be gained from politics or documents, and that promises of political liberty and exemption from tribulation are a lie bought by the covetous and fearful. Urges turning to the Lord and staying in His word, and notes that a believer threatened with death is being threatened with Heaven.
teachings.text:
I have said it before; There is no liberty outside of Christ. 

There is no liberty to be gained from politics or enshrined in documents or anything else of this world.

The false promises of politically guaranteed liberty, material prosperity and being entitled to exemption from tribulation is the lie sold by the devil himself, and bought by every covetous and fearful dummy. Selling their eternal and holy inheritance and losing their blessings that go along with it for corruptible things of the flesh. Esau selling it for a bowl of pottage.

People desperate for us to 'do something,' terrified of tyranny, confusing discomfort and hardship with true persecution, they hate the idea of doing the one thing we can, turn to the Lord. Stay in His word. They scoff. They talk sedition and rebellion instead, and flock to places where they are insulted and outraged, assaulted and maligned, consuming things created by people who hate them and God.

If you're looking to avoid tribulation and persecution by any means necessary, if you're that fearful and have so little faith, I frankly don't think you're saved. I would say you need to get right with Jesus, but I don't think some of you can in the state of terror you're in.

.

If you truly believed that when they threaten your life, they are threatening you with Heaven, you wouldn't be afraid.

teachings.title: God sees when we go quiet
teachings.summary: Compares a child who goes silent when up to something to a believer who stops praying. Encourages talking to God about sin and bad decisions, with an apology, because he still loves us as a parent loves a child.
teachings.text:
Having adult children, it gives you some perspective on how God feels, sometimes.

You notice that when your kids are up to something they know you wouldn't approve of, they go silent suddenly. The everyday or every other day conversations dry up for a few days.

That's how God sees it when we're not praying to him everyday. He sees right through it

Don't let sin in your life stop you from talking to God about it. Don't let bad decisions you've made go without at least an apology. He still loves you, just as a parent still loves their child. Don't let embarrassment keep you from Him

How many times have you ghosted your own parents who you love, ghosted them for a few days cuz you just don't want to hear it.

Everybody raise their hand

teachings.title: Saved Christians forget they were sinners
teachings.summary: Observes that many Christians act as though they were never sinners or backslidden after salvation. Says most believers go through backsliding and that real maturity admits sin and shows grace to others.
teachings.text:
I think a lot of Christians, especially online (but even before there was an internet believe me), but a lot of Christians act as though they were never sinners or backslidden after they've been saved. The average span of zealous devotion in the faith is something like 3 years. It generally takes the old man about 3 years to push his way back after one receives the new man.

Some people remain cast away for the rest of their natural life, even though they have that eternal reward waiting. Many eventually mature and come to understand the awesomeness of the gift they've been given. But most go through some form of backsliding, or falling away. 

The cares of the world come for us all in different ways through different means, and the devil is like a ravenous lion seeking whom he can devour. 

But, most Christians will portray themselves as having always been perfect in their ways. They may admit to a sinful past as part of a testimony to how much they've changed, but it's rare they'll admit their own sins. It takes a kind of maturity in Christ and in faith to be able to. 

I mean, when you ask them they'll all admit of course I'm a sinner, but few really mean it because we all want to look good. But you can tell when someone has had a sincere repentance from whatever had taken them away from their love of the Gospel.

teachings.title: The shape of the earth is not Bible doctrine
teachings.summary: Says neither the flat nor the globe view is Biblical doctrine and that doubting someone's salvation over it is wrong. Warns that wonder at world events must not outrank a relationship with God, and that nothing is known for certain apart from Christ and him crucified.
teachings.text:
The shape of the earth isn't Biblical doctrine, and both FEs and globers claims that it is are foolish. 

And suggestions that either view isn't saved, based only on whatever preferred theory they have about it is uncalled for. Not only uncalled for, but an indication that you think belief in the shape of the earth being round or flat is part of the Gospel, and so it casts doubts on your own salvation. Don't do it. 

And, as always, this *not* an invitation to try and prove your view is the real biblical one to me.

If your wonder at what's going on all around you in the world is more important than your spiritual relationship with God, your priorities are wrong and you need to get right with Jesus.

This goes for fears and cares of this world. They should be an incidental distraction or a sign of the times, to observe. Not your religion.

And if you think you know for certain anything other than Christ and him crucified, you're a fool.

teachings.title: Turning toward the Lord is all we have
teachings.summary: Only Bible-believing Christians turning from their own wicked ways to God can delay the wrath America deserves; voting, shooting or vengeance are vanity.
teachings.text:
It is in the hands of Christians, Bible believing, born again sons of God, to turn away from their wicked ways, their indulgence in the world, in sin, in the subversive and perverse things we are tempted with, and turn towards God the Father, in Jesus' name.

All other methods of delaying the wrath that America deserves are vanity. We cannot vote our way out. We cannot shoot our way out. We cannot riot and murder and exact our own vengeance, and expect any relief.

There is only one path. Turning to the right or left leads to destruction. Turning towards the Lord is all we have. #IndependenceDay #4thofJuly

teachings.title: How reprobates draw people toward reprobation
teachings.summary: Describes abortion, pornography, grooming and divorce as means reprobates use to break people until they reject God and He rejects them. Says the purpose is to corrupt whole nations and bring them into God's wrath.
teachings.text:
Things like abortion, pornography, grooming children with pride sodomite normalization, divorce and illegitimacy are all ways that reprobates use to bring normal people, the younger the better, unto reprobation. 

Molesting kids obviously is one way to traumatize them into hating God. But they have so many other means of causing people to become so broken and angry that they reject God until He rejects them.

So many women today are ruined because they participated in an abortion and the guilt, and hardness of conscience that they develop from trying to deal with it in a culture that tells them they should be shouting their abortion, in Pride, leaves them despising God.

All of these things are wicked abominations obviously, but don't lose sight of their purpose which is to corrupt whole Nations and bring them into God's wrath, because Satan wants to make everyone as Damned as he.

teachings.title: We all sin every day
teachings.summary: Since we all sin daily, repenting from sin for righteousness is foolish; God forgives us in Jesus' name, and the Spirit and word help us overcome sin for our edification.
teachings.text:
Drinking is a sin. So is eating that extra cupcake. So are thoughts of foolishness. We all sin every day. The idea we can "Repent from sin" for righteousness is itself a foolish thought.

We wrestle with the flesh daily, we are called to crucify ourselves daily. To mortify our members and being ourselves into subjection. To strive for that prize of rewards in Heaven by doing God's work which is honoring Him, spreading the good news of Jesus Christ and taking care of and being a good judge of the poor, lame, widows and fatherless.

God knows we are in sinful flesh and He forgives us in Jesus name, and the Spirit and His word are there to help us overcome sin as Christ overcame the world, to our own edification and to be conformed to His use.

teachings.title: Ananias and Sapphira: chastened unto death
teachings.summary: Ananias and Sapphira were saved church members, and their deaths show not lost salvation but that God scourges His own children for sin, even unto death.
teachings.text:
Acts 5 picks up immediately following the last verses of 4, where the gathered believers of the assembly had just praised God in Jesus name, and been filled with the Holy Ghost to preach the scriptures boldly. They had all things in common, meaning they shared possessions as needed, forsaking materialism to edify the church and do great things for the Lord. One disciple, Barnabas had just sold property and donated the sum to the church at Jerusalem. Likely to praise and blessings. And so we meet a married couple, Ananias and Sapphira.

Ananias and Sapphira, in the context of seeing Barnabas coveted his praise and honor in the church, and having land themselves to sell, sold it for a sum, but presented to the Apostles a lesser amount, keeping a portion of the proceeds for themselves while saying they gave all of it to the church.

Peter, by the Holy Ghost calls out Ananias, who is present before them presenting the gift. Peter says he knows that it's not the full total, and asks why lie to the Holy Ghost about it considering they weren't required to sell the land at all, or to give any of the money to the church. They had every right to give a portion, as it was theirs to give.

But the lying for praise and to be favored among the congregation is the problem, and confronted, Ananias collapses dead at Peter's feet.

The brothers bury him, and a few hours later, as they are putting him in the ground along comes the wife, Sapphira.

Peter gives her a chance to be truthful, and she sticks to the story her and her husband had concocted. Peter, again in the Spirit curses her to the same fate of her husband, striking her dead. The gathered now know Ananias' death wasn't just happenstance, but that the couple has been punished by God.

Were Ananias and Sapphira saved? Didn't they just feel the presence of the Holy Ghost when the church prayed the chapter before? The Bible says in Acts 4 that the entire church was of one heart and one soul. They were of that church. I think the implication is clear they were.

But their being in Heaven when they die, justified by faith and Jesus' imputed righteousness didn't keep them from sinning, nor did it stop God from punishing them with their lives.

Many of the religion of works, who maintain that you must repent of sinning to be saved, and claim that the Gospel of Christ, salvation by faith in grace, is a "license to sin." And so, being fruit inspectors, take this story as evidence they were not believers. But what it shows is that God chastises His own for our iniquity. He takes the rod to His children when they sin. The Bible says He scourges His adopted sons and daughters. Even unto death. We saved are held to a higher standard than the unsaved, and we are punished here in this earth, sometimes more so than the unsaved, who are not God's children. This is why we should walk in the word, live for God, take up the cross and follow Jesus. Honoring our heavenly Father, which brings blessings upon blessings.

It is an amazing gift to be given a chance by God to bless others, to help people. To give freely what we have to others in the church in need. But our own pride and greed can often stop us from receiving the blessings, and instead lead us to chastisement in our sin.

teachings.title: Fear is a sin: step away from what feeds it
teachings.summary: Advises walking away from online content that leaves a believer afraid or anxious, since anything that does not edify one's service to God is a sin to engage in. Warns against becoming loyal to the source that sells the fear.
teachings.text:
I don't know who might need to hear this, but if any of the things that you're finding online, be it political, conspiracy theory stuff, White identity stuff, great reset / great replacement, w e f Black Rock and whatever else... If it leaves you more afraid, if it gives you anxiety and controls your thought patterns and behaviors, rather than entertain and amuse, inform, edify or give you a like-minded community to belong to, stop engaging in it. 

If the fake and gay gets too real and hard for you, you're better off walking away. Being simple about evil as the Bible says. If something isn't edifying you and your ability to serve God, then engaging in it is a sin. Fear is a sin.

I confess sometimes the food stuff gets me and I want to be sure I can feed my family, but a lot of the spiritual aspect of growing my own food has taught me to fear a lot less and to trust God a lot more.

Also if that fear makes you become fiercely loyal to whatever source of information is feeding that fear to make merchandise of it? To become the content you consume? Defending it like a junkie protecting his dealer?

Step away for a while. There's nothing you can really do online anyway and they're selling you fear wrapped in false hope.

teachings.title: Romans 13: living in godly subjection
teachings.summary: Believers are to submit to the authorities God ordains, obeying God rather than man only where they conflict, and trust God, for godly subjection is how God changes who rules over us.
teachings.text:
Romans 13 continues the theme of how saved Christians are to behave. It begins telling us God's view of earthly authority. Parents, bosses, civic leaders, law enforcement, all authorities under God, wicked and cruel or righteous and kind, to serve His will.

Of course we are to follow the higher law of God when earthly authority contradicts it. We are to obey God rather than man, but *if at all possible to live peaceably with all men*.

Many of us bristle at this. It requires our subjection and faith that God will protect and deliver us.
